title: Maternal RSVpreF Vaccine Effectiveness Against Respiratory Syncytial Virus in Hospitalized Infants.
abstract: IMPORTANCE: In February 2025, Australia introduced maternal vaccination with bivalent respiratory syncytial virus prefusion F protein-based vaccine (RSVpreF) in the National Immunization Program for pregnant individuals from 28 weeks' gestation as the primary, year-round strategy to prevent RSV disease in infants 6 months of age or younger. OBJECTIVE: To estimate effectiveness of RSVpreF vaccination during pregnancy against infant RSV hospitalization in Australia. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This retrospective case-control study with a test-negative design was conducted in 9 hospitals across Australia with year-round respiratory testing for acute respiratory illness (ARI) among infants born from 28 weeks' gestation and hospitalized with ARI at 6 months of age or younger, March 1, 2025, through February 28, 2026. Data were analyzed March 2026 through May 2026. EXPOSURE: Maternal RSVpreF vaccination administered from 28 weeks' gestation and 14 days or more before delivery. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Maternal RSVpreF effectiveness was evaluated against hospitalization for RSV lower respiratory tract disease (RSV-LRTD, primary objective), severe RSV-LRTD, and RSV-ARI. Logistic regression with confounder adjustment was used to calculate vaccine effectiveness (VE) as (1 - adjusted odds ratio) × 100%. RESULTS: Of 1012 infants hospitalized with ARI, 655 had LRTD, with 114 of 386 case infants (30%) and 171 of 269 control infants (64%) born to RSVpreF-vaccinated mothers (median [IQR] gestational age at vaccination, 31 weeks [29-33]). Median (IQR) maternal age at delivery was 32 years (29-35). Median (IQR) age of infants hospitalized for LRTD was 52 days (30-89); 495 of 655 (76%) were aged 3 months or younger. VE against RSV-LRTD hospitalization was 77.8% (95% CI, 66.4%-85.3%) among infants from birth through 6 months of age, 80.2% (95% CI, 71.1%-86.5%) among infants from birth through 3 months of age, 86.3% (95% CI, 79.0%-91.1%) among infants from birth through 2 months of age, and 68.2% (95% CI, 42.2%-82.5%) among infants older than 2 months through 4 months of age. Comparable VE among infants aged 6 months or younger was observed for severe RSV-LRTD (80.4%; 95% CI, 54.4%-91.6%) and RSV-ARI (80.8%; 95% CI, 70.4%-87.6%) hospitalization, with similar age-specific trends. VE was consistent across stratifications by gestational age at vaccination, vaccination to delivery time interval, and proximal administration with other vaccines during pregnancy. Descriptively, among all infants hospitalized with ARI, 161 of 499 (32%) born to RSVpreF-unvaccinated mothers had severe LRTD, while 87 of 513 (17%) born to RSVpreF-vaccinated mothers had severe LRTD. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Findings in this case-control study demonstrate high year-round effectiveness of RSVpreF vaccination against RSV-associated hospitalization in infants 6 months of age or younger in the first year following introduction in Australia, with the highest VE observed in the earliest age intervals. Future analyses with larger sample sizes will evaluate VE among additional subgroups.

title_zh: 母亲 RSVpreF 疫苗 对住院婴儿中 呼吸道合胞病毒 的有效性。
source_body_en: IMPORTANCE: In February 2025, Australia introduced maternal vaccination with bivalent respiratory syncytial virus prefusion F protein-based vaccine (RSVpreF) in the National Immunization Program for pregnant individuals from 28 weeks' gestation as the primary, year-round strategy to prevent RSV disease in infants 6 months of age or younger. OBJECTIVE: To estimate effectiveness of RSVpreF vaccination during pregnancy against infant RSV hospitalization in Australia. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This retrospective case-control study with a test-negative design was conducted in 9 hospitals across Australia with year-round respiratory testing for acute respiratory illness (ARI) among infants born from 28 weeks' gestation and hospitalized with ARI at 6 months of age or younger, March 1, 2025, through February 28, 2026. Data were analyzed March 2026 through May 2026. EXPOSURE: Maternal RSVpreF vaccination administered from 28 weeks' gestation and 14 days or more before delivery. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Maternal RSVpreF effectiveness was evaluated against hospitalization for RSV lower respiratory tract disease (RSV-LRTD, primary objective), severe RSV-LRTD, and RSV-ARI. Logistic regression with confounder adjustment was used to calculate vaccine effectiveness (VE) as (1 - adjusted odds ratio) × 100%. RESULTS: Of 1012 infants hospitalized with ARI, 655 had LRTD, with 114 of 386 case infants (30%) and 171 of 269 control infants (64%) born to RSVpreF-vaccinated mothers (median [IQR] gestational age at vaccination, 31 weeks [29-33]). Median (IQR) maternal age at delivery was 32 years (29-35). Median (IQR) age of infants hospitalized for LRTD was 52 days (30-89); 495 of 655 (76%) were aged 3 months or younger. VE against RSV-LRTD hospitalization was 77.8% (95% CI, 66.4%-85.3%) among infants from birth through 6 months of age, 80.2% (95% CI, 71.1%-86.5%) among infants from birth through 3 months of age, 86.3% (95% CI, 79.0%-91.1%) among infants from birth through 2 months of age, and 68.2% (95% CI, 42.2%-82.5%) among infants older than 2 months through 4 months of age. Comparable VE among infants aged 6 months or younger was observed for severe RSV-LRTD (80.4%; 95% CI, 54.4%-91.6%) and RSV-ARI (80.8%; 95% CI, 70.4%-87.6%) hospitalization, with similar age-specific trends. VE was consistent across stratifications by gestational age at vaccination, vaccination to delivery time interval, and proximal administration with other vaccines during pregnancy. Descriptively, among all infants hospitalized with ARI, 161 of 499 (32%) born to RSVpreF-unvaccinated mothers had severe LRTD, while 87 of 513 (17%) born to RSVpreF-vaccinated mothers had severe LRTD. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Findings in this case-control study demonstrate high year-round effectiveness of RSVpreF vaccination against RSV-associated hospitalization in infants 6 months of age or younger in the first year following introduction in Australia, with the highest VE observed in the earliest age intervals. Future analyses with larger sample sizes will evaluate VE among additional subgroups.

title: Recommendations for the Prevention of Respiratory Syncytial Virus Disease in Infants and Children: Policy Statement.
abstract: This policy statement updates recommendations of the American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) for the use of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) immunization for the prevention of lower respiratory tract infection (LRTI) caused by RSV in infants and children. The AAP recommends RSV immunization for all infants under 8 months of age born during or entering their first RSV season, unless the infant has documented protection from vaccination of their pregnant parent; and for infants and children 8 through 19 months of age who are at high risk of severe RSV disease and entering their second RSV season. A review of evidence supports expanding the high-risk criteria for administration of RSV immunization in infants and children 8 through 19 months of age entering their second RSV season. A discussion of the evidence supporting the AAP recommendations and additional details on infants and children included in the expanded recommendations are in the accompanying technical report (https://doi.org/10.1542/peds.2026-079049).

title: A Phase 2 Trial of a Respiratory Syncytial Virus and Human Metapneumovirus Combination Virus-Like Particle Vaccine IVX-A12 in Adults ≥60 Years of Age.
abstract: Abstract Background Older adults (≥60 years) are susceptible to severe outcomes from infection with respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) or human metapneumovirus (hMPV). IVX-A12 is an investigational vaccine that uses virus-like particles (VLPs) to elicit an immune response against RSV and hMPV. Methods This Phase 2 trial (NCT06481579) randomized (1:1) adults ≥60 years of age to receive a single dose of IVX-A12 (150 μg RSV/150 μg hMPV) or the licensed RSV vaccine RSVPreF3 120 μg with AS01E adjuvant. Safety and immunogenicity were evaluated through 180 days post-vaccination. Results Overall, 143 participants received IVX-A12 (n = 71) or RSVPreF3 (n = 72). Solicited adverse reactions were reported through 7 days post-vaccination (IVX-A12, 25 [35.2%]; RSVPreF3, 36 [50.0%]). Unsolicited adverse events (AEs) were collected through Day 29 (IVX-A12, 5 [7.0%]; RSVPreF3, 11 [15.3%]). Serious AEs (IVX-A12, 2 [2.8%]; RSVPreF3, 1 [1.4%]) and medically attended AEs (IVX-A12, 1 [1.4%]; RSVPreF3, 9 [12.5%]) were documented through Day 181. There were no AEs of special interest and AEs leading to study discontinuation. At Day 29, IVX-A12 and RSVPreF3 administration increased RSV A neutralizing antibody (nAb) levels with geometric mean fold rise (GMFR) of 3.4 and 6.5, and RSV B nAb levels with GMFR of 2.9 and 5.4, respectively. IVX-A12, but not RSVPreF3, also increased hMPV A (GMFR 3.0) and hMPV B (GMFR 2.9) nAb levels. Conclusions IVX-A12 and RSVPreF3 were well tolerated and elicited nAb responses against their targeted pathogens. Given the neutralizing antibody response following IVX-A12, further investigation of an RSV-hMPV VLP combination vaccine is warranted.

source_body_en: Abstract Background Older adults (≥60 years) are susceptible to severe outcomes from infection with respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) or human metapneumovirus (hMPV). IVX-A12 is an investigational vaccine that uses virus-like particles (VLPs) to elicit an immune response against RSV and hMPV. Methods This Phase 2 trial (NCT06481579) randomized (1:1) adults ≥60 years of age to receive a single dose of IVX-A12 (150 μg RSV/150 μg hMPV) or the licensed RSV vaccine RSVPreF3 120 μg with AS01E adjuvant. Safety and immunogenicity were evaluated through 180 days post-vaccination. Results Overall, 143 participants received IVX-A12 (n = 71) or RSVPreF3 (n = 72). Solicited adverse reactions were reported through 7 days post-vaccination (IVX-A12, 25 [35.2%]; RSVPreF3, 36 [50.0%]). Unsolicited adverse events (AEs) were collected through Day 29 (IVX-A12, 5 [7.0%]; RSVPreF3, 11 [15.3%]). Serious AEs (IVX-A12, 2 [2.8%]; RSVPreF3, 1 [1.4%]) and medically attended AEs (IVX-A12, 1 [1.4%]; RSVPreF3, 9 [12.5%]) were documented through Day 181. There were no AEs of special interest and AEs leading to study discontinuation. At Day 29, IVX-A12 and RSVPreF3 administration increased RSV A neutralizing antibody (nAb) levels with geometric mean fold rise (GMFR) of 3.4 and 6.5, and RSV B nAb levels with GMFR of 2.9 and 5.4, respectively. IVX-A12, but not RSVPreF3, also increased hMPV A (GMFR 3.0) and hMPV B (GMFR 2.9) nAb levels. Conclusions IVX-A12 and RSVPreF3 were well tolerated and elicited nAb responses against their targeted pathogens. Given the neutralizing antibody response following IVX-A12, further investigation of an RSV-hMPV VLP combination vaccine is warranted.

title: Enhanced respiratory syncytial virus surveillance of young children admitted to the Sydney Children's Hospitals Network, 2019-2023.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: In this study, we aimed to comprehensively describe the clinical characteristics, management and outcomes of children with respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) disease admitted to the Sydney Children's Hospitals Network (SCHN), determine the full burden of severe disease and identify population-specific risk factors for intensive care unit (ICU) admission. STUDY TYPE: Multi-centre, retrospective cohort study conducted over 5 years. METHODS: The study was conducted at two tertiary paediatric hospitals in metropolitan New South Wales, Australia, before implementation of government-funded immunisation programs against RSV in children. Participants were children aged <2 years hospitalised with laboratory-confirmed RSV from 1 January 2019 to 31 December 2023, comprising all ICU admitted, and a random sample of non-ICU admitted patients. The main outcome measures were characteristics and incidence rate of RSV hospitalisations and ICU admissions among children aged <2 years. RESULTS: Over a 5-year period, 4414 children were hospitalised with laboratory-confirmed RSV, of whom 11.3% (499/4414) were admitted to ICU. The median age was younger in the ICU cohort (n = 499) compared with the non-ICU sample (n = 1000; 3.3 vs 7.1 months, P < 0.0001). Factors associated with higher odds of ICU admission in multivariate logistic regression were decreasing month of age (OR 1.10, 95% CI 1.06-1.11), prematurity (OR 2.17, 95% CI 1.61-2.91), Indigenous identity (OR 4.10, 95% CI 2.30-7.56) and cardiac disease (OR 3.39, 95% CI 2.06-5.70). The average hospitalisation incidence rate was 1615 per 100,000 (95% CI 1565-1666), with higher rates among children aged <1 year, 2141 per 100,000 (95% CI 2061-2224) compared with those aged 1-2 years, 1088 per 100,000 (95% CI 1030-1148). CONCLUSIONS: RSV immunisation programs are expected to substantially reduce the burden of hospitalisation among Australian children in their first year of life. Children who are Indigenous, were born prematurely or have heart disease are at greatest risk of severe disease and may benefit from extended preventative programs.

elements_en.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to comprehensively describe the clinical characteristics, management and outcomes of children with respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) disease admitted to the Sydney Children's Hospitals Network, determine the full burden of severe disease and identify population-specific risk factors for intensive care unit (ICU) admission.
elements_en.study_design_and_population: The study was a multi-centre, retrospective cohort study conducted over 5 years at two tertiary paediatric hospitals in metropolitan New South Wales, Australia, involving 4414 children aged <2 years hospitalised with laboratory-confirmed RSV, of whom 11.3% were admitted to ICU.
elements_en.methods: The study was conducted at two tertiary paediatric hospitals in metropolitan New South Wales, Australia, before implementation of government-funded immunisation programs against RSV in children. The main outcome measures were characteristics and incidence rate of RSV hospitalisations and ICU admissions among children aged <2 years. Factors associated with higher odds of ICU admission were identified using multivariate logistic regression.
elements_en.main_results: Over a 5-year period, 4414 children were hospitalised with laboratory-confirmed RSV, of whom 11.3% (499/4414) were admitted to ICU. The median age was younger in the ICU cohort (n = 499) compared with the non-ICU sample (n = 1000; 3.3 vs 7.1 months, P < 0.0001).

title_zh: 2019-2023 年悉尼儿童医院网络收治的幼儿的增强型 呼吸道合胞病毒 监测。
source_body_en: OBJECTIVES: In this study, we aimed to comprehensively describe the clinical characteristics, management and outcomes of children with respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) disease admitted to the Sydney Children's Hospitals Network (SCHN), determine the full burden of severe disease and identify population-specific risk factors for intensive care unit (ICU) admission. STUDY TYPE: Multi-centre, retrospective cohort study conducted over 5 years. METHODS: The study was conducted at two tertiary paediatric hospitals in metropolitan New South Wales, Australia, before implementation of government-funded immunisation programs against RSV in children. Participants were children aged <2 years hospitalised with laboratory-confirmed RSV from 1 January 2019 to 31 December 2023, comprising all ICU admitted, and a random sample of non-ICU admitted patients. The main outcome measures were characteristics and incidence rate of RSV hospitalisations and ICU admissions among children aged <2 years. RESULTS: Over a 5-year period, 4414 children were hospitalised with laboratory-confirmed RSV, of whom 11.3% (499/4414) were admitted to ICU. The median age was younger in the ICU cohort (n = 499) compared with the non-ICU sample (n = 1000; 3.3 vs 7.1 months, P < 0.0001). Factors associated with higher odds of ICU admission in multivariate logistic regression were decreasing month of age (OR 1.10, 95% CI 1.06-1.11), prematurity (OR 2.17, 95% CI 1.61-2.91), Indigenous identity (OR 4.10, 95% CI 2.30-7.56) and cardiac disease (OR 3.39, 95% CI 2.06-5.70). The average hospitalisation incidence rate was 1615 per 100,000 (95% CI 1565-1666), with higher rates among children aged <1 year, 2141 per 100,000 (95% CI 2061-2224) compared with those aged 1-2 years, 1088 per 100,000 (95% CI 1030-1148). CONCLUSIONS: RSV immunisation programs are expected to substantially reduce the burden of hospitalisation among Australian children in their first year of life. Children who are Indigenous, were born prematurely or have heart disease are at greatest risk of severe disease and may benefit from extended preventative programs.

title: Respiratory Syncytial Virus Vaccine Effectiveness in Medicare Beneficiaries Residing in Nursing Homes.
abstract: IMPORTANCE: Vaccine effectiveness (VE) estimates are needed to determine the effectiveness of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) vaccinations during their first season of availability among populations at high risk for severe RSV. OBJECTIVE: To assess RSV VE against RSV-associated outcomes for nursing home residents. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This retrospective cohort study of Medicare fee-for-service beneficiaries used electronic medical claims data from September 10, 2023, to March 30, 2024. A cohort was created for each outcome: an RSV-associated hospitalization cohort; an RSV-associated death cohort; a severe RSV-associated outcome cohort; and an RSV-associated thromboembolic event cohort. To be eligible for inclusion in a cohort, a Medicare fee-for-service beneficiary must be aged 65 years or older, reside in a US nursing home during the study period for at least 1 day, have continuous enrollment in Medicare Parts A and B (365 days prior to the index date), and have continuous enrollment in Part D (beginning on June 21, 2023). EXPOSURE: RSV vaccination. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Outcomes were RSV-associated hospitalization, RSV-associated death, severe RSV-associated outcomes (intensive care unit or critical care unit admission, medical ventilator use, or RSV-associated death), and RSV-associated thromboembolic event. RSV diagnoses and outcome definitions were based on claims with relevant International Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, Tenth Revision codes. RSV vaccine doses were determined from Medicare Part D claims using the National Drug Code Directory. Hazard ratios (HRs) from multivariable Cox proportional hazards models compared the times to first outcomes among RSV vaccinated beneficiaries and unvaccinated beneficiaries. VE was calculated as (1-HR) × 100%. RESULTS: Of 597 430 included Medicare beneficiaries (66% female; median age, 82 [IQR, 75-88] years), RSV VE against RSV-associated hospitalizations was 73% (95% CI, 65%-79%). Among beneficiaries aged 65 to 74 years VE was 60% (95% CI, 35%-76%), 75% (95% CI, 67%-82%) among beneficiaries 75 years or older, 67% (95% CI, 55%-76%) among short-stay residents (<100 cumulative days), and 80% (95% CI, 68%-87%) among long-stay residents (≥100 cumulative days). VE against RSV-associated death was 56% (95% CI, 39%-69%), VE against severe RSV-associated outcomes was 59% (95% CI, 44%-70%), and VE against RSV-associated thromboembolic events was 66% (95% CI, 44%-79%). CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this study, in the first season of availability, RSV vaccines were associated with improved RSV-associated outcomes among US Medicare beneficiaries residing in nursing homes.

title: Under pressure: lessons learnt from rapid implementation of the respiratory syncytial virus maternal vaccine and infant nirsevimab in Sydney, Australia.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To share lessons learnt from the Sydney Local Health District (SLHD) rollout of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) prevention products, and present data on immunisation uptake for mothers and babies in two maternity hospitals. TYPE OF SERVICE: Rollout of the RSV maternal vaccine and the injectable, long-acting monoclonal antibody nirsevimab for newborn infants to protect them from RSV infection and hospitalisation. METHODS: Deidentified summary data from the electronic medical record on RSV immunisation status in two SLHD maternity hospitals were analysed descriptively as counts and proportions. The Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research was used as a lens to reflect on the rollout process. RESULTS: RSV vaccination coverage in women giving birth in two SLHD hospitals improved from 4% in the first month of rollout (February 2025) to a range of 70-74% from June to September 2025. As antenatal coverage improved, the number of live born babies requiring nirsevimab decreased. Among eligible newborns, 36% of families declined nirsevimab, with reason for refusal not recorded. Documentation of RSV immunisation status improved as the rollout progressed. LESSONS LEARNT: Engaging multidisciplinary leaders and clinicians is critical for a coordinated response and program rollout success. Leveraging existing education structures, staff meetings and using online prerecording can optimise clinician education. New programs take time to embed into routine clinical practice, and programs that involve delivering multiple immunisation products for distinct groups require clear messaging and systemic safeguards to prevent errors. Integrating immunisation into medical record workflows as standard practice can support program adoption and uptake.

analysis.methods: Deidentified summary data from electronic medical records were analysed descriptively as counts and proportions. The Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research was used to evaluate the rollout process and identify factors influencing immunisation uptake.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在分享快速实施 RSV 预防产品的经验教训,并提供两家妇产医院母亲和婴儿的免疫接种数据。这项研究需要解决将新的 RSV 预防策略纳入常规临床实践的挑战。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究涉及在悉尼地方卫生区的两家妇产医院推出 RSV 母体 疫苗 和可注射单克隆抗体 尼塞韦单抗。该研究时间跨度为 2025 年 2 月至 9 月,重点关注母亲和符合条件的新生儿的免疫接种情况。
elements_zh.methods: 来自电子病历的去识别化摘要数据被描述性地分析为计数和比例。实施研究综合框架用于评估推广过程并确定影响免疫接种的因素。
elements_zh.main_results: RSV 疫苗接种 在两家医院分娩的妇女的覆盖率从推出第一个月的 4% 增加到 2025 年 6 月至 9 月的 70-74%。随着产前覆盖率的提高,需要 尼塞韦单抗 的活产婴儿数量减少。在符合条件的新生儿中,36%的家庭拒绝了尼塞韦单抗,拒绝的原因没有记录。随着推广的进展,RSV 免疫状态的记录得到改善。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为证据,表明多学科领导者和临床医生的协调参与对于项目的成功推出至关重要。该研究强调了在针对不同群体实施多种免疫产品时,明确的信息传递和系统保障措施的重要性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果可以通过证明临床医生教育和将免疫接种纳入医疗记录工作流程等策略的有效性,为未来 RSV 预防计划的发展提供信息。他们还提供了有关提高 RSV 疫苗 和单克隆抗体的吸收率和降低拒绝率的见解。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的局限性在于它依赖于未识别身份的汇总数据,并且没有记录拒绝的原因。由于分析的描述性以及缺乏详细的统计或因果解释,证据的强度中等。

title: Respiratory syncytial virus incidence and clinical outcomes in patients with inflammatory bowel disease: a National Veterans Affairs cohort study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Data describing the incidence and clinical outcomes of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection among patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) are limited. METHODS: We conducted a nationwide retrospective cohort study using the Veterans Health Administration (VHA) database. Adults with IBD were identified using a previously validated algorithm and matched 1:2 to non-IBD controls using propensity score matching. Laboratory-confirmed RSV infections that occurred between January 1, 2021, and December 31, 2024, were identified using standardized laboratory codes and confirmed by manual chart adjudication. Primary outcomes included RSV incidence and hospitalizations. Secondary outcomes included intensive care unit (ICU) admission and patient outcomes stratified by IBD medication class. RESULTS: After propensity score matching, 52 740 IBD patients and 104 997 non-IBD controls were included. Infection with RSV occurred in 219 patients with IBD and 426 non-IBD patients. Incidence rates of RSV were similar between cohorts across all years in our study period. Hospitalization related to RSV occurred in 18.26% of IBD-RSV patients compared with 13.15% of non-IBD patients (P = .08). ICU admission was rare in both groups (<1%). Among patients with IBD, RSV-related hospitalization did not differ significantly by medication class, when comparing biologic therapy (8.93%) with 5-aminosalicylic acid monotherapy (17.58%) (P = .15). CONCLUSIONS: In this nationwide cohort, patients with IBD, with predominantly lower exposure to advanced therapies, did not have higher rates of RSV infection or worse clinical outcomes compared with matched non-IBD controls. RSV outcomes were similar across IBD medication classes. These findings support current vaccination recommendations and provide reassurance regarding RSV risk among patients with IBD.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to investigate the incidence and clinical outcomes of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection among patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). A nationwide retrospective cohort study was conducted using the Veterans Health Administration (VHA) database, where adults with IBD were matched 1:2 to non-IBD controls. The study identified RSV infections between 2021 and 2024 and assessed outcomes such as hospitalization and ICU admission. Results showed similar RSV incidence rates between IBD and non-IBD patients, with no significant difference in hospitalization rates. The findings suggest that IBD patients do not have higher RSV infection rates or worse clinical outcomes compared to non-IBD controls, and outcomes were consistent across different IBD medication classes. These results support existing vaccination recommendations and offer reassurance about RSV risk in IBD patients. The study's evidence is strong, but specific limitations were not detailed.

title: Circulating Biomarkers Associated with Severe Respiratory Syncytial Virus Infection in Infants Under 2 Years: A Systematic Review
abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of acute lower respiratory tract infection in infants, but circulating biomarkers for severity stratification remain insufficiently validated. This systematic review evaluated circulating biomarkers associated with acute RSV disease severity in children aged≤ 24 months. PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus were searched for English-language reports published between 1 January 2016 and 1 March 2026, with the last searches performed on 1 March 2026. Study-level risk of bias was assessed using the Newcastle–Ottawa Scale or the Joanna Briggs Institute checklist, according to study design. Findings were synthesized descriptively using study-level effect estimates and reported severity-discrimination measures. Twenty-four studies contributed 174 extractable comparisons. Biomarker associations varied across populations, age strata, sampling times, and severity definitions, and reproducibility across independent cohorts was limited. In one cohort, fibrinogen and the fibrinogen-to-albumin ratio (FAR) showed large differences between severity groups; FAR had a reported AUC of 0.875. These findings do not establish comparative superiority or external validity. Important limitations include heterogeneous clinical comparisons, limited confounder adjustment, and predominantly single-cohort evidence. Current evidence does not support using FAR, the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), or other circulating biomarkers alone to predict subsequent clinical deterioration. Whether these markers add useful information to clinical assessment requires prospective validation. Registration: PROSPERO, CRD420261471336.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review investigates circulating biomarkers associated with severe respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection in infants under 2 years. The review included 24 studies contributing 174 extractable comparisons, with evidence sourced from PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus between 2016 and 2026. The findings show variability in biomarker associations across populations, age groups, sampling times, and severity definitions, with limited reproducibility across independent cohorts. The fibrinogen-to-albumin ratio (FAR) demonstrated a reported AUC of 0.875 in one cohort, but the evidence does not establish its comparative superiority or external validity. The study-level risk of bias was assessed using the Newcastle–Ottawa Scale or the Joanna Briggs Institute checklist, and the review was registered with PROSPERO.

title: Phosphate-modified PROTECs as potent antivirals against respiratory syncytial virus by targeting the fusion protein.
abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) remains a major cause of severe respiratory infections, highlighting the need for antiviral strategies with novel mechanisms. Here, we extended our protein-radical-oxidation targeting enediyne chimera (PROTEC) strategy to the RSV fusion (F) protein. BMS-433771 was employed as the protein-targeting group and conjugated to a maleimide-based acyclic enediyne bearing phosphate hydrophilicity-adjusting groups, which simplified synthesis compared with our previous sulfate-containing PROTECs. Three analogues with different linker lengths ( n = 3, 5, and 7) were synthesized and evaluated. All compounds showed low cytotoxicity (CC 50 > 100 μM) and potent anti-RSV activity. PROTEC-R7 ( n = 7) exhibited the highest potency, with an IC 50 of 110.3 nM and a selectivity index > 906. In contrast, the non-targeted control EDY-R showed substantially weaker activity (IC 50 = 16.3 μM). These results demonstrate the importance of targeted delivery and linker engineering and support PROTEC as a promising strategy for targeting viral surface proteins.

source_records.title: Phosphate-modified PROTECs as potent antivirals against respiratory syncytial virus by targeting the fusion protein.

Here, we extended our protein-radical-oxidation targeting enediyne chimera (PROTEC) strategy to the RSV fusion (F) protein. BMS-433771 was employed as the protein-targeting group and conjugated to a maleimide-based acyclic enediyne bearing phosphate hydrophilicity-adjusting groups, which simplified synthesis compared with our previous sulfate-containing PROTECs. Three analogues with different linker lengths ( n = 3, 5, and 7) were synthesized and evaluated. All compounds showed low cytotoxicity (CC 50 > 100 μM) and potent anti-RSV activity. PROTEC-R7 ( n = 7) exhibited the highest potency, with an IC 50 of 110.3 nM and a selectivity index > 906. In contrast, the non-targeted control EDY-R showed substantially weaker activity (IC 50 = 16.3 μM). These results demonstrate the importance of targeted delivery and linker engineering and support PROTEC as a promising strategy for targeting viral surface proteins.

abstract_zh: 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 仍然是严重呼吸道感染的主要原因,这凸显了对具有新颖机制的 抗病毒药物 策略的需求。在这里,我们将蛋白质自由基氧化靶向烯二炔嵌合体 (PROTEC) 策略扩展到 RSV 融合 (F) 蛋白。BMS-433771 被用作蛋白质靶向基团,并与带有磷酸盐亲水性调节基团的基于马来酰亚胺的无环烯二炔缀合,与我们之前的含硫酸盐的 PROTEC 相比,这简化了合成。合成并评估了具有不同接头长度的三种类似物(n = 3、5 和 7)。所有化合物均表现出低细胞毒性 (CC 50 > 100 μM) 和有效的抗 RSV 活性。PROTEC-R7 ( n = 7) 表现出最高的效力,IC 50 为 110.3 nM,选择性指数 > 906。相比之下,非靶向对照 EDY-R 显示出明显较弱的活性 (IC 50 = 16.3 μM)。这些结果证明了靶向递送和接头工程的重要性,并支持 PROTEC 作为靶向病毒表面蛋白的有前途的策略。

title: In Vitro Evaluation of Repurposed Antivirals and Their Combinations Against Respiratory Syncytial Virus and Human Parainfluenza Virus Type 2: Evidence of Ribavirin-Oseltamivir Synergy.
abstract: Treating respiratory viral infections remains challenging, necessitating exploration of novel therapeutic approaches. Alternative strategies, such as drug repurposing or combinations, are essential for treating them. This study evaluated the in vitro activities of the antivirals ribavirin, favipiravir, and oseltamivir, and the mucolytic drugs N-acetylcysteine (NAC) and erdosteine, alone or in combination, against Human Parainfluenza Virus (HPIV) and Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV). HPIV-2 and RSV were cultured in VERO and HEp-2 cell lines, respectively. Antiviral efficacy was assessed by calculating IC 50 values using MTT and plaque reduction assays. For combination studies, synergy scores were analyzed using the SynergyFinder program. We investigated potential interactions underlying the synergistic activities using an in silico approach, that combined virtual screening and molecular docking. The IC 50 values of ribavirin, favipiravir, and oseltamivir against HPIV-2 and RSV ranged from 4.46 to 14.1 μg/mL, and the results from both methods were highly similar. All three antivirals' cytotoxicity was well above their C-max, and SIs were 12.43-36.69 for HPIV-2 and 15.88-38.12 for RSV. The ribavirin-oseltamivir combination synergy scores of 13.35 for HPIV-2 and 17.98 for RSV indicate clear synergism, while other combinations were additive. Docking analysis identified potential molecular interactions that may contribute to the antiviral activity of the ribavirin-oseltamivir combination against RSV and HPIV-2. Ribavirin, favipiravir, and oseltamivir showed good activity against HPIV-2 and RSV, and the ribavirin-oseltamivir combination exhibited strong synergistic interactions, suggesting promising therapeutic potential.

title: Recommendations for the Prevention of Respiratory Syncytial Virus Disease in Infants and Children: Technical Report.
abstract: This technical report accompanies the American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) policy statement (https://doi.org/10.1542/peds.2026-079047) and recommendations for respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) immunization during the 2026-2027 RSV season. The rationale is presented for recommending immunization of all infants younger than 8 months born during or entering their first RSV season, unless the infant has documented protection from vaccination of the pregnant parent; and infants and children 8 through 19 months of age who are at high risk of severe RSV disease and entering their second RSV season. The report synthesizes current evidence on RSV epidemiology, disease burden, immunization effectiveness, safety, and cost-effectiveness in pediatric populations; including evidence supporting expansion of high-risk groups for second season administration. Additionally, the report provides an overview of available RSV immunization products, formulations, and coadministration with other immunizations.

The rationale is presented for recommending immunization of all infants younger than 8 months born during or entering their first RSV season, unless the infant has documented protection from vaccination of the pregnant parent; and infants and children 8 through 19 months of age who are at high risk of severe RSV disease and entering their second RSV season. The report synthesizes current evidence on RSV epidemiology, disease burden, immunization effectiveness, safety, and cost-effectiveness in pediatric populations; including evidence supporting expansion of high-risk groups for second season administration. Additionally, the report provides an overview of available RSV immunization products, formulations, and coadministration with other immunizations.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本报告解决了针对婴儿和儿童 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 疾病更新预防策略的需求,重点关注 2026-2027 RSV 季节期间免疫建议的基本原理。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究是一份技术报告,综合了儿科人群(包括患有严重 RSV 疾病的高风险人群)的 RSV 流行病学、疾病负担、免疫有效性、安全性和成本效益的当前证据。
elements_zh.methods: 该报告回顾并综合了 RSV 免疫的现有证据,包括有效性、安全性和成本效益的数据,并概述了可用的 RSV 免疫产品和配方。
elements_zh.main_results: 该报告概述了建议对在第一个 RSV 季节期间或进入其第一个 RSV 季节期间出生的所有 8 个月以下婴儿进行免疫接种的理由,除非婴儿已证明怀孕父母对 疫苗接种 具有保护作用,以及患有严重 RSV 疾病高风险并进入第二个 RSV 季节的 8 至 19 个月大的婴儿和儿童。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为支持扩大第二季 RSV 免疫接种的高危人群,这代表了解决弱势儿科人群疾病负担的一种新方法。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为 RSV 预防的公共卫生策略提供信息,特别是在识别高危人群和优化婴儿和儿童的免疫计划方面。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该报告基于现有证据的综合,这些证据在普遍性和最新数据方面可能存在局限性,但证据被认为是强有力的,并且对所提供的建议得到了充分支持。

title: Dynamic structural adaptation of a conserved interaction hotspot in the respiratory syncytial virus fusion glycoprotein F.
abstract: Protein interaction sites must maintain structural integrity while accommodating conformational fluctuations and sequence perturbations. Molecular determinants that distinguish locally adaptable residues from structurally constrained positions within conserved interfaces remain incompletely understood. Here, we investigate this problem using the prefusion respiratory syncytial virus fusion glycoprotein F as a model system, focusing on a conserved interaction hotspot proximal to the MEDI8897-binding interface. An integrated computational framework combining evolutionary conservation, structure-based energetic analysis, residue interaction networks, and molecular dynamics simulations was used to characterize mutation-dependent structural responses. Analysis of 1848 RSV F sequences revealed strong conservation of the CPINKC hotspot comprising C69, P205, I206, N208, K209, and C212. Despite conservation, saturation mutagenesis and structural analysis revealed pronounced heterogeneity in calculated energetic response to substitution. P205R and N208R produced highly unfavorable calculated energetic effects, whereas I206R exhibited an approximately neutral energetic response. Residue interaction network analysis identified I206 as topologically central residue with the highest betweenness and closeness centrality within the hotspot. Aggregate MD sampling comprised three independent 500-ns simulations for each of seven systems, yielding 10.5 μs of total simulation time. All systems retained the overall prefusion architecture over the simulated timescale but exhibited distinct local and interprotomer responses. N208R produced the strongest local perturbation, including increased hotspot flexibility and reduced interprotomer contact occupancy. In contrast, P205R maintained restrained local dynamics despite its energetic penalty, whereas I206R preserved a broadly wild-type-like dynamic profile. These findings indicate that energetic cost, residue interaction topology, and conformational dynamics provide complementary information for characterizing mutation-induced structural adaptation.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to understand how protein interaction sites maintain structural integrity while allowing conformational changes and sequence variations. The research addressed a gap in knowledge about the molecular factors that differentiate adaptable residues from structurally constrained ones in conserved viral interfaces.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study focused on the respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) fusion glycoprotein F, specifically examining a conserved interaction hotspot near the MEDI8897-binding interface. It analyzed 1848 RSV F sequences to identify patterns of conservation and mutation effects.
analysis.methods: The researchers employed an integrated computational framework that combined evolutionary conservation analysis, structure-based energetic calculations, residue interaction network assessments, and molecular dynamics simulations to evaluate mutation-dependent structural responses.
analysis.main_results: Analysis of RSV F sequences showed strong conservation of the CPINKC hotspot, including residues C69, P205, I206, N208, K209, and C212. Saturation mutagenesis and structural analysis revealed significant variation in the energetic response to substitutions, with P205R and N208R showing highly unfavorable effects and I206R having a neutral response.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that energetic cost, residue interaction topology, and conformational dynamics provide distinct yet complementary insights into how mutations affect structural adaptation in viral proteins.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the structural adaptation of a conserved interaction hotspot in the respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) fusion glycoprotein F. The research aimed to understand how residues within this hotspot maintain structural integrity despite conformational changes and sequence variations. Using an integrated computational framework, the study analyzed 1848 RSV F sequences and found strong conservation of the CPINKC hotspot. Saturation mutagenesis and structural analysis revealed that substitutions at specific residues, such as P205R and N208R, had highly unfavorable energetic effects, while I206R showed a neutral response. These insights could inform the development of antiviral strategies targeting RSV. However, the study's reliance on computational models and sequence data limits the confidence in its conclusions, suggesting a moderate evidence strength.

title_zh: 呼吸道合胞病毒 融合糖蛋白 F 中保守相互作用热点的动态结构适应。
source_body_en: Protein interaction sites must maintain structural integrity while accommodating conformational fluctuations and sequence perturbations. Molecular determinants that distinguish locally adaptable residues from structurally constrained positions within conserved interfaces remain incompletely understood. Here, we investigate this problem using the prefusion respiratory syncytial virus fusion glycoprotein F as a model system, focusing on a conserved interaction hotspot proximal to the MEDI8897-binding interface. An integrated computational framework combining evolutionary conservation, structure-based energetic analysis, residue interaction networks, and molecular dynamics simulations was used to characterize mutation-dependent structural responses. Analysis of 1848 RSV F sequences revealed strong conservation of the CPINKC hotspot comprising C69, P205, I206, N208, K209, and C212. Despite conservation, saturation mutagenesis and structural analysis revealed pronounced heterogeneity in calculated energetic response to substitution. P205R and N208R produced highly unfavorable calculated energetic effects, whereas I206R exhibited an approximately neutral energetic response. Residue interaction network analysis identified I206 as topologically central residue with the highest betweenness and closeness centrality within the hotspot. Aggregate MD sampling comprised three independent 500-ns simulations for each of seven systems, yielding 10.5 μs of total simulation time. All systems retained the overall prefusion architecture over the simulated timescale but exhibited distinct local and interprotomer responses. N208R produced the strongest local perturbation, including increased hotspot flexibility and reduced interprotomer contact occupancy. In contrast, P205R maintained restrained local dynamics despite its energetic penalty, whereas I206R preserved a broadly wild-type-like dynamic profile. These findings indicate that energetic cost, residue interaction topology, and conformational dynamics provide complementary information for characterizing mutation-induced structural adaptation.
abstract_zh: 蛋白质相互作用位点必须保持结构完整性,同时适应构象波动和序列扰动。将局部适应性残基与保守界面内结构受限位置区分开来的分子决定因素仍不完全清楚。在这里,我们使用预融合 呼吸道合胞病毒 融合糖蛋白 F 作为模型系统来研究这个问题,重点关注靠近 MEDI8897 结合界面的保守相互作用热点。使用结合了进化守恒、基于结构的能量分析、残基相互作用网络和分子动力学模拟的集成计算框架来表征依赖于 突变 的结构响应。对 1848 个 RSV F 序列的分析揭示了 CPINKC 热点(包括 C69、P205、I206、N208、K209 和 C212)的高度保守性。尽管保守,饱和诱变和结构分析揭示了计算的替代能量响应中明显的异质性。P205R 和 N208R 产生了非常不利的计算能量效应,而 I206R 表现出近似中性的能量响应。残基相互作用网络分析将 I206 确定为拓扑中心残基,在热点内具有最高的中介性和接近中心性。聚合 MD 采样包括七个系统中每个系统的三个独立的 500 ns 模拟,产生 10.5 μs 的总模拟时间。所有系统在模拟时间尺度上都保留了整体预融合架构,但表现出不同的局部和原体间响应。N208R 产生最强的局部扰动,包括增加热点灵活性和减少原体间接触占用。相比之下,P205R 尽管存在能量损失,但仍保持有限的局部动态,而 I206R 则保留了大致与野生型相似的动态特征。这些发现表明能量成本、残基相互作用拓扑和构象动力学为表征 突变 诱导的结构适应提供了补充信息。

title: Respiratory Pathogens Detected among Pediatric Hospitalizations for Pneumonia: A Multicenter Study from Saitama, Japan.
abstract: Routine in-hospital testing may not detect the full range of respiratory pathogens in children hospitalized with pneumonia. We conducted a prefecture-wide multicenter retrospective cohort study at four hospitals in Saitama, Japan, from July 2023 to March 2024 to describe detected respiratory pathogens and assess the additional findings obtained by multiplex polymerase chain reaction (PCR) beyond routine in-hospital testing. Among 1,170 pediatric hospitalizations for acute respiratory infections (ARIs), 457 (39.1%) were complicated by pneumonia. Human metapneumovirus (hMPV; n=124, 27.1%) and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV; n=85, 18.6%) were the most frequently detected pathogens. Multiplex PCR was performed in 199 hospitalizations. Among 123 hospitalizations in which at least one in-hospital respiratory pathogen test was performed and all results were negative, multiplex PCR detected at least one pathogen in 85 (69.1%). In an exploratory unadjusted comparison excluding 16 group A Streptococcus-positive hospitalizations, antibiotic initiation was associated with older age, higher C-reactive protein levels, and absence of a positive in-hospital test. Among 210 antibiotic-treated hospitalizations without a positive in-hospital test, 110 underwent multiplex PCR and a viral pathogen was detected in 74/110 (67.3%). Multiplex PCR frequently identified pathogens after negative routine testing and broadened the detectable pathogen spectrum beyond targeted in-hospital tests.

elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,多重 PCR 显着增强了常规检测之外的病原体检测,突显了其提高小儿肺炎病例诊断准确性的潜力。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,多重 PCR 可以提供更全面的病原体检测,这可能为改进小儿肺炎的诊断策略和有针对性的 治疗 方法提供信息。

title: The MSC–RSV/HMPV interface: impacts on pulmonary homeostasis, remodeling, and risk of non-atopic asthma and COPD
abstract: Respiratory tract infections continue to represent a major cause of pediatric morbidity and mortality. Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) and Human Metapneumovirus (HMPV) are highlighted as key etiologic agents of bronchiolitis and pneumonia, particularly in children under two years old. Recurrent infections during the second year of life may be associated with significant histopathological damage and might also be a risk factor for developing chronic pulmonary diseases, such as non-atopic asthma. In adults, these viruses similarly elevate clinical burden on the elderly and individuals with Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD), causing the exacerbation of respiratory signals and symptoms and, consequently, promoting a chronic inflammatory response that modifies the lung tissue and disease progression. Tissue repair and the homeostasis recovery might be associated with the participation of Mesenchymal Stem Cells (MSCs), both lung resident and migratory MSCs, these cells are characterized by their plasticity and immunomodulatory capacity, which are relevant to restoring tissue homeostasis after injury. However, RSV and HMPV may also infect MSCs, raising the question that infected MSCs could lose immunomodulatory efficacy and plasticity, thereby affecting tissue renewal. This review aims to provide an overview of the effect of respiratory viral infections, their implications in the lung tissue damage and the possible participation of MSCs in the recovery of lung homeostasis by tissue repair and immune response modulation.
journal: Frontiers in Cellular and Infection Microbiology

title: Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV)–An Urgent Priority in Respiratory Disease Prevention
abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of lower respiratory tract disease in infants, young children, older adults, and individuals with cardiopulmonary comorbidities or immunocompromised states. Recent advances enable layered prevention through maternal vaccination for infant protection, long-acting monoclonal antibodies for newborns and select toddlers, and vaccines for older adults. However, inequities in surveillance, seasonality-driven timing, and challenges in affordability and delivery—particularly in low- and middle-income countries— impede equitable uptake. This editorial underscores priority populations, synthesizes current evidence and policy directions, and outlines actionable levers in financing, procurement, and integrated maternal–child health delivery to accelerate access, making RSV prevention an urgent and achievable global health priority.

title: Diagnostic performance of antigen-based rapid test kits for six respiratory viruses in children: comparison with a multiplex PCR panel and correlation with viral load.
abstract: ABSTRACT Rapid antigen tests are widely used for point-of-care diagnosis of respiratory tract infection (RTI) in children, but how the sensitivity is influenced by viral load has not been comprehensively characterized across multiple pediatric respiratory viruses. In this prospective, paired-specimen study conducted at the pediatric center, two simultaneous nasopharyngeal swabs were obtained from children with RTI. One swab was tested using antigen-based rapid test kits (ImunoAce series, Tauns Laboratories, Inc.) for SARS-CoV-2, influenza A, influenza B, adenovirus, human metapneumovirus (hMPV), and respiratory syncytial virus; the other was tested using the FilmArray Respiratory Panel (bioMérieux). Specimens positive by either method underwent confirmatory quantitative real-time PCR to determine viral load. Sensitivity was stratified by viral load. A total of 1,584 paired specimens from 1,232 children (median age: 3.0 years [IQR: 1.0–6.0]; 53.7% male) were analyzed. Sensitivity of the antigen tests ranged from 20.6% (adenovirus) to 79.7% (hMPV), while specificity exceeded 99% for all six targets and overall agreement ranged from 90.7% to 99.0%. For every virus, antigen test positivity increased steeply with viral load, approaching 90–100% at viral loads ≥10 6 –10 7 copies/100 μL and falling below 50% at loads ≤10 4 –10 5 copies/100 μL. Antigen-based rapid tests for common pediatric respiratory viruses showed high specificity and viral-load-dependent sensitivity, detecting nearly all specimens with high viral load regardless of the target virus. These findings support a role for antigen testing in identifying children with the highest viral burden—who are most likely to have acute infection. IMPORTANCE The sensitivity of rapid antigen tests for respiratory viruses relative to PCR-based testing has been incompletely characterized. This study evaluated antigen tests for six common pediatric respiratory viruses—SARS-CoV-2, influenza A, influenza B, adenovirus, human metapneumovirus, and respiratory syncytial virus—against a multiplex PCR reference standard across 1,584 clinical specimens and linked test performance directly to quantitative viral load. We show that antigen test sensitivity is strongly and consistently dependent on viral load, approaching 90–100% at high viral loads with very high specificity across all six targets. These findings clarify the clinical role of rapid antigen testing: it reliably identifies children with the highest viral burden, who are most likely to have acute, symptomatic infection warranting immediate clinical action.

analysis.study_design_and_population: This prospective, paired-specimen study was conducted at a pediatric center, where two simultaneous nasopharyngeal swabs were collected from 1,232 children (median age: 3.0 years [IQR: 1.0–6.0]; 53.7% male) with respiratory tract infections.
analysis.methods: One swab was tested using antigen-based rapid test kits (ImunoAce series, Tauns Laboratories, Inc.) for RSV and other respiratory viruses, while the other was tested using the FilmArray Respiratory Panel (bioMérieux). Specimens positive by either method underwent confirmatory quantitative real-time PCR to determine viral load.
analysis.main_results: Sensitivity of the antigen tests for RSV ranged from 20.6% (adenovirus) to 79.7% (hMPV), while specificity exceeded 99% for all six targets. For RSV, antigen test positivity increased steeply with viral load, approaching 90–100% at viral loads ≥10^6–10^7 copies/100 μL and falling below 50% at loads ≤10^4–10^5 copies/100 μL.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings demonstrate that antigen test sensitivity for RSV is strongly and consistently dependent on viral load, with very high specificity across all targets. This highlights the utility of antigen testing in identifying children with the highest viral burden.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results clarify the clinical role of rapid antigen testing for RSV, showing its reliability in detecting high viral load cases, which are most likely to represent acute, symptomatic infection requiring immediate clinical action.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to paired specimens from a single pediatric center, which may affect generalizability. However, the evidence is strong, with high specificity and clear viral-load-dependent sensitivity observed for RSV.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the diagnostic performance of antigen-based rapid test kits for respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) in children, comparing them with a multiplex PCR panel. The research aimed to understand how RSV sensitivity is influenced by viral load, as this relationship has not been fully characterized. The study was conducted at a pediatric center, where two simultaneous nasopharyngeal swabs were collected from 1,232 children. Antigen tests showed high specificity for RSV and other respiratory viruses, with sensitivity strongly dependent on viral load. For RSV, antigen test positivity increased steeply with viral load, approaching 90–100% at loads ≥10^6–10^7 copies/100 μL. These findings support the use of antigen testing to identify children with the highest viral burden, who are most likely to have acute infection. The study's results are robust, but its single-center design may limit generalizability.

title_zh: 基于抗原的快速检测试剂盒对儿童六种呼吸道病毒的诊断性能:与多重 PCR 检测组的比较以及与病毒载量的相关性。
source_body_en: ABSTRACT Rapid antigen tests are widely used for point-of-care diagnosis of respiratory tract infection (RTI) in children, but how the sensitivity is influenced by viral load has not been comprehensively characterized across multiple pediatric respiratory viruses. In this prospective, paired-specimen study conducted at the pediatric center, two simultaneous nasopharyngeal swabs were obtained from children with RTI. One swab was tested using antigen-based rapid test kits (ImunoAce series, Tauns Laboratories, Inc.) for SARS-CoV-2, influenza A, influenza B, adenovirus, human metapneumovirus (hMPV), and respiratory syncytial virus; the other was tested using the FilmArray Respiratory Panel (bioMérieux). Specimens positive by either method underwent confirmatory quantitative real-time PCR to determine viral load. Sensitivity was stratified by viral load. A total of 1,584 paired specimens from 1,232 children (median age: 3.0 years [IQR: 1.0–6.0]; 53.7% male) were analyzed. Sensitivity of the antigen tests ranged from 20.6% (adenovirus) to 79.7% (hMPV), while specificity exceeded 99% for all six targets and overall agreement ranged from 90.7% to 99.0%. For every virus, antigen test positivity increased steeply with viral load, approaching 90–100% at viral loads ≥10 6 –10 7 copies/100 μL and falling below 50% at loads ≤10 4 –10 5 copies/100 μL. Antigen-based rapid tests for common pediatric respiratory viruses showed high specificity and viral-load-dependent sensitivity, detecting nearly all specimens with high viral load regardless of the target virus. These findings support a role for antigen testing in identifying children with the highest viral burden—who are most likely to have acute infection. IMPORTANCE The sensitivity of rapid antigen tests for respiratory viruses relative to PCR-based testing has been incompletely characterized. This study evaluated antigen tests for six common pediatric respiratory viruses—SARS-CoV-2, influenza A, influenza B, adenovirus, human metapneumovirus, and respiratory syncytial virus—against a multiplex PCR reference standard across 1,584 clinical specimens and linked test performance directly to quantitative viral load. We show that antigen test sensitivity is strongly and consistently dependent on viral load, approaching 90–100% at high viral loads with very high specificity across all six targets. These findings clarify the clinical role of rapid antigen testing: it reliably identifies children with the highest viral burden, who are most likely to have acute, symptomatic infection warranting immediate clinical action.
abstract_zh: 摘要 快速抗原检测广泛用于儿童呼吸道感染 (RTI) 的护理点 诊断,但病毒载量对敏感性的影响尚未全面表征多种儿科呼吸道病毒的特征。在儿科中心进行的这项前瞻性配对样本研究中,从患有 RTI 的儿童身上同时采集了两份鼻咽拭子。使用基于抗原的快速检测试剂盒(ImunoAce 系列,Tauns Laboratories,Inc.)对一根拭子进行了 SARS-CoV-2、甲型流感、乙型流感、腺病毒、人类偏肺病毒 (hMPV) 和 呼吸道合胞病毒 的检测;另一个使用 FilmArray 呼吸面板 (bioMérieux) 进行测试。任一方法呈阳性的样本均需进行验证性定量实时 PCR 以确定病毒载量。敏感性按病毒载量分层。总共分析了来自 1,232 名儿童(中位年龄:3.0 岁 [IQR:1.0–6.0];53.7% 男性)的 1,584 个配对样本。抗原测试的敏感性范围为 20.6%(腺病毒)至 79.7%(hMPV),而所有六个目标的特异性均超过 99%,总体一致性范围为 90.7% 至 99.0%。对于每种病毒,抗原检测阳性率随病毒载量急剧增加,病毒载量≥10 6 –10 7 拷贝/100 μL 时接近 90-100%,病毒载量≤10 4 –10 5 拷贝/100 μL 时下降到 50% 以下。针对常见儿科呼吸道病毒的基于抗原的快速检测显示出高特异性和病毒载量依赖性敏感性,可检测几乎所有具有高病毒载量的样本,无论目标病毒如何。这些发现支持抗原检测在识别病毒负荷最高的儿童(最有可能患有急性感染)方面的作用。重要性 呼吸道病毒快速抗原检测相对于基于 PCR 的检测的敏感性尚未完全确定。这项研究根据 1,584 份临床样本的多重 PCR 参考标准评估了六种常见儿科呼吸道病毒(SARS-CoV-2、甲型流感、乙型流感、腺病毒、人类偏肺病毒和 呼吸道合胞病毒)的抗原测试,并将测试性能直接与定量病毒载量联系起来。我们表明,抗原测试敏感性强烈且始终依赖于病毒载量,在高病毒载量时接近 90-100%,并且对所有六个目标具有非常高的特异性。这些发现阐明了快速抗原检测的临床作用:它可靠地识别出病毒负荷最高的儿童,这些儿童最有可能患有急性症状感染,需要立即采取临床行动。

title: Respiratory Syncytial Virus Infection in Children During the COVID-19 Pandemic: Findings from a Tertiary-Care Pediatric Cohort
abstract: Objective: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a major cause of lower respiratory tract infection in children. This study aimed to describe the clinical and laboratory characteristics of RSV-positive children older than 28 days in a tertiary-care cohort, explore characteristics associated with hospitalization in group comparisons, and identify factors independently associated with pediatric intensive care unit (PICU) admission among hospitalized children.Materials and Methods: This retrospective single-center study screened RSV testing records between August 2020 and August 2022 and included children older than 28 days with laboratory-confirmed RSV infection identified between February 2021 and August 2022. Demographic, clinical, laboratory, treatment, hospitalization, PICU admission, respiratory support, and outcome data were recorded. Comparisons were performed according to hospitalization status, clinical diagnosis, and PICU admission. A prespecified parsimonious multivariable logistic regression model evaluated factors associated with PICU admission among hospitalized children.Results: Of the 3523 children with available RSV test results during the study period, 561 RSV-positive children aged >28 days were included. Median age was 4 months (IQR, 2-14), and 317 patients (56.5%) were male. Bronchiolitis was the most common diagnosis (63.5%), followed by pneumonia (28.5%) and upper respiratory tract infection (8.0%). Hospitalization was required in 478 patients (85.2%), and 35 (6.2%) required PICU admission. Pneumonia was associated with higher rates of hypoxia, noninvasive ventilatory support, PICU admission, longer hospitalization, and delayed clinical improvement. Documented viral coinfection was detected in 30 patients (5.3%); no association was detected between documented viral coinfections and hospitalizations or PICU admission in this dataset. In hospitalized patients, pneumonia (OR, 2.59; 95% CI, 1.07-6.24; p=0.034) and hypoxia (OR, 32.08; 95% CI, 13.09-78.66; p<0.001) were independently associated with PICU admission.Conclusion: RSV infection predominantly affected infants and most commonly presented as bronchiolitis. Pneumonia and hypoxia were independently associated with PICU admission in this tertiary-care cohort.

Demographic, clinical, laboratory, treatment, hospitalization, PICU admission, respiratory support, and outcome data were recorded. Comparisons were performed according to hospitalization status, clinical diagnosis, and PICU admission. A prespecified parsimonious multivariable logistic regression model evaluated factors associated with PICU admission among hospitalized children.Results: Of the 3523 children with available RSV test results during the study period, 561 RSV-positive children aged >28 days were included. Median age was 4 months (IQR, 2-14), and 317 patients (56.5%) were male. Bronchiolitis was the most common diagnosis (63.5%), followed by pneumonia (28.5%) and upper respiratory tract infection (8.0%). Hospitalization was required in 478 patients (85.2%), and 35 (6.2%) required PICU admission. Pneumonia was associated with higher rates of hypoxia, noninvasive ventilatory support, PICU admission, longer hospitalization, and delayed clinical improvement. Documented viral coinfection was detected in 30 patients (5.3%); no association was detected between documented viral coinfections and hospitalizations or PICU admission in this dataset. In hospitalized patients, pneumonia (OR, 2.59; 95% CI, 1.07-6.24; p=0.034) and hypoxia (OR, 32.08; 95% CI, 13.09-78.66; p<0.001) were independently associated with PICU admission.Conclusion: RSV infection predominantly affected infants and most commonly presented as bronchiolitis. Pneumonia and hypoxia were independently associated with PICU admission in this tertiary-care cohort.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 是儿童下呼吸道感染的主要原因。本研究旨在描述三级护理 队列研究 中 28 天以上 RSV 阳性儿童的临床和实验室特征,探索与住院治疗相关的组间比较特征,并确定与住院儿童入院儿科重症监护病房 (PICU) 独立相关的因素。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项回顾性单中心研究筛选了 2020 年 8 月至 2022 年 8 月期间的 RSV 检测记录,纳入了 2021 年 2 月至 2022 年 8 月期间经实验室确诊的 RSV 感染的 28 天以上儿童。在研究期间有可用 RSV 检测结果的 3523 名儿童中,包括 561 名年龄 >28 天的 RSV 阳性儿童。
elements_zh.methods: 记录人口统计、临床、实验室、治疗、住院、PICU 入院、呼吸支持和结果数据。根据住院状况、临床 诊断 和 PICU 入院情况进行比较。预先指定的简约多变量逻辑回归模型评估了住院儿童入住 PICU 的相关因素。
elements_zh.main_results: 478 名患者(85.2%)需要住院治疗,其中 35 名患者(6.2%)需要入住 PICU。肺炎与缺氧、无创通气支持、PICU 入住、住院时间较长和临床改善延迟的发生率较高有关。在 30 名患者 (5.3%) 中检测到有记录的病毒双重感染;在此数据集中,未发现记录的病毒合并感染与住院或 PICU 入住之间存在关联。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 在该三级护理 队列研究 中,肺炎和缺氧与 PICU 入住独立相关。该研究重点介绍了 RSV 感染儿童的临床特征和入住 PICU 的危险因素,为了解 RSV 疾病的严重程度提供了见解。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为 监测 和儿科人群 RSV 风险评估策略提供信息,特别是在识别可能需要重症监护的高风险患者方面。他们还支持制定有针对性的干预措施来管理严重 RSV 感染。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其回顾性设计和单中心设置而受到限制,这可能会影响普遍性。该证据是中等的,因为它基于三级护理 队列研究,并且不包括前瞻性数据或外部验证。

title: Bardoxolone methyl exerts an inhibitory effect on respiratory syncytial virus infection by downregulating IL-6 via the IKKβ/NF-κB signaling pathway
abstract: ABSTRACT Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) causes severe lower respiratory tract infections in infants, older adults, and immunocompromised individuals, but therapeutic options for active infection remain limited. Interleukin-6 (IL-6) contributes to RSV replication and RSV-induced inflammation, and the IKKβ/NF-κB pathway is a major regulator of IL-6 expression. Bardoxolone methyl (BXM) was identified by network medicine as a potential anti-RSV compound, with molecular docking suggesting interactions with the IKKβ/NF-κB pathway. We investigated whether BXM inhibits RSV infection through modulation of the IKKβ/NF-κB/IL-6 axis in RSV-infected BEAS-2B cells and BALB/c mice. RSV infection increased IL-6 expression and activated IKKβ/NF-κB signaling, whereas IL-6 knockdown reduced viral replication and inflammatory mediator expression. BXM significantly suppressed RSV replication, as shown by RT-qPCR, TCID50, plaque reduction assays, and Western blotting, and decreased IL-6 expression in vitro . Mechanistically, BXM attenuated RSV-induced phosphorylation of IKKβ and NF-κB. The IKKβ inhibitor TPCA-1 produced similar inhibitory effects, whereas recombinant human IL-6 add-back partially restored inflammatory mediator expression in BXM-treated RSV-infected cells. In mice, BXM reduced lung viral titers, RSV-F expression, IL-6 expression, IKKβ/NF-κB activation, and RSV-induced lung injury. These findings suggest that BXM suppresses RSV replication and inflammation, at least in part, by modulating the IKKβ/NF-κB/IL-6 axis, supporting its potential as a therapeutic candidate for RSV infection. IMPORTANCE Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a major cause of respiratory illness, especially in infants, older adults, and people with weakened immune systems. Although preventive strategies are available for some high-risk groups, treatment options for active RSV infection remain limited. This study identifies bardoxolone methyl (BXM) as a potential anti-RSV compound and shows that it can reduce both viral replication and virus-induced inflammation in cell and mouse models. Importantly, our findings suggest that BXM acts, at least in part, by reducing IL-6-related inflammatory signaling, which is closely associated with RSV disease severity. These results provide experimental evidence supporting BXM as a promising candidate for further development against RSV infection and offer insight into a potential host-targeted therapeutic strategy.

abstract_zh: 摘要 呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)会导致婴儿、老年人和免疫功能低下人群的严重下呼吸道感染,但针对活动性感染的治疗选择仍然有限。白细胞介素-6(IL-6)促进RSV复制和RSV引发的炎症,而IKKβ/NF-κB通路是调控IL-6表达的主要途径。甲基巴多昔芬(BXM)通过网络医学被鉴定为一种潜在的抗RSV化合物,分子对接研究表明其与IKKβ/NF-κB通路存在相互作用。我们研究了BXM是否通过调节RSV感染的BEAS-2B细胞和BALB/c小鼠中的IKKβ/NF-κB/IL-6轴来抑制RSV感染。RSV感染会增加IL-6表达并激活IKKβ/NF-κB信号通路,而IL-6敲低则会减少病毒复制和炎症介质的表达。BXM在体外显著抑制了RSV复制,如RT-qPCR、TCID50、斑块减少实验和Western blotting所示,并降低了IL-6的表达。从机制上看,BXM减弱了RSV诱导的IKKβ和NF-κB的磷酸化。IKKβ抑制剂TPCA-1产生了类似的抑制效果,而重组人IL-6添加则部分恢复了BXM处理的RSV感染细胞中炎症介质的表达。在小鼠中,BXM降低了肺部病毒滴度、RSV-F表达、IL-6表达、IKKβ/NF-κB激活以及RSV诱导的肺损伤。这些发现表明,BXM通过调节IKKβ/NF-κB/IL-6轴抑制RSV复制和炎症,支持其作为RSV感染治疗候选药物的潜力。重要性 呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)是导致呼吸道疾病的主要原因之一,尤其是在婴儿、老年人和免疫功能低下人群中。尽管某些高危群体已有预防策略,但针对活动性RSV感染的治疗选择仍然有限。本研究确定了甲基巴多昔芬(BXM)作为潜在的抗RSV化合物,并表明其在细胞和小鼠模型中可以减少病毒复制和病毒诱导的炎症。重要的是,我们的发现表明,BXM至少部分通过减少与IL-6相关的炎症信号发挥作用,而这些信号与RSV疾病的严重程度密切相关。这些结果为BXM作为对抗RSV感染的潜在候选药物提供了实验依据,并为针对宿主的治疗策略提供了见解。

title: Coinfections With Respiratory Syncytial Virus in a Cohort of Adults With High‐Risk Conditions, 2015–2020: A Retrospective Observational Study
abstract: Summary Coinfections may influence the clinical outcome of respiratory illness. Data are limited regarding RSV coinfections in adults with high‐risk conditions. Residual respiratory specimens from community‐dwelling adults (≥ 18 years) with ≥ 1 high‐risk condition were retested using a multiplex panel for multiple viral pathogens. We compared demographic and clinical characteristics between those with RSV coinfection versus RSV single infection. RSV coinfections comprised 5.9% of all RSV infections among adults with ≥ 1 high‐risk condition. No statistically significant differences were observed between those with RSV coinfections and single infections according to presence of specific high‐risk conditions or clinical disease presentation.

Using a multiplex panel, residual respiratory specimens were retested to identify multiple viral pathogens. The findings suggest that RSV coinfections are common but do not significantly alter clinical outcomes. This study provides descriptive insights into RSV coinfections, which may help improve surveillance and diagnostic approaches. The evidence is moderate due to the retrospective design and potential selection bias.

elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,RSV 合并感染在患有高危疾病的成年人中相对常见,但与单一感染相比,似乎不会显着影响临床结果。本研究对该人群中 RSV 合并感染进行了描述性分析。

title: Đặc điểm tiến hóa phân tử của vi rút hợp bào hô hấp trên bệnh nhân nhi viêm đường hô hấp cấp tính nặng (SARI) tại miền Bắc Việt Nam, 2017-2020 Molecular Evolution of Human Respiratory Syncytial Virus in Pediatric Patients with Severe Acute Respiratory Infection (SARI) in Northern Viet Nam, 2017-2020
abstract: Vi rút hợp bào hô hấp ở người (Respiratory Syncytial Virus – RSV) là một trong những nguyên nhân hàng đầu gây nhiễm trùng đường hô hấp cấp tính ở trẻ nhỏ. Các nghiên cứu về đặc điểm sinh học phân tử và tiến hoá của RSV vẫn còn hạn chế tại những quốc gia có thu nhập thấp và trung bình. Nghiên cứu này được thực hiện nhằm xác định đặc điểm tiến hóa phân tử của RSV trên bệnh nhân nhi nhiễm trùng hô hấp cấp tính nặng tại miền Bắc Việt Nam giai đoạn 2017–2020. Từ các mẫu viêm đường hô hấp cấp tính nặng được xác định dương tính với RSV tại Bệnh viện Nhi Trung ương và Bệnh viện đa khoa tỉnh Quảng Ninh trong 4 năm (2017-2020) tiến hành lựa chọn 56 mẫu dương tính RSV-A và 50 mẫu dương tính RSV-B để giải trình tự toàn bộ gen G bằng kỹ thuật giải trình tự gen thế hệ mới. Các mẫu này được lựa chọn theo giá trị Ct, phân nhóm, tuổi, giới tính, thời gian lấy mẫu và địa điểm. Từ kết quả giải trình tự, các phân tích phát sinh chủng loại và tiến hóa được thực hiện để phân tích đặc điểm tiến hoá phân tử. Kết quả cho thấy các chủng RSV-A đều thuộc clade A.D, kiểu gen ON1 (53 chủng) và non-ON1 (3 chủng), 50 chủng RSV-B thuộc clade B.D.4, kiểu gen BA9. Tất cả các chủng RSV-A của Việt Nam trong nghiên cứ này đều không có đoạn lặp 72 nucleotide ở vùng siêu biến đổi thứ hai trên gen G. Tốc độ tiến hóa phân tử ước tính của gen G RSV-A và RSV-B lần lượt là 1,32 × 10-3 và 8,29 × 10-4 thay thế/ vị trí/năm. Các vị trí N-glycosyl hóa và các vị trí axit amin chịu áp lực chọn lọc ở cả hai phân nhóm vi rút cũng được xác định. Nghiên cứu đã đưa ra được tốc độ tiến hóa và các đặc điểm tiến hoá phân tử của cả RSV-A và RSV-B tại miền Bắc Việt Nam giai đoạn 2017-2020, góp phần cung cấp các dữ liệu cho việc thực hiện giám sát sự lưu hành của vi rút này trong thời gian tới tại Việt Nam.

title: Classifying and Differentiating Clinical Coding of Respiratory Syncytial Virus, Influenza, and COVID-19 in OpenSAFELY Between 2016 and 2024
abstract: Electronic health records (EHRs) are a rich source of data which can be used to analyse health outcomes using computable phenotypes. With the approval of NHS England we used the OpenSAFELY secure analytics platform to design and assess phenotypes to classify three key respiratory viruses - respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), influenza, and COVID-19 - in English coded health data between September 2016 and August 2024. We compared narrow and broad phenotypes to one another and to publicly available surveillance data. Cases from both phenotypes showed similar seasonal patterns to surveillance data. Broad phenotypes led to increased risk of misclassification than narrow phenotypes for mild cases. For severe cases the risk of misclassification was higher in infants than for older adults, irrespective of the phenotype used. The phenotypes presented here offer a potential route to classify respiratory viruses from coded health records in the absence of testing information.

source_body_en: Electronic health records (EHRs) are a rich source of data which can be used to analyse health outcomes using computable phenotypes. Broad phenotypes led to increased risk of misclassification than narrow phenotypes for mild cases. For severe cases the risk of misclassification was higher in infants than for older adults, irrespective of the phenotype used. The phenotypes presented here offer a potential route to classify respiratory viruses from coded health records in the absence of testing information.

title: RSV Bivalent Prefusion F Protein Vaccine in Pregnancy and Protection Against RSV-Associated Illness in Infants: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: IMPORTANCE: The respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) bivalent prefusion F protein vaccine (RSVpreF) administered during pregnancy has demonstrated efficacy in protecting infants against early-life RSV disease in the pivotal clinical trial. OBJECTIVE: To conduct a systematic review and meta-analysis to synthesize real-world evidence on the effectiveness of RSVpreF in preventing RSV-associated lower respiratory tract infection (LRTI) in infants. DATA SOURCES: PubMed, Scopus, and Europe PMC were searched from January 1, 2020, through January 30, 2026. STUDY SELECTION: A total of 1144 studies were initially identified. Eligible were nonrandomized studies reporting the effectiveness of RSVpreF vaccine in pregnancy in the prevention of RSV-associated LRTI in infants. DATA EXTRACTION AND SYNTHESIS: All studies were screened independently by 2 reviewers. Data were extracted on RSV-associated outcomes among infants born to women who received RSVpreF vaccination during pregnancy and infants born to unvaccinated women. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was RSV-associated LRTI hospitalization. Odds ratios (ORs) were pooled using random-effects meta-analysis with the Hartung-Knapp adjustment and Sidik-Jonkman estimator. Vaccine effectiveness against RSV-associated LRTI hospitalization was calculated as (1 - OR) × 100% and assessed in infants from birth to age 3 months and from birth to 6 months, separately. The limited available data precluded meta-analysis of effectiveness against the secondary outcomes of RSV-associated emergency department visits, intensive care unit admissions, and death. RESULTS: A total of 7 studies were included, comprising 7112 infants, of whom 2684 were born to vaccinated mothers. The studies collected data from January 2024 through April 2025 from Argentina, the UK, and the US. Pooled vaccine effectiveness against RSV-associated LRTI hospitalization was 82% (95% CI, 81%-82%; 3 studies, 4397 participants; I2 = 0%) in infants from birth to 3 months and 78% (95% CI, 70%-84%; 6 studies, 3008 participants; I2 = 18.7%) in infants from birth to 6 months, when mothers were vaccinated 14 days or more before delivery. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: The results of this systematic review and meta-analysis suggest that postimplementation data support the effectiveness of RSVpreF in pregnancy for the prevention of RSV-associated LRTI hospitalization during the first 6 months of life. The results support the introduction of RSVpreF into routine antenatal immunization programs.

Objective To conduct a systematic review and meta-analysis to synthesize real-world evidence on the effectiveness of RSVpreF in preventing RSV-associated lower respiratory tract infection (LRTI) in infants. Data Sources PubMed, Scopus, and Europe PMC were searched from January 1, 2020, through January 30, 2026. Study Selection A total of 1144 studies were initially identified. Eligible were nonrandomized studies reporting the effectiveness of RSVpreF vaccine in pregnancy in the prevention of RSV-associated LRTI in infants. Data Extraction and Synthesis All studies were screened independently by 2 reviewers. Data were extracted on RSV-associated outcomes among infants born to women who received RSVpreF vaccination during pregnancy and infants born to unvaccinated women. Main Outcomes and Measures The primary outcome was RSV-associated LRTI hospitalization. Odds ratios (ORs) were pooled using random-effects meta-analysis with the Hartung-Knapp adjustment and Sidik-Jonkman estimator. Vaccine effectiveness against RSV-associated LRTI hospitalization was calculated as (1 − OR) × 100% and assessed in infants from birth to age 3 months and from birth to 6 months, separately. The limited available data precluded meta-analysis of effectiveness against the secondary outcomes of RSV-associated emergency department visits, intensive care unit admissions, and death. Results A total of 7 studies were included, comprising 7112 infants, of whom 2684 were born to vaccinated mothers. The studies collected data from January 2024 through April 2025 from Argentina, the UK, and the US. Pooled vaccine effectiveness against RSV-associated LRTI hospitalization was 82% (95% CI, 81%-82%; 3 studies, 4397 participants; I 2 = 0%) in infants from birth to 3 months and 78% (95% CI, 70%-84%; 6 studies, 3008 participants; I 2 = 18.7%) in infants from birth to 6 months, when mothers were vaccinated 14 days or more before delivery. Conclusions and Relevance The results of this systematic review and meta-analysis suggest that postimplementation data support the effectiveness of RSVpreF in pregnancy for the prevention of RSV-associated LRTI hospitalization during the first 6 months of life. The results support the introduction of RSVpreF into routine antenatal immunization programs.

title_original: RSV Bivalent Prefusion F Protein Vaccine in Pregnancy and Protection Against RSV-Associated Illness in Infants: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on the effectiveness of the RSV bivalent prefusion F protein vaccine (RSVpreF) administered during pregnancy in preventing RSV-associated lower respiratory tract infection (LRTI) in infants. The central question is whether RSVpreF provides protection against RSV-related illness in infants, with a specific emphasis on hospitalization due to LRTI.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review conducted a systematic search of PubMed, Scopus, and Europe PMC from January 1, 2020, through January 30, 2026. A total of 1144 studies were initially identified, and all were screened independently by 2 reviewers. The meta-analysis used random-effects models with Hartung-Knapp adjustment and Sidik-Jonkman estimator to pool odds ratios (ORs). Vaccine effectiveness was calculated as (1 - OR) × 100% for the primary outcome of RSV-associated LRTI hospitalization.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The pooled vaccine effectiveness against RSV-associated LRTI hospitalization was 82% (95% CI, 81%-82%) in infants from birth to 3 months and 78% (95% CI, 70%-84%) in infants from birth to 6 months, when mothers were vaccinated 14 days or more before delivery. These results support the effectiveness of RSVpreF in pregnancy for preventing RSV-associated LRTI hospitalization during the first 6 months of life.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The limited available data precluded meta-analysis of effectiveness against secondary outcomes such as RSV-associated emergency department visits, intensive care unit admissions, and death. This indicates a gap in the evidence for these specific outcomes, which are not fully addressed in the current review.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The results support the introduction of RSVpreF into routine antenatal immunization programs. Further research is needed to evaluate its effectiveness against secondary outcomes and to expand the geographic and demographic scope of the studies.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluates the effectiveness of the RSV bivalent prefusion F protein vaccine (RSVpreF) administered during pregnancy in preventing RSV-associated lower respiratory tract infection (LRTI) in infants. The review synthesized real-world evidence from 7 studies involving 7112 infants, with 2684 born to vaccinated mothers. Pooled vaccine effectiveness against RSV-associated LRTI hospitalization was 82% (95% CI, 81%-82%) in infants from birth to 3 months and 78% (95% CI, 70%-84%) in infants from birth to 6 months, when mothers were vaccinated 14 days or more before delivery. These findings support the use of RSVpreF in antenatal immunization programs. However, the limited data precluded meta-analysis of secondary outcomes such as emergency department visits, ICU admissions, and mortality. The review highlights the need for further research to address these gaps and to confirm the vaccine's broader impact on RSV-related illnesses in infants.
