elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述的重点是妊娠期间施用 RSV 二价预融合 F 蛋白 疫苗 (RSVpreF) 在预防婴儿 RSV 相关下呼吸道感染 (LRTI) 方面的有效性。核心问题是 RSVpreF 是否能针对婴儿 RSV 相关疾病提供保护,特别是针对 LRTI 导致的住院治疗。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述对2020年1月1日至2026年1月30日期间的PubMed、Scopus和Europe PMC进行了系统检索。初步确定了总共1144项研究,所有研究均由2名评审员独立筛选。荟萃分析使用带有 Hartung-Knapp 调整和 Sidik-Jonkman 估计器的随机效应模型来合并比值比 (OR)。RSV 相关 LRTI 住院主要结局的 疫苗 有效性计算为 (1 - OR) × 100%。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 合并的疫苗对呼吸道合胞病毒相关下呼吸道感染住院的预防效果在出生至3个月的婴儿中为82%(95%置信区间,81%-82%),在出生至6个月的婴儿中为78%(95%置信区间,70%-84%),当母亲在分娩前14天或更早接种疫苗时。这些结果支持在妊娠期间接种RSVpreF可有效预防出生后6个月内因呼吸道合胞病毒相关下呼吸道感染导致的住院。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 有限的可用数据无法对次要结果(如 RSV 相关急诊就诊、重症监护病房入院和死亡)的有效性进行荟萃分析。这表明这些具体结果的证据存在差距,当前的审查尚未完全解决这些问题。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 结果支持将 RSVpreF 引入常规产前免疫计划。需要进一步的研究来评估其对次要结果的有效性,并扩大研究的地理和人口范围。

title: [Update on vaccination for older adults].
abstract: Older adults are highly susceptible to infections, some of which are vaccine preventable. Therefore, the Standing Committee on Vaccination (STIKO) regularly updates its vaccination recommendations for older adults as well. Since the 2025/26 season, the adjuvanted influenza vaccine is recommended for people aged 60 and older, in addition to the high-dose influenza vaccine. In addition, a one-time vaccination against respiratory syncytial virus in autumn has been added as a routine vaccination for 75-year-olds and as an indication-based vaccination for those aged 60 and older with severe underlying medical conditions. Little attention has been paid so far to the now well documented additional benefits of vaccinations against shingles, pneumococcal disease, influenza, and RSV - that is, effects that go beyond the primary therapeutic benefit and make a significant contribution to healthy aging. These include a reduction in myocardial and cerebrovascular events, as well as a protective effect against neurodegenerative processes. In particular it has been demonstrated that the influenza vaccine is as effective as statins in the secondary prevention of myocardial infarction. These findings could lead to an increased acceptance of vaccination and, consequently, to an increase in vaccination rates, which remain insufficient. To continue improving the benefits of vaccination in the future, vaccines need to be further developed to achieve greater efficacy, which could also help increase acceptance of vaccination. Several new developments are currently in the pipeline, particularly for the pneumococcal vaccine. source_records.title: Update Impfungen im Alter
source_records.abstract: Für die Influenzaimpfung werden nun alternativ 2 Vakzine empfohlen, zum einen der bereits zuvor schon empfohlene Hochdosisgrippeimpfstoff, zum anderen neu ein adjuvantierter Grippeimpfstoff. Neu hinzugekommen ist die einmalige Impfung im Herbst gegen RSV als Standardimpfung für die ab 75-Jährigen sowie als Indikationsimpfung für ab 60-Jährige mit schweren Vorerkrankungen. Es entfällt die Empfehlung zum Erlangen der Basisimmunität für die erwachsene Bevölkerung. Die Altersgrenze für die jährliche Standard-COVID-19-Auffrischimpfung wird von 60 auf 75 Jahre angehoben. Für einen bestmöglichen Impfschutz sollte die jährliche COVID-19-Auffrischimpfung zu Beginn der COVID-19-Saison im Spätsommer/Frühherbst erfolgen. Mittlerweile ist gut belegt, dass die Vakzinierung gegen Herpes zoster, Pneumokokken, Influenza und RSV signifikante „Off-Target-Effekte“, also Wirkungen, die über den primär therapeutischen Effekt hinausgehen, besitzt. Zu diesen gehören die Reduktion myokardialer und zerebrovaskulärer Ereignisse sowie eine protektive Wirkung gegen neurodegenerative Prozesse. Insbesondere für die Influenzaimpfung ist belegt, dass sie in der Sekundärprävention des Myokardinfarktes eine vergleichbare Wirksamkeit hat wie Statine. In Europa ist seit 03/2025 ein 21-valenter Pneumokokkenkonjugatimpfstoff für Erwachsene zugelassen. Er berücksichtigt im Vergleich zu den bisher eingesetzten Vakzinen vor allem die Serotypen, die schwere Infektionen im höheren Alter verursachen. Er ist in den USA neben PCV15 und PCV20 für die Impfung von Erwachsenen empfohlen. Aufgrund der späteren Zulassung in Europa liegt von der STIKO noch keine Stellungnahme vor. Weitere Vakzinkandidaten sind in der Entwicklung unter Einsatz neuer Technologien, um die Limitationen der üblichen Konjugatvakzinen zu umgehen.

title: RSV Disease Among Hospitalized Children: Second vs. First Year of Life Multicenter Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of pediatric hospitalization, yet data on children hospitalized with RSV in their second year of life are limited. OBJECTIVE: To compare clinical characteristics and management practices of children hospitalized with RSV during their second versus first year of life. METHODS: This retrospective multicenter study included children aged 0-23 months hospitalized with RSV infection across 11 medical centers between 2017 and 2021. We compared demographics, outcomes (length of stay [LOS] > 3 days, and pediatric intensive care unit [PICU] admission), and systemic corticosteroid and antibiotic use between the second and first years of life, adjusting for prematurity, comorbidities, and the COVID-19 pandemic. RESULTS: Among 6260 children hospitalized with laboratory-confirmed RSV infection, 1321 (21%) were hospitalized during their second year of life. Compared with first-year admissions, second-year patients had higher rates of prematurity (18.0% vs. 13.4%) and comorbidities (6.3% vs. 2.6%) (both p < 0.001). They more frequently received corticosteroids (53.5% vs. 23.2%) and antibiotics (63.4% vs. 45.9%) (both p < 0.001) and had lower PICU admission rates (4.6% vs. 7.0%; p < 0 0.001) and similar rates of prolonged LOS (35.0% vs. In adjusted analyses, second-year hospitalization was associated with increased corticosteroid use (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 4.28; 95% CI, 3.67-4.99) and antibiotic use (aOR, 2.09; 95% CI, 1.80-2.43), and lower odds of PICU admission (aOR, 0.56; 95% CI, 0.40-0.79). CONCLUSIONS: RSV hospitalization in the second year of life carries a significant burden, with higher antibiotic and corticosteroid use despite lower PICU rates and similar LOS. These findings highlight the need for better characterization of this age group to optimize future immunoprophylaxis strategies.

title: RSV Disease Burden in Adults in Emerging Market Countries, a Systematic Review and Modelling Analysis
abstract: Abstract Background Most previous studies on adult respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) burden focus on high-income settings (HIC). With the recent approval of RSV vaccines for adults, extending epidemiological understanding to emerging market countries (EMC) is critical for informing prevention strategies. We aimed to characterize the burden of RSV among adults ≥18 years in EMC. Methods We conducted a systematic review (PROSEPRO: CRD420251137828) to identify studies reporting estimates of RSV burden from any care setting in adults>18 years in EMC. For each individual study included, we followed a two-step statistical approach to adjust for RSV case under-ascertainment related to the use of clinical specimen and diagnostic test. Random-effects meta-analysis was conducted to estimate RSV incidence rate, proportion positive, hospitalisation, and mortality burden. Findings We included 70 studies of which the majority were from China (30/70) and PCR was the predominant diagnostic method (59/70). Adjusted RSV disease incidence rate (approximately 2.5 times higher than unadjusted) ranged from 2,544 (95% CI 1,352-4,787) per 100,000 in adults aged 18-49 years to 2,392 (1,618-3,534) in adults ≥65 years after accounting for clinical sampling and diagnostic testing. Adjusted hospitalisation rates increased with age, from 20 (8-51) per 100,000 in 18-49 years to 74 (3-2,027) in adults ≥65 years, representing an approximate 2.5-fold increase after adjustment. The adjusted RSV proportion positive was relatively stable, ranging from 1.8% (0.4-8.5) to 9.7% (6.3-14.6), regardless of settings or clinical case definitions. The unadjusted in-hospital case fatality ratio (hCFR) was 6.0% (2.9-11.9) in adults ≥65 years vs 3.1 (2.0-5.0) in those 18-49 years. Among hospitalized RSV-positive adults, 95.8% (84.2-99.0) had at least one comorbidity, most commonly hypertension, diabetes, and COPD. Conclusion The estimated incidence and proportion positive of RSV disease in EMC is substantially lower than HIC. Narrow case definitions requiring fever, less sensitive testing such as direct fluorescent antibody testing, reduced healthcare access, and incomplete surveillance may be contributing to these lower estimates. In-hospital CFR are comparable to or higher than in HIC.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review and modelling analysis aimed to characterize the burden of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) among adults ≥18 years in emerging market countries (EMC). The review included 70 studies, predominantly from China, using PCR as the main diagnostic method. Adjusted RSV incidence rates were found to be 2,544 (95% CI 1,352-4,787) per 100,000 in adults aged 18-49 years and 2,392 (1,618-3,534) in adults ≥65 years. Adjusted hospitalisation rates increased with age, from 20 (8-51) per 100,000 in 18-49 years to 74 (3-2,027) in adults ≥65 years. The unadjusted in-hospital case fatality ratio (hCFR) was 6.0% (2.9-11.9) in adults ≥65 years versus 3.1% (2.0-5.0) in those aged 18-49 years. The study concluded that RSV disease burden in EMC is substantially lower than in high-income settings (HIC). The authors suggested that narrow case definitions, less sensitive testing, reduced healthcare access, and incomplete surveillance may contribute to these lower estimates. The findings highlight the importance of extending epidemiological understanding to EMC to inform RSV prevention strategies, especially with the recent approval of RSV vaccines for adults.

title: Risk Factors for COVID-19 and Influenza Nonvaccination during the 2025-2026 Respiratory Season among a Cross-Sectional Sample of Older US Adults.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Adults aged ≥ 65 years are high-risk for severe coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) and influenza outcomes, but reasons for nonvaccination remain understudied. METHODS: We estimated age- and gender-adjusted prevalence ratios (aPRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CI) among adults aged ≥ 65 years in the Communities, Households, and SARS-CoV-2 Epidemiology (CHASING) COVID Cohort living in the USA for two comparisons: (1) receiving neither the COVID-19 nor the influenza vaccine versus both vaccines, and (2) receiving only influenza versus both vaccines between September 2025 and March 2026. Reasons for nonreceipt are summarized. RESULTS: Among 649 participants, 42.1% did not receive the COVID-19 vaccine and 21.4% did not receive the influenza vaccine in the 2025-2026 respiratory season. Those with the lowest trust in their doctor (aPR: 5.56, 95% CI: 4.25-7.27), most difficulty asking their provider vaccine questions (aPR: 2.59, 95% CI: 1.70-3.94), lowest perceived community benefit of influenza (aPR: 12.25, 95% CI: 8.58-17.49) and COVID-19 (aPR: 12.12, 95% CI: 8.52-17.26) vaccination, and receipt of no other (respiratory syncytial virus [RSV], shingles, or pneumococcal) vaccine during the 2025-2026 respiratory season (aPR: 3.48, 95% CI: 2.13-5.66) had a higher likelihood of receiving neither versus both vaccines. These associations were attenuated when comparing receiving only influenza versus both the influenza and COVID-19 vaccines. Side effects and safety concerns were the most common reasons for not receiving the COVID-19 vaccine, though lack of a health care provider recommendation was a commonly reported reason among those who received ≥ 1 other vaccine (influenza, RSV, shingles, or pneumococcal) during the time period. For nonreceipt of the influenza vaccine, concerns about side effects and low perceived need were common reasons cited. CONCLUSIONS: Focused efforts are particularly needed to increase COVID-19 vaccination among this high-risk group. Health care providers should leverage clinical encounters to build trust, address safety and efficacy concerns, and ensure that older adults receive the full range of recommended vaccines, but reducing access barriers and building and maintaining trust in vaccines among older adults will likely also require a multipronged approach.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates risk factors for nonvaccination against COVID-19 and influenza among older US adults during the 2025-2026 respiratory season. It highlights that low trust in healthcare providers, difficulty in asking vaccine-related questions, and low perceived community benefit of vaccination are associated with not receiving both vaccines. The study found that 42.1% of participants did not receive the COVID-19 vaccine, while 21.4% did not receive the influenza vaccine. These findings suggest that targeted interventions to improve trust and address concerns are essential for increasing vaccination rates in this high-risk population. The study is based on a cross-sectional analysis of the CHASING cohort, and the results emphasize the need for a multifaceted approach to enhance vaccine uptake. However, the evidence does not explicitly report limitations or the strength of the findings.

source_body_en: INTRODUCTION: Adults aged ≥ 65 years are high-risk for severe coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) and influenza outcomes, but reasons for nonvaccination remain understudied. METHODS: We estimated age- and gender-adjusted prevalence ratios (aPRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CI) among adults aged ≥ 65 years in the Communities, Households, and SARS-CoV-2 Epidemiology (CHASING) COVID Cohort living in the USA for two comparisons: (1) receiving neither the COVID-19 nor the influenza vaccine versus both vaccines, and (2) receiving only influenza versus both vaccines between September 2025 and March 2026. Reasons for nonreceipt are summarized. RESULTS: Among 649 participants, 42.1% did not receive the COVID-19 vaccine and 21.4% did not receive the influenza vaccine in the 2025-2026 respiratory season. Those with the lowest trust in their doctor (aPR: 5.56, 95% CI: 4.25-7.27), most difficulty asking their provider vaccine questions (aPR: 2.59, 95% CI: 1.70-3.94), lowest perceived community benefit of influenza (aPR: 12.25, 95% CI: 8.58-17.49) and COVID-19 (aPR: 12.12, 95% CI: 8.52-17.26) vaccination, and receipt of no other (respiratory syncytial virus [RSV], shingles, or pneumococcal) vaccine during the 2025-2026 respiratory season (aPR: 3.48, 95% CI: 2.13-5.66) had a higher likelihood of receiving neither versus both vaccines. These associations were attenuated when comparing receiving only influenza versus both the influenza and COVID-19 vaccines. Side effects and safety concerns were the most common reasons for not receiving the COVID-19 vaccine, though lack of a health care provider recommendation was a commonly reported reason among those who received ≥ 1 other vaccine (influenza, RSV, shingles, or pneumococcal) during the time period. For nonreceipt of the influenza vaccine, concerns about side effects and low perceived need were common reasons cited. CONCLUSIONS: Focused efforts are particularly needed to increase COVID-19 vaccination among this high-risk group. Health care providers should leverage clinical encounters to build trust, address safety and efficacy concerns, and ensure that older adults receive the full range of recommended vaccines, but reducing access barriers and building and maintaining trust in vaccines among older adults will likely also require a multipronged approach.

title: Shifting viral aetiology, codetection and age-specific mortality in severe acute respiratory infection in Brazil, 2022-2025: a nationwide surveillance study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Respiratory viral aetiology and codetection among severe acute respiratory infection (SARI) notifications have evolved post-COVID-19. We examined temporal patterns, age heterogeneity, and severe outcome associations in Brazil. METHODS: We analysed nationwide SIVEP-Gripe SARI records (2022-2025; extracted July 2026) with RT-PCR viral detection. Seven mutually exclusive categories were evaluated using robust Poisson regression to estimate adjusted risk ratios (aRRs) for SARI-attributed mortality and a severe composite outcome (ICU admission, invasive ventilation, or death). RESULTS: Among 447,107 virus-positive records, 7.2% involved codetections and 25.4% included RSV. Isolated SARS-CoV-2 declined from 72.4% (2022) to 6.8% (2025), while codetections rose from 3.0% to 11.2%. Compared to isolated RSV, mortality was higher for codetection without RSV (aRR 1.80, 95% CI: 1.67-1.94), isolated SARS-CoV-2 (1.62, 1.54-1.70), and codetection with RSV (1.40, 1.27-1.55). Associations varied by age ($p < .001$). Among RSV-positive cases, codetection conferred increased mortality risk (aRR 1.46, 1.32-1.61). Excluding isolated SARS-CoV-2 attenuated the 2025-versus-2022 codetection prevalence ratio from 1.85 to 1.10. CONCLUSIONS: Viral detections shifted towards greater heterogeneity, strongly driven by changing surveillance composition. Varying testing indications and panels limit causal inference. Integrated, age-sensitive surveillance with standardized diagnostic reporting is essential; surveillance proportions do not reflect population incidence.

title_zh: 2022-2025 年巴西严重急性呼吸道感染的病毒病原学、联合检测和年龄特异性 死亡率 的变化:一项全国性 监测 研究。
source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Respiratory viral aetiology and codetection among severe acute respiratory infection (SARI) notifications have evolved post-COVID-19. We examined temporal patterns, age heterogeneity, and severe outcome associations in Brazil. METHODS: We analysed nationwide SIVEP-Gripe SARI records (2022-2025; extracted July 2026) with RT-PCR viral detection. Seven mutually exclusive categories were evaluated using robust Poisson regression to estimate adjusted risk ratios (aRRs) for SARI-attributed mortality and a severe composite outcome (ICU admission, invasive ventilation, or death). RESULTS: Among 447,107 virus-positive records, 7.2% involved codetections and 25.4% included RSV. Isolated SARS-CoV-2 declined from 72.4% (2022) to 6.8% (2025), while codetections rose from 3.0% to 11.2%. Compared to isolated RSV, mortality was higher for codetection without RSV (aRR 1.80, 95% CI: 1.67-1.94), isolated SARS-CoV-2 (1.62, 1.54-1.70), and codetection with RSV (1.40, 1.27-1.55). Associations varied by age ($p < .001$). Among RSV-positive cases, codetection conferred increased mortality risk (aRR 1.46, 1.32-1.61). Excluding isolated SARS-CoV-2 attenuated the 2025-versus-2022 codetection prevalence ratio from 1.85 to 1.10. CONCLUSIONS: Viral detections shifted towards greater heterogeneity, strongly driven by changing surveillance composition. Varying testing indications and panels limit causal inference. Integrated, age-sensitive surveillance with standardized diagnostic reporting is essential; surveillance proportions do not reflect population incidence.

title: Non-invasive quantification of lower airway antigen-specific antibodies using exhaled breath particles - an observational proof-of-concept study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Advancements in mucosal vaccine development highlight the urgent need for practical methods to assess immune responses in both upper and lower airways. Although nasal sampling is increasingly standardised, a non-invasive technique for directly assessing antigen-specific antibodies in the distal airways has been lacking. METHODS: We used Particles in Exhaled Air (PExA), a non-invasive method capturing aerosolised respiratory tract lining fluid (RTLF) from the distal airways, to quantify antigen-specific IgA and IgG. Antibodies were measured in paired serum, nasal secretions, and PExA samples from 28 healthcare workers during spring 2025, including 18 with RT-qPCR-confirmed SARS-CoV-2, influenza A (H1N1), or respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection. FINDINGS: Antigen-specific IgA and IgG measurements in PExA samples showed low variability (median CVs: spike-IgA 3.7%, H1-IgA 7.2%, RSV pre-F-IgA 5.3%). Strong correlations (Spearman's rho >0.85, p < 0.0001) were observed between PExA and serum IgG, which may be consistent with a systemic contribution to lower-airway IgG levels. In contrast, IgA correlations were more modest, which may reflect local IgA production in the lungs. IgG and IgA correlated between PExA and nasal secretions, while the IgA/IgG ratio was higher in nasal secretions (median 5.0 vs 0.6, p < 0.0001), consistent with expected isotype distribution in upper and lower airways. INTERPRETATION: This study demonstrates the feasibility of non-invasive measurement of antigen-specific antibodies in the lower airways. Our approach proposes a framework for assessing lower-airway immunity and supporting next-generation mucosal vaccine development. FUNDING: This study was funded by the European Research Council, the Swedish Society for Medical Research, and the Knut and Alice Wallenberg Foundation.

FINDINGS: Antigen-specific IgA and IgG measurements in PExA samples showed low variability (median CVs: spike-IgA 3.7%, H1-IgA 7.2%, RSV pre-F-IgA 5.3%). Strong correlations (Spearman's rho >0.85, p < 0.0001) were observed between PExA and serum IgG, which may be consistent with a systemic contribution to lower-airway IgG levels. In contrast, IgA correlations were more modest, which may reflect local IgA production in the lungs. IgG and IgA correlated between PExA and nasal secretions, while the IgA/IgG ratio was higher in nasal secretions (median 5.0 vs 0.6, p < 0.0001), consistent with expected isotype distribution in upper and lower airways. INTERPRETATION: This study demonstrates the feasibility of non-invasive measurement of antigen-specific antibodies in the lower airways. Our approach proposes a framework for assessing lower-airway immunity and supporting next-generation mucosal vaccine development. FUNDING: This study was funded by the European Research Council, the Swedish Society for Medical Research, and the Knut and Alice Wallenberg Foundation.

title: Upper Airway and Neurological Manifestations of Pediatric Omicron Infection: From Novel Pathogen to Endemic Respiratory Virus — A Natural Experiment in Immuno-naive versus Primed Children
abstract: Abstract Background The Omicron variant of SARS-CoV-2 has been associated with altered clinical phenotypes in children, including upper airway involvement and neurological complications. However, the magnitude of these manifestations relative to established pediatric respiratory viruses remains incompletely quantified, and the extent to which immune priming attenuates severity is unknown. We aimed to characterize upper airway obstruction (UAO) and neurological events in hospitalized children with Omicron infection, to compare outcomes with respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and human rhinovirus (HRV) using propensity score-matched analyzes, and to leverage a unique natural experiment to assess the impact of first versus second immune exposure on disease severity. Methods In this retrospective cohort study, we identified 2,085 hospitalized children (0–18 years) with laboratory-confirmed infection: 211 with Omicron (temporal proxy), 424 with RSV, 824 with HRV, and 957 with other viruses. Primary outcomes were UAO and neurological events. Propensity score matching (1:2) compared Omicron with RSV and HRV, adjusting for age, sex, comorbidities, and admission severity. A natural-experiment analysis compared first exposure (Wave 1, December 2022–February 2023, n = 82) versus second exposure (Wave 2+, March–December 2023, n = 51) among children ≥ 6 months of age. Age-stratified and wave-period analyzes were prespecified. Results UAO occurred in 20 of 211 children with Omicron (9.5%, 95% CI 5.9–14.2%) versus 1 of 424 with RSV (0.2%) and 1 of 824 with HRV (0.2%). Any neurological event was observed in 44 of 211 with Omicron (20.9%, 95% CI 15.7–26.9%) versus 20 of 424 with RSV (4.7%) and 26 of 824 with HRV (3.2%). After matching, Omicron was associated with increased risks of MODS score ≥ 2 (vs. RSV: RR 3.80, 95% CI 1.84–7.86; vs. HRV: RR 4.50, 95% CI 2.32–8.72), non-febrile neurological events (vs. RSV: RR 5.2, 95% CI 2.8–9.6; vs. HRV: RR 6.8, 95% CI 3.9–11.8), and severe adverse outcomes (vs. RSV: RR 3.08, 95% CI 1.52–6.24; vs. HRV: RR 3.85, 95% CI 1.98–7.49). In the immune exposure analysis, severe outcomes were markedly lower after second exposure (13.7%) than after first exposure (45.1%; p < 0.001), representing a 71% relative reduction. UAO decreased from 18.3% to 2.0% (p = 0.005), while LRTI rates were unchanged (45.1% vs. 56.9%; p = 0.214), indicating immune “taming” of severity without prevention of infection. Conclusions Pediatric Omicron infection was associated with substantially higher rates of UAO and neurological events than RSV or HRV, with risks extending beyond infancy. Immune priming dramatically attenuated severe outcomes and upper airway toxicity, though lower respiratory involvement persisted. These findings document the transition of Omicron from a novel, severe pediatric pathogen toward an established respiratory virus, and highlight the need for age-specific clinical vigilance and ongoing surveillance.

Age-stratified and wave-period analyzes were prespecified. analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the clinical manifestations of pediatric Omicron infection, comparing it to RSV and HRV. It found that Omicron was associated with significantly higher rates of upper airway obstruction and neurological events than RSV or HRV. Propensity score matching revealed increased risks of severe outcomes with Omicron compared to these viruses. The study is limited by its retrospective design and the absence of detailed limitations or evidence strength assessment.

title_zh: 儿科 Omicron 感染的上呼吸道和神经系统表现:从新型病原体到地方性呼吸道病毒 - 免疫初始儿童与已免疫儿童的自然实验
source_body_en: Abstract Background The Omicron variant of SARS-CoV-2 has been associated with altered clinical phenotypes in children, including upper airway involvement and neurological complications. However, the magnitude of these manifestations relative to established pediatric respiratory viruses remains incompletely quantified, and the extent to which immune priming attenuates severity is unknown. We aimed to characterize upper airway obstruction (UAO) and neurological events in hospitalized children with Omicron infection, to compare outcomes with respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and human rhinovirus (HRV) using propensity score-matched analyzes, and to leverage a unique natural experiment to assess the impact of first versus second immune exposure on disease severity. Methods In this retrospective cohort study, we identified 2,085 hospitalized children (0–18 years) with laboratory-confirmed infection: 211 with Omicron (temporal proxy), 424 with RSV, 824 with HRV, and 957 with other viruses. Primary outcomes were UAO and neurological events. Propensity score matching (1:2) compared Omicron with RSV and HRV, adjusting for age, sex, comorbidities, and admission severity. A natural-experiment analysis compared first exposure (Wave 1, December 2022–February 2023, n = 82) versus second exposure (Wave 2+, March–December 2023, n = 51) among children ≥ 6 months of age. Age-stratified and wave-period analyzes were prespecified. Results UAO occurred in 20 of 211 children with Omicron (9.5%, 95% CI 5.9–14.2%) versus 1 of 424 with RSV (0.2%) and 1 of 824 with HRV (0.2%). Any neurological event was observed in 44 of 211 with Omicron (20.9%, 95% CI 15.7–26.9%) versus 20 of 424 with RSV (4.7%) and 26 of 824 with HRV (3.2%). After matching, Omicron was associated with increased risks of MODS score ≥ 2 (vs. RSV: RR 3.80, 95% CI 1.84–7.86; vs. HRV: RR 4.50, 95% CI 2.32–8.72), non-febrile neurological events (vs. RSV: RR 5.2, 95% CI 2.8–9.6; vs. HRV: RR 6.8, 95% CI 3.9–11.8), and severe adverse outcomes (vs. RSV: RR 3.08, 95% CI 1.52–6.24; vs. HRV: RR 3.85, 95% CI 1.98–7.49). In the immune exposure analysis, severe outcomes were markedly lower after second exposure (13.7%) than after first exposure (45.1%; p < 0.001), representing a 71% relative reduction. UAO decreased from 18.3% to 2.0% (p = 0.005), while LRTI rates were unchanged (45.1% vs. 56.9%; p = 0.214), indicating immune “taming” of severity without prevention of infection. Conclusions Pediatric Omicron infection was associated with substantially higher rates of UAO and neurological events than RSV or HRV, with risks extending beyond infancy. Immune priming dramatically attenuated severe outcomes and upper airway toxicity, though lower respiratory involvement persisted. These findings document the transition of Omicron from a novel, severe pediatric pathogen toward an established respiratory virus, and highlight the need for age-specific clinical vigilance and ongoing surveillance.

title: Impact of national RSV immunization programme on the epidemiology of bronchiolitis in Greece.
abstract: Abstract Universal RSV immunization strategies for infants, including monoclonal antibody administration and maternal vaccination during pregnancy, were implemented in Greece for the first time during the 2025–2026 season. We conducted a prospective observational study of infants aged <12 months hospitalized with bronchiolitis at a quaternary paediatric hospital in Greece between November 2025 and April 2026. Bronchiolitis incidence was compared with that of the 2023–2024 and 2024–2025 seasons. Severity of bronchiolitis was assessed using the modified Tal score. Across the three seasons, 854 of 15246 admissions were due to bronchiolitis. The incidence decreased significantly in 2025–2026 to 42 per 1000 admissions, compared to 64 and 59 in 2024–2025 and 2023–2024, respectively. The 2025–2026 epidemic curve of bronchiolitis was flatter and more prolonged, with a delayed peak in March. Of 186 infants with bronchiolitis, 19.9% had received RSV immunization. Disease severity and oxygen requirements did not differ significantly between immunized and unimmunized infants, although unimmunized infants were older and had a trend towards higher complication rates. In conclusion, national RSV immunization was associated with reduced bronchiolitis hospitalizations and complications. However, the smaller-than-expected reduction in disease rates underscores the need to improve awareness, coverage, and timely immunization.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the impact of the national RSV immunization programme on bronchiolitis epidemiology in Greece during the 2025–2026 season. A prospective observational study was conducted at a quaternary paediatric hospital, comparing bronchiolitis incidence across three seasons. The results showed a significant decrease in bronchiolitis admissions in 2025–2026 compared to previous years, with the epidemic curve being flatter and more prolonged. The authors interpreted this as an association between RSV immunization and reduced hospitalizations and complications. The findings suggest that immunization could be a valuable strategy for mitigating bronchiolitis burden. However, the smaller-than-expected reduction highlights the need for improved awareness and coverage. The evidence is moderate, as the study is observational and does not establish causality.

title: Estimating viral interference from wastewater surveillance: a Bayesian multi-pathogen SEIR framework.
abstract: The concurrent circulation of influenza, SARS-CoV-2, and RSV creates complex transmission dynamics in which infection with one virus may reduce or enhance transmission of another. We developed a Bayesian multi-pathogen SEIR model in which the transmission of each virus is reduced by the prevalence of co-circulating pathogens, quantified by an aggregate population-level interference coefficient θ. We fit the model to weekly wastewater data from six Canadian provinces over the 2024-2025 respiratory season, avoiding the use of clinical data, which are limited by under-reporting and inconsistent testing. Our findings show the estimated interference corresponded to a 4 to 30% reduction in peak transmission of each virus during co-circulation, with smaller reductions in the effective reproduction number. Although these estimates are based on a single respiratory season and can vary under different patterns of co-circulation, they are consistent with recent studies on multi-pathogen viral interference using clinical surveillance data.

title: Sociodemographic and Clinical Factors Associated With Nirsevimab Receipt Among Children Aged Younger Than 20 Months in the New Vaccine Surveillance Network in 2023 to 2025.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: We aim to evaluate the association of sociodemographic and clinical factors with nirsevimab receipt among children with medically attended acute respiratory illness (ARI) across multiple seasons and beyond birth hospitalization. PATIENTS AND METHODS: We included nirsevimab-eligible children aged younger than 8 months and 8 to 19 months with ARI enrolled in the New Vaccine Surveillance Network during the 2023 to 2024 and 2024 to 2025 respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) seasons (October 1 to March 31). A mixed-effects logistic regression model was used to evaluate the association between sociodemographic and clinical factors with the likelihood of nirsevimab receipt among enrolled children aged younger than 8 months. RESULTS: Of the 2151 nirsevimab-eligible children with ARI enrolled in the 2023 to 2024 RSV season and 1819 in the 2024 to 2025 RSV season, 96% were aged younger than 8 months and in their first RSV season. Fourteen percent and 36% of eligible children aged younger than 8 months received nirsevimab in the 2023 to 2024 and 2024 to 2025 seasons, respectively. Among infants aged younger than 8 months, those born during the RSV season and those with an underlying medical condition were more likely to receive nirsevimab in both RSV seasons; infant female sex and maternal education were also associated with nirsevimab receipt during 2023 to 2024 but not 2024 to 2025. CONCLUSION: Most nirsevimab-eligible children with medically attended ARI in this analysis did not receive nirsevimab during the first 2 seasons of nirsevimab availability. Factors such as birth before the RSV season were associated with a decreased likelihood of nirsevimab receipt, emphasizing the need for tailored interventions following birth hospitalization to increase nirsevimab uptake for this group of children.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the factors associated with nirsevimab receipt among children with medically attended acute respiratory illness (ARI) during the first two seasons of its availability. The research focused on children aged younger than 20 months enrolled in the New Vaccine Surveillance Network during the 2023 to 2024 and 2024 to 2025 RSV seasons. The study used a mixed-effects logistic regression model to analyze sociodemographic and clinical factors. Results showed that 14% and 36% of eligible children aged younger than 8 months received nirsevimab in the 2023 to 2024 and 2024 to 2025 seasons, respectively. Infants born during the RSV season and those with underlying medical conditions were more likely to receive the vaccine, while female sex and maternal education were associated with receipt in the first season but not the second. The study concluded that most eligible children did not receive nirsevimab, emphasizing the need for tailored interventions to improve uptake. The findings suggest potential strategies for increasing vaccine access and highlight the importance of considering birth timing and medical conditions in vaccination programs.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在评估多个季节和出生后住院治疗的急性呼吸道疾病 (ARI) 儿童中社会人口统计学和临床​​因素与 尼塞韦单抗 收据的关联。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究包括在 2023 年至 2024 年和 2024 年至 2025 年 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 季节(10 月 1 日至 3 月 31 日)期间加入新 疫苗 监测 网络的符合 尼塞韦单抗 资格的儿童,年龄小于 8 个月和 8 至 19 个月,患有 ARI。
elements_zh.methods: 使用混合效应逻辑回归模型来评估社会人口统计学和临床​​因素与 8 个月以下入组儿童接受 尼塞韦单抗 的可能性之间的关联。
elements_zh.main_results: 在2023至2024呼吸道合胞病毒流行季入组的2151名符合尼塞韦单抗条件的儿童中,以及在2024至2025呼吸道合胞病毒流行季入组的1819名儿童中,96%年龄小于8个月且处于首个呼吸道合胞病毒流行季。在年龄小于8个月的符合条件儿童中,于2023至2024流行季和2024至2025流行季分别有14%和36%接种了尼塞韦单抗。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 在 8 个月以下的婴儿中,在 RSV 季节出生的婴儿和有基础疾病的婴儿更有可能在两个 RSV 季节接受 尼塞韦单抗;婴儿女性性别和母亲教育也与 2023 年至 2024 年期间的 尼塞韦单抗 收据相关,但与 2024 年至 2025 年无关。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果强调,需要采取有针对性的干预措施,以提高符合条件的儿童,特别是在 RSV 季节之前出生的儿童对 尼塞韦单抗 的吸收。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 所提供的证据并未报告局限性,但该研究基于新 疫苗 监测 网络的数据,这可能会限制对其他人群的普遍适用性。

abstract_zh: 目的:我们的目的是评估社会人口统计学和临床​​因素与在多个季节和出生后住院治疗的急性呼吸道疾病 (ARI) 儿童中接受 尼塞韦单抗 的关系。患者和方法:我们纳入了在 2023 年至 2024 年和 2024 年至 2025 年 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 季节(10 月 1 日至 3 月 31 日)期间加入新 疫苗 监测 网络的符合 尼塞韦单抗 资格的儿童,年龄小于 8 个月和 8 至 19 个月。使用混合效应逻辑回归模型来评估社会人口统计学和临床​​因素与 8 个月以下入组儿童接受 尼塞韦单抗 的可能性之间的关联。结果:在 2023 年至 2024 年 RSV 季节登记的 2151 名符合 尼塞韦单抗 资格的 ARI 儿童和 2024 年至 2025 年 RSV 季节登记的 1819 名儿童中,96% 的年龄小于 8 个月且处于第一个 RSV 季节。在 2023 年至 2024 年和 2024 年至 2025 年季节,分别有 14% 和 36% 的 8 个月以下符合条件的儿童获得了 尼塞韦单抗。在 8 个月以下的婴儿中,在 RSV 季节出生的婴儿和有基础疾病的婴儿更有可能在两个 RSV 季节接受 尼塞韦单抗;婴儿女性性别和母亲教育也与 2023 年至 2024 年期间的 尼塞韦单抗 接收相关,但与 2024 年至 2025 年无关。结论:本次分析中,大多数符合 尼塞韦单抗 资格且就医的 ARI 儿童在 尼塞韦单抗 可用性的前 2 个季节期间没有接受 尼塞韦单抗。RSV 季节之前出生等因素与 尼塞韦单抗 接收的可能性降低相关,强调需要在出生住院后采取量身定制的干预措施,以增加该组儿童对 尼塞韦单抗 的吸收。

title: A Confirmatory, Dual Center Nonhuman Primate Study on the Efficacy of Novel Oropharyngeal Spray Immunization With an Adenoviral Vector Vaccine Against RSV-Important Lessons Learned.
abstract: BACKGROUND: In a randomized, blinded, dual center study across two European primate research facilities, we evaluated the immunogenicity and protective efficacy of a DNA prime-oropharyngeal adenoviral boost vaccination strategy against respiratory syncytial virus (RSV). METHODS: Rhesus macaques received an RSV fusion protein (F) DNA vaccine via electroporation, followed by two mucosal administrations of a recombinant adenovirus vector encoding the same antigen. Mock-vaccinated animals and a comparator group mimicking natural immunity induced by primary RSV infection were included as controls. Systemic and mucosal immune responses were monitored longitudinally. RESULTS: We detected robust cellular and humoral immune responses, but with some variability between the two centers. Nevertheless, RSV-vaccinated animals demonstrated markedly reduced viral replication in the upper and lower respiratory tract after RSV challenge infection. Unexpected RSV-specific immunity in the control group at one single study site prevented confirmation of the predefined primary endpoint. CONCLUSION: Our results support the potential of mucosal adenoviral boosting following DNA priming to induce protective immunity against RSV, while highlighting challenges associated with multi-center preclinical vaccine studies.

title: Multi-virus Wastewater Surveillance in Heterogeneous Urban-Sewage Systems: Comparative Insights From Sewage Treatment Plants and Open Drains.
abstract: Wastewater-based epidemiology (WBE) has been applied for public health surveillance for several decades but gained unprecedented global prominence during the COVID-19 pandemic, leading to its broader adoption for multi-pathogen surveillance. However, the impact of heterogeneous urban wastewater infrastructure on the detection and interpretation of pathogen signals remains inadequately characterised, particularly in settings such as Mumbai, with fragmented and partially connected sewer networks. This study systematically compared multi-pathogen wastewater surveillance from centralised sewage treatment plants (STPs) and decentralised open drains (ODs), which represent aggregated and localised population catchments, respectively. Wastewater was collected during two monitoring periods (2023 and 2024) and analysed by RT-qPCR for SARS-CoV-2, influenza viruses, and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV). Comparative analyses included detection frequency, temporal dynamics, and patterns of viral co-occurrence between node types. Viral detection rates were highest in STP influent, consistent with signal integration over larger populations and reduced short-term variability. Conversely, open drains exhibited greater temporal fluctuation, which may be consistent with localised, short-term changes but with reduced signal persistence. In the absence of concurrent clinical data, these node-level differences are interpreted as patterns in the wastewater signal rather than demonstrated gains in epidemiological sensitivity or earlier detection. SARS-CoV-2 was consistently detected across both node types, while influenza virus detection was more sporadic and exhibited marked variability, suggesting seasonal transmission dynamics. Co-detection of influenza A and B was observed in 2023, and influenza A subtyping revealed limited within-type diversity; source attribution for the detected subtypes could not be determined. Collectively, these findings indicate that wastewater signal profiles reflect an interplay between pathogen-specific characteristics and the structural configuration of the sampling network. Overall, the findings support integrated surveillance frameworks that leverage both centralised and decentralised nodes, while highlighting the need for extended temporal monitoring and independent clinical validation to strengthen epidemiological inference.

title: Prompt engineering for epidemiological surveillance: A step toward wider access to public health data analysis through natural language processing.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to describe and assess a framework that generates epidemiological analysis scripts from natural-language queries constrained by surveillance data dictionaries. STUDY DESIGN: Methodological framework development with internal consistency assessment. METHODS: PEFES (Prompt Engineering for Epidemiological Surveillance) restricts large language model output to dictionary-declared variables and coding schemes, validates scope before generating a script, and does not execute code. Two authors with prior programming experience ('raters') submitted identical sets of 22 in-scope and 22 scope-control queries across three case studies (respiratory syncytial virus, influenza A and dengue) using Claude Opus 4.8 and Gemini 3.7 Flash against OpenDataSUS datasets. RESULTS: The two raters agreed on the behavior for all 22 scope-control queries: the 17 queries that were expected to be declined did not produce a script, and all 5 in-scope counterparts produced a script. Every source field read was dictionary-declared. Reported values were identical for 14 of the 22 in-scope queries and divergent for 8 (all where a prompt left a choice unstated). One session compared a declared field against wrong-type values, returning empty tables under formatted headings. CONCLUSIONS: Dictionary constraints restricted which data a generated script could analyze, but not how it was analyzed: reproducibility was dependent on both the prompt and dictionary, not the constraint mechanism alone. Errors within the declared set were identified by rater review, not by the framework, motivating pre-execution type checks or returning unstated choices as clarification requests. PEFES accelerates epidemiological work rather than replacing it, and it is a step toward wider access to surveillance data analysis.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to describe and assess a framework that generates epidemiological analysis scripts from natural-language queries constrained by surveillance data dictionaries. The framework was developed to address the need for more accessible public health data analysis tools.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved the development of a methodological framework with internal consistency assessment. Two authors with prior programming experience submitted identical sets of 22 in-scope and 22 scope-control queries across three case studies (respiratory syncytial virus, influenza A, and dengue) using Claude Opus 4.8 and Gemini 3.7 Flash against OpenDataSUS datasets.
analysis.methods: PEFES (Prompt Engineering for Epidemiological Surveillance) restricts large language model output to dictionary-declared variables and coding schemes, validates scope before generating a script, and does not execute code. The framework was tested by comparing generated scripts against predefined queries and datasets.
analysis.main_results: The two raters agreed on the behavior for all 22 scope-control queries: the 17 queries that were expected to be declined did not produce a script, and all 5 in-scope counterparts produced a script. Every source field read was dictionary-declared. Reported values were identical for 14 of the 22 in-scope queries and divergent for 8 (all where a prompt left a choice unstated).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Dictionary constraints restricted which data a generated script could analyze, but not how it was analyzed: reproducibility was dependent on both the prompt and dictionary, not the constraint mechanism alone. The study highlights the potential of natural language processing in epidemiological surveillance.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: PEFES accelerates epidemiological work rather than replacing it, and it is a step toward wider access to surveillance data analysis. This could enhance the efficiency of public health data processing and interpretation.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Errors within the declared set were identified by rater review, not by the framework, motivating pre-execution type checks or returning unstated choices as clarification requests. The evidence is moderate as the study is based on internal consistency assessment and limited case studies.

analysis.summary_en: This study introduces PEFES, a framework that generates epidemiological analysis scripts from natural-language queries constrained by surveillance data dictionaries. The aim was to assess the framework's ability to restrict data analysis to dictionary-declared variables and coding schemes. The study involved two authors with programming experience submitting identical sets of 22 in-scope and 22 scope-control queries across three case studies (respiratory syncytial virus, influenza A, and dengue) using large language models against OpenDataSUS datasets. The results showed that all 17 scope-control queries were declined, while all 5 in-scope queries produced scripts. Every source field read was dictionary-declared, and reported values were identical for 14 of the 22 in-scope queries. The authors concluded that dictionary constraints limit data analysis scope but not the analysis method itself, with reproducibility depending on both the prompt and dictionary. The framework's potential to accelerate epidemiological work and improve access to surveillance data analysis is highlighted, though the study's evidence is moderate due to its reliance on internal consistency assessment and limited case studies.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在描述和评估一个框架,该框架根据 监测 数据字典约束的自然语言查询生成流行病学分析脚本。该框架的开发是为了满足对更易于使用的公共卫生数据分析工具的需求。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究涉及开发具有内部一致性评估的方法框架。两位具有编程经验的作者使用 Claude Opus 4.8 和 Gemini 3.7 Flash 针对 OpenDataSUS 数据集在三个案例研究(呼吸道合胞病毒、甲型流感和登革热)中提交了相同的 22 个范围内查询和 22 个范围控制查询集。
elements_zh.methods: PEFES(流行病学提示工程 监测)将大型语言模型输出限制为字典声明的变量和编码方案,在生成脚本之前验证范围,并且不执行代码。通过将生成的脚本与预定义的查询和数据集进行比较来测试该框架。

elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 字典约束限制了生成的脚本可以分析哪些数据,但不限制如何分析数据:可重复性取决于提示和字典,而不仅仅是约束机制。该研究强调了自然语言处理在流行病学领域的潜力 监测。

The framework was developed to address the need for more accessible public health data analysis tools.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: The study involved the development of a methodological framework with internal consistency assessment. Two authors with prior programming experience submitted identical sets of 22 in-scope and 22 scope-control queries across three case studies (respiratory syncytial virus, influenza A, and dengue) using Claude Opus 4.8 and Gemini 3.7 Flash against OpenDataSUS datasets.
analysis_en.methods: PEFES (Prompt Engineering for Epidemiological Surveillance) restricts large language model output to dictionary-declared variables and coding schemes, validates scope before generating a script, and does not execute code. The framework was tested by comparing generated scripts against predefined queries and datasets.
analysis_en.main_results: The two raters agreed on the behavior for all 22 scope-control queries: the 17 queries that were expected to be declined did not produce a script, and all 5 in-scope counterparts produced a script. analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: Dictionary constraints restricted which data a generated script could analyze, but not how it was analyzed: reproducibility was dependent on both the prompt and dictionary, not the constraint mechanism alone. analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: PEFES accelerates epidemiological work rather than replacing it, and it is a step toward wider access to surveillance data analysis. This could enhance the efficiency of public health data processing and interpretation.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Errors within the declared set were identified by rater review, not by the framework, motivating pre-execution type checks or returning unstated choices as clarification requests. title_zh: 流行病学 监测 的快速工程:通过自然语言处理更广泛地获取公共卫生数据分析的一步。
source_body_en: OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to describe and assess a framework that generates epidemiological analysis scripts from natural-language queries constrained by surveillance data dictionaries. STUDY DESIGN: Methodological framework development with internal consistency assessment. METHODS: PEFES (Prompt Engineering for Epidemiological Surveillance) restricts large language model output to dictionary-declared variables and coding schemes, validates scope before generating a script, and does not execute code. Two authors with prior programming experience ('raters') submitted identical sets of 22 in-scope and 22 scope-control queries across three case studies (respiratory syncytial virus, influenza A and dengue) using Claude Opus 4.8 and Gemini 3.7 Flash against OpenDataSUS datasets. RESULTS: The two raters agreed on the behavior for all 22 scope-control queries: the 17 queries that were expected to be declined did not produce a script, and all 5 in-scope counterparts produced a script. Every source field read was dictionary-declared. Reported values were identical for 14 of the 22 in-scope queries and divergent for 8 (all where a prompt left a choice unstated). One session compared a declared field against wrong-type values, returning empty tables under formatted headings. CONCLUSIONS: Dictionary constraints restricted which data a generated script could analyze, but not how it was analyzed: reproducibility was dependent on both the prompt and dictionary, not the constraint mechanism alone. Errors within the declared set were identified by rater review, not by the framework, motivating pre-execution type checks or returning unstated choices as clarification requests. PEFES accelerates epidemiological work rather than replacing it, and it is a step toward wider access to surveillance data analysis.
abstract_zh: 目标:本研究的目的是描述和评估一个框架,该框架根据 监测 数据字典约束的自然语言查询生成流行病学分析脚本。研究设计:方法框架开发和内部一致性评估。方法:PEFES(流行病学提示工程 监测)将大型语言模型输出限制为字典声明的变量和编码方案,在生成脚本之前验证范围,并且不执行代码。两位具有编程经验的作者(“评估者”)使用 Claude Opus 4.8 和 Gemini 3.7 Flash 针对 OpenDataSUS 数据集在三个案例研究(呼吸道合胞病毒、甲型流感和登革热)中提交了相同的 22 个范围内查询和 22 个范围控制查询。结果:两位评估者就所有 22 个范围控制查询的行为达成一致:预计被拒绝的 17 个查询没有生成脚本,而所有 5 个范围内对应查询都生成了脚本。读取的每个源字段都是字典声明的。22 个范围内查询中,有 14 个查询的报告值相同,有 8 个查询的报告值不同(所有查询均在提示中留下了未说明的选项)。一个会话将声明的字段与错误类型的值进行比较,在格式化标题下返回空表。结论:字典约束限制了生成的脚本可以分析哪些数据,但不限制分析数据的方式:再现性取决于提示和字典,而不是单独的约束机制。声明的集合中的错误是由评估者审查而不是由框架识别的,从而激发执行前类型检查或返回未声明的选择作为澄清请求。PEFES 加速了流行病学工作,而不是取代它,这是朝着更广泛地获取 监测 数据分析迈出的一步。

title: First- and Second-Year Outcomes After Nirsevimab Immunization.
abstract: IMPORTANCE: The consistency of nirsevimab effectiveness across consecutive seasons and its broader clinical protective effects remain to be fully characterized. OBJECTIVE: To assess whether first-season effectiveness of nirsevimab against respiratory syncytial virus (RSV)-lower respiratory tract infection (LRTI)-related hospitalizations is maintained during a new RSV season, whether the effectiveness persists beyond the first season, and whether nirsevimab exposure is associated with hospitalizations for non-RSV infections and asthma during the first and second years of follow-up. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This cohort study analyzed 2 nationwide matched cohorts using the French National Health Data System, including infants born in metropolitan France before the 2023 and 2024 immunization campaigns. Infants receiving nirsevimab were matched 1:1 to unimmunized infants. Both cohorts were followed up for 1 year after immunization, with an additional second year of follow-up for the 2023 cohort. Data analysis was performed from February 2023 to August 2025. EXPOSURES: Single dose of nirsevimab. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: RSV-LRTI-related, non-RSV infection, and asthma hospitalizations were assessed using weighted Cox proportional hazards models. RESULTS: This cohort study included 74 672 infants in 2023 and 175 526 in 2024. At baseline, the mean (SD) age of immunized infants was 4.5 (2.0) months in the 2023 cohort; 19 633 (52.6%) were male and 17 703 (47.4%) were female. The mean (SD) age of the 2024 cohort was 4.8 (2.2) months; 44 863 immunized infants (51.1%) were male and 42 900 (48.9%) were female. Among 37 366 infant pairs in 2023 and 87 763 pairs in 2024, RSV-LRTI-related hospitalizations during the first year of follow-up occurred in 299 (0.8%) immunized vs 899 (2.4%) unimmunized infants in 2023 and 456 (0.5%) vs 1711 (1.9%), respectively, in 2024. Nirsevimab was associated with a lower rate of RSV-LRTI-related hospitalization in both the 2023 and 2024 cohort during the first year of follow-up, with effectiveness estimates of 66% (95% CI, 61%-70%) and 72% (95% CI, 69%-75%), respectively. An association with higher rates of hospitalization for ear, nose, and throat (ENT) bacterial infections was observed (2023 cohort: weighted hazard ratio [wHR], 1.36; 95% CI, 1.00-1.84; 2024 cohort: wHR, 1.43; 95% CI, 1.15-1.78). No significant association was observed for other outcomes. During the second year of follow-up, no protective association was observed for RSV-LRTI-related hospitalization (wHR, 1.03; 95% CI, 0.73-1.43). An association with higher rates of hospitalization for ENT (wHR, 1.56; 95% CI, 1.10-2.22) and asthma (wHR, 1.24; 95% CI, 1.05-1.46) was observed. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: This study found that nirsevimab was associated with a substantial reduction in RSV-LRTI-related hospitalizations during the first year across both the 2023-2024 and 2024-2025 seasons. It was not associated with reduced hospitalizations due to non-RSV infections or asthma, nor during the second year of follow-up.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在评估 尼塞韦单抗 在连续季节中对 RSV-LRTI 相关住院治疗的有效性,及其与随访第一年和第二年因非 RSV 感染和哮喘住院的关系。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项 队列研究 研究使用法国国家健康数据系统分析了 2 个全国匹配的 队列研究,其中包括 2023 年和 2024 年免疫接种活动之前在法国本土出生的婴儿。接受 尼塞韦单抗 的婴儿与未免疫婴儿以 1:1 进行匹配。两种 队列研究 均在免疫后随访 1 年,并对 2023 队列研究 进行第二年随访。
elements_zh.methods: 使用加权 Cox 比例风险模型评估 RSV-LRTI 相关、非 RSV 感染和哮喘住院情况。数据分析于2023年2月至2025年8月进行。

title: The Impact of Socioeconomic and Geographic Factors in Respiratory Virus Testing in Australia.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) causes significant disease burden in Australia, yet most confirmatory laboratory data come from acute healthcare settings. This study analyses RSV and other respiratory virus testing across different socio-demographic groups and healthcare settings using data from private and public laboratories Australia-wide. METHODOLOGY: We analysed de-identified nucleic acid amplification test (NAATs) data for RSV (n=9.35 million), influenza A (n=9.42 million), influenza B (n=9.26 million), and SARS-CoV-2 (n=52.94 million) from 1 September 2017 to 31 August 2023, sourced from the three largest private and two public pathology providers in Australia. Data were stratified by socio-economic indexes for areas (SEIFA), remoteness, age, jurisdiction and care settings. Population-adjusted testing rates and positivity percentages were calculated. RESULTS: NAATs were highest in the most advantaged socio-economic quintile and major cities, declining with increased socio-economic disadvantage and geographic remoteness. Positivity rates were highest in the most advantaged quintile, but no consistent pattern was seen across other quintiles. Community settings accounted for most RSV testing, predominantly by private pathology providers. The COVID-19 pandemic from 2020 altered NAAT panels used and disrupted usual seasonal trends for RSV and influenza. CONCLUSION: Substantial variation exists in respiratory virus NAAT and positivity rates across socio-demographic groups, jurisdictions, and healthcare settings. Improving equitable access to testing among disadvantaged and remote populations is essential for accurate surveillance, timely intervention and effective prioritisation of public health interventions.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在解决澳大利亚不同社会经济和地理环境中呼吸道病毒检测模式的巨大差距,重点关注呼吸道合胞病毒和其他呼吸道病毒。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究分析了 2017 年 9 月 1 日至 2023 年 8 月 31 日期间 RSV、甲型流感、乙型流感和 SARS-CoV-2 的去识别化核酸扩增测试 (NAAT) 数据,这些数据来自澳大利亚三个最大的私人和两个公共病理学提供商,涉及各种社会经济指标、偏远地区、年龄、管辖范围和护理环境。
elements_zh.methods: RSV、甲型流感、乙型流感和 SARS-CoV-2 的 NAAT 数据按地区社会经济指数 (SEIFA)、偏远程度、年龄、管辖范围和护理环境进行分层,并计算了人口调整后的检测率和阳性百分比。
elements_zh.main_results: RSV NAAT 在最有利的社会经济五分位和主要城市中最高,随着社会经济劣势和地理偏远的增加而下降。最有利的五分之一的阳性率最高,但在其他五分之一中没有看到一致的模式。社区环境占 RSV 检测的大部分,主要由私人病理学提供者进行。COVID-19 大流行改变了 NAAT 检测组的使用,并扰乱了 RSV 和流感的通常季节性趋势。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究发现,不同社会人口群体、司法管辖区和医疗机构的呼吸道病毒 NAAT 和阳性率存在显着差异,这凸显了弱势群体和偏远人群公平获得检测机会的必要性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 改善弱势和偏远人群获得检测的公平机会对于准确的 监测、及时干预和有效确定公共卫生干预措施的优先顺序至关重要。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的结果受到对去识别化数据的依赖以及测试模式可能存在偏差的限制。样本量和数据来源很全面,但可能无法完全代表澳大利亚的所有社会经济和地理区域。

title: Air sampling for facility-based respiratory pathogen surveillance in rural Zambia: a prospective comparison with human surveillance
abstract: Abstract Respiratory infections are the leading cause of acute disease incidence globally and disproportionately burden low-and middle-income countries where surveillance capacity is limited. While facility-based surveillance remains the standard for respiratory pathogen monitoring in human populations, environmental air sampling offers potential advantages as a non-invasive supplementary method. We conducted a prospective environmental air sampling study nested within ongoing respiratory disease surveillance at Macha Hospital in Southern Province, Zambia, from July 2025 to June 2026. Air samplers were deployed continuously in the outpatient department and three inpatient wards, with filters collected and tested three times weekly. Surveillance in the patient population was conducted year-round with nasopharyngeal samples collected from patients with influenza-like illness. All samples were tested for influenza A/B virus, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), and SARS-CoV-2 using the Cepheid GeneXpert platform. We analyzed concordance between air and nasopharyngeal samples using percent agreement, Cohen’s Kappa, Spearman correlations, and logistic regression with generalized estimating equations. Over 12 months, 596 air samples and 701 human samples were analyzed. Influenza A virus was the most common pathogen, detected in 38 air samples and 87 nasopharyngeal samples, with most cases detected from July to September 2025. For Influenza A, there was strong same-week concordance between air and nasopharyngeal samples (80.4% overall agreement; 44.4% positive agreement; Cohen’s Kappa = 0.5; Spearman’s rho = 0.57). SARS-CoV-2 was also common, detected in 18 air samples and 16 nasopharyngeal samples, with cases detected sporadically throughout the year. For SARS-CoV-2, there was limited concordance between air and nasopharyngeal samples (68.6% agreement; 23.8% positive agreement; Cohen’s Kappa = 0.2; Spearman’s rho = 0.2). Influenza B virus (1 air and 13 nasopharyngeal samples positive) and RSV (0 air and 4 nasopharyngeal samples positive) circulated sporadically, and unsurprisingly, gave limited concordance between samples. Cycle threshold values for influenza A virus (median for target 1: 36.7 vs. 25.1; p<0.001; median for target 2: 39.5 vs. 28.6; p<0.001) and SARS-CoV-2 (median: 41.3 vs. 27.5; p<0.001) were significantly higher for positive air samples than for nasopharyngeal samples. Implementation challenges were documented, including intermittent power outages and compromised electrical outlets causing sampler shutdowns, as well as study awareness issues that required sensitization activities for both facility staff and patients. Air sampling was feasible and demonstrated promise as a supplementary method for facility-based respiratory pathogen surveillance in rural resource-limited settings. These findings support integrating environmental air sampling alongside surveillance in patient populations as part of a multimodal approach to respiratory pathogen monitoring.

Surveillance in the patient population was conducted year-round with nasopharyngeal samples collected from patients with influenza-like illness. All samples were tested for influenza A/B virus, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), and SARS-CoV-2 using the Cepheid GeneXpert platform. We analyzed concordance between air and nasopharyngeal samples using percent agreement, Cohen’s Kappa, Spearman correlations, and logistic regression with generalized estimating equations. Over 12 months, 596 air samples and 701 human samples were analyzed. Influenza A virus was the most common pathogen, detected in 38 air samples and 87 nasopharyngeal samples, with most cases detected from July to September 2025. For Influenza A, there was strong same-week concordance between air and nasopharyngeal samples (80.4% overall agreement; 44.4% positive agreement; Cohen’s Kappa = 0.5; Spearman’s rho = 0.57). SARS-CoV-2 was also common, detected in 18 air samples and 16 nasopharyngeal samples, with cases detected sporadically throughout the year. For SARS-CoV-2, there was limited concordance between air and nasopharyngeal samples (68.6% agreement; 23.8% positive agreement; Cohen’s Kappa = 0.2; Spearman’s rho = 0.2). Influenza B virus (1 air and 13 nasopharyngeal samples positive) and RSV (0 air and 4 nasopharyngeal samples positive) circulated sporadically, and unsurprisingly, gave limited concordance between samples. Cycle threshold values for influenza A virus (median for target 1: 36.7 vs. 25.1; p<0.001; median for target 2: 39.5 vs. 28.6; p<0.001) and SARS-CoV-2 (median: 41.3 vs. 27.5; p<0.001) were significantly higher for positive air samples than for nasopharyngeal samples. Implementation challenges were documented, including intermittent power outages and compromised electrical outlets causing sampler shutdowns, as well as study awareness issues that required sensitization activities for both facility staff and patients. Air sampling was feasible and demonstrated promise as a supplementary method for facility-based respiratory pathogen surveillance in rural resource-limited settings. These findings support integrating environmental air sampling alongside surveillance in patient populations as part of a multimodal approach to respiratory pathogen monitoring.

title: RSV-specific humoral and cellular immune responses in kidney transplant recipients
abstract: Induction of virus-specific immune responses in kidney transplant recipients (KTR) by vaccination is challenging. However, it is not well-described whether pre-existing immunity against respiratory viruses initially encountered before transplantation, like respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), is maintained. Therefore, we assessed RSV-specific humoral and cellular immune responses in KTR and controls at two timepoints during the COVID-19 pandemic. Binding and neutralizing antibodies were determined in serum samples from 64 KTR and 37 controls. Cellular immune responses were measured in a cohort subset (15 KTR, 14 controls) by stimulation of peripheral blood mononuclear cells with RSV-derived peptide pools. This was followed by phenotypic analysis using an activation-induced marker assay and cytokine release assay. RSV-specific binding IgG and neutralizing antibody titers were comparable between KTR and controls and stable over time. While total lymphocyte levels were significantly lower in KTR, relative frequencies of RSV-specific CD4 + and CD8 + memory T cells were comparable between groups. Unsupervised hierarchical clustering distinguished three cytokine production profiles with divergent RSV-specific immune responses, but KTR and controls were equally distributed throughout. Thus, KTR have comparable RSV-specific humoral and cellular immune responses to controls. Our findings suggest that pre-existing respiratory virus-specific immune responses persist under immunosuppressive treatment.

title: Prenatal MRI Diagnosis and Favorable Neurodevelopmental Outcome in Isolated Medullary Tegmental Cap Dysplasia: A Case Report and Literature Review
abstract: Medullary tegmental cap dysplasia (MTCD) is an extremely rare congenital brainstem malformation, with few cases reported to date. We report a fetus referred for an occipital meningocele, in whom fetal MRI at 27 weeks’ gestation identified a dorsal protrusion of the medulla oblongata consistent with MTCD. No supratentorial, infratentorial, or extracerebral anomalies were detected. Prenatal investigations, including chromosomal microarray and trio whole-exome sequencing, were noncontributory. Postnatal magnetic resonance imaging confirmed isolated MTCD with an occipital meningocele and preserved transverse pontine fibers on diffusion tractography. Neonatal evaluation was unremarkable apart from transient feeding difficulties and obstructive sleep apnea in the context of RSV infection. At 16 months, the child showed normal neurodevelopment, including independent walking, language, and social interaction. This case expands the phenotypic spectrum of MTCD and suggests a favorable outcome when MTCD is isolated and genetic investigations are negative. Recognition on fetal imaging is essential for prenatal counseling and postnatal management.

No supratentorial, infratentorial, or extracerebral anomalies were detected. Prenatal investigations, including chromosomal microarray and trio whole-exome sequencing, were noncontributory. Postnatal magnetic resonance imaging confirmed isolated MTCD with an occipital meningocele and preserved transverse pontine fibers on diffusion tractography. Neonatal evaluation was unremarkable apart from transient feeding difficulties and obstructive sleep apnea in the context of RSV infection. At 16 months, the child showed normal neurodevelopment, including independent walking, language, and social interaction. This case expands the phenotypic spectrum of MTCD and suggests a favorable outcome when MTCD is isolated and genetic investigations are negative. Recognition on fetal imaging is essential for prenatal counseling and postnatal management.

title: Molecular Evolution of Human Coronavirus 229E in Russia
abstract: Human coronavirus 229E (hCoV-229E) is an endemic alphacoronavirus that causes mild to moderate respiratory infections in humans. Despite its long-term circulation in the human population, the genetic diversity and evolutionary dynamics of hCoV-229E remain insufficiently studied, especially in Russia. The aim of this study was to analyze the genetic diversity and molecular characteristics of hCoV-229E strains circulating in Russia from 2017 to 2025. A total of 69,053 nasopharyngeal swabs from hospitalized patients with symptoms of acute respiratory viral infections, mainly from Saint Petersburg, were analyzed. Respiratory pathogens were identified by multiplex RT-PCR. Whole-genome sequencing was performed on selected hCoV-229E-positive samples. Phylogenetic analysis was carried out using the maximum likelihood method, and amino acid substitutions in the S protein were analyzed. Potential N-linked glycosylation sites were predicted using NetNGlyc. hCoV-229E circulated during all eight epidemic seasons, with a pronounced spring peak; its proportion among acute respiratory viral infections ranged from 0.1% to 11%. The most common coinfections were combinations with SARS-CoV-2 (144 cases), human respiratory syncytial virus hRSV (62), and human rhinovirus hRV (48). Based on the whole-genome tree topology, we propose two novel genotypes, 7 and 8 (Bootstrap >70%), with genotype 8 further differentiating into sublineages 8a and 8b. Phylogenetic analysis demonstrated that all contemporary Russian isolates are assigned to these two genotypes. A total of 137 Russian whole-genome sequences were deposited in the international GenBank database, accounting for 23.22% of all available hCoV-229E genomes. In the receptor-binding domain (RBD), the amino acid substitutions E309D, R312S, and H314R (loop 1) were identified, which are characteristic of Russian genotype 8 isolates. The P358A substitution (loop 2) was found exclusively in three isolates from Saint Petersburg in 2023. Thirty-five potential N-glycosylation sites were predicted, of which 26 were conserved across all strains. At the same time, the N714 glycosylation site in the S2 subunit, present in the reference strain and in the 1989 isolate, was lost in all modern viruses. This study provides a comprehensive characterization of the circulation and evolution of hCoV-229E in Russia, demonstrating a shift in dominant genotypes, the formation of regional phylogenetic clades with unique molecular markers, and changes in the glycosylation profile. The results emphasize the need for continuous genomic monitoring of endemic coronaviruses for the timely detection of new genetic variants.

title_zh: 俄罗斯人类冠状病毒 229E 分子 进化
source_body_en: Human coronavirus 229E (hCoV-229E) is an endemic alphacoronavirus that causes mild to moderate respiratory infections in humans. Despite its long-term circulation in the human population, the genetic diversity and evolutionary dynamics of hCoV-229E remain insufficiently studied, especially in Russia. The aim of this study was to analyze the genetic diversity and molecular characteristics of hCoV-229E strains circulating in Russia from 2017 to 2025. A total of 69,053 nasopharyngeal swabs from hospitalized patients with symptoms of acute respiratory viral infections, mainly from Saint Petersburg, were analyzed. Respiratory pathogens were identified by multiplex RT-PCR. Whole-genome sequencing was performed on selected hCoV-229E-positive samples. Phylogenetic analysis was carried out using the maximum likelihood method, and amino acid substitutions in the S protein were analyzed. Potential N-linked glycosylation sites were predicted using NetNGlyc. hCoV-229E circulated during all eight epidemic seasons, with a pronounced spring peak; its proportion among acute respiratory viral infections ranged from 0.1% to 11%. The most common coinfections were combinations with SARS-CoV-2 (144 cases), human respiratory syncytial virus hRSV (62), and human rhinovirus hRV (48). Based on the whole-genome tree topology, we propose two novel genotypes, 7 and 8 (Bootstrap >70%), with genotype 8 further differentiating into sublineages 8a and 8b. Phylogenetic analysis demonstrated that all contemporary Russian isolates are assigned to these two genotypes. A total of 137 Russian whole-genome sequences were deposited in the international GenBank database, accounting for 23.22% of all available hCoV-229E genomes. In the receptor-binding domain (RBD), the amino acid substitutions E309D, R312S, and H314R (loop 1) were identified, which are characteristic of Russian genotype 8 isolates. The P358A substitution (loop 2) was found exclusively in three isolates from Saint Petersburg in 2023. Thirty-five potential N-glycosylation sites were predicted, of which 26 were conserved across all strains. At the same time, the N714 glycosylation site in the S2 subunit, present in the reference strain and in the 1989 isolate, was lost in all modern viruses. This study provides a comprehensive characterization of the circulation and evolution of hCoV-229E in Russia, demonstrating a shift in dominant genotypes, the formation of regional phylogenetic clades with unique molecular markers, and changes in the glycosylation profile. The results emphasize the need for continuous genomic monitoring of endemic coronaviruses for the timely detection of new genetic variants.
abstract_zh: 人类冠状病毒 229E (hCoV-229E) 是一种地方性 α 冠状病毒,可引起人类轻度至中度呼吸道感染。尽管它在人群中长期传播,但 hCoV-229E 的遗传多样性和进化动力学仍然没有得到充分研究,特别是在俄罗斯。本研究的目的是分析 2017 年至 2025 年在俄罗斯传播的 hCoV-229E 病毒株的遗传多样性和分子特征。分析了主要来自圣彼得堡的有急性呼吸道病毒感染症状的住院患者的 69,053 份鼻咽拭子。通过多重 RT-PCR 鉴定呼吸道病原体。对选定的 hCoV-229E 阳性样本进行全 基因组 测序。采用最大似然法进行系统发育分析,分析S蛋白中的氨基酸取代情况。使用 NetNGlyc 预测潜在的 N 连接糖基化位点。hCoV-229E 在所有八个流行季节都有传播,其中春季高峰明显;其在急性呼吸道病毒感染中所占的比例为0.1%至11%。最常见的合并感染是与 SARS-CoV-2(144 例)、人 呼吸道合胞病毒 hRSV(62 例)和人鼻病毒 hRV(48 例)的组合。基于整个 基因组 树拓扑,我们提出了两种新的基因型 7 和 8(Bootstrap > 70%),其中基因型 8 进一步分化为亚系 8a 和 8b。系统发育分析表明,所有当代俄罗斯分离株都属于这两种基因型。国际GenBank数据库中共有137个俄罗斯基因组全序列,占所有可用hCoV-229E 基因组的23.22%。在受体结合域 (RBD) 中,鉴定出氨基酸取代 E309D、R312S 和 H314R(环 1),这是俄罗斯基因型 8 分离株的特征。2023 年,仅在来自圣彼得堡的三个分离株中发现了 P358A 取代(环 2)。预测了 35 个潜在的 N-糖基化位点,其中 26 个在所有菌株中都是保守的。与此同时,参考毒株和 1989 年分离株中存在的 S2 亚基中的 N714 糖基化位点在所有现代病毒中都丢失了。这项研究提供了 hCoV-229E 在俄罗斯的循环和 进化 的全面特征,证明了显性基因型的转变、具有独特分子标记的区域系统发育分支的形成以及糖基化谱的变化。结果强调需要对地方性冠状病毒进行持续的基因组监测,以便及时检测新的遗传变异。

title: Viral replacement or proportional change? Respiratory surveillance as RSV prevention expands in Latin America
abstract: Maternal immunisation with RSVpreF and infant immunisation with the long-acting monoclonal antibodies nirsevimab and clesrovimab are reshaping prevention of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) disease. Trials showed that RSVpreF reduced severe RSV-associated lower respiratory tract illness and that both antibodies reduced RSV-associated hospitalisations in infants.1–3 As RSV disease declines, however, a larger share of remaining respiratory admissions may test positive for other viruses. Distinguishing that proportional change from a true increase in their incidence is an urgent surveillance question for Latin America.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the need to understand how the expansion of RSV prevention strategies is affecting the epidemiology of respiratory infections, particularly in Latin America, where surveillance systems are adapting to monitor changes in viral patterns.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study is based on observational data from respiratory surveillance in Latin America, focusing on the impact of RSV prevention measures on the incidence of other respiratory viruses during the study period.
analysis.methods: The methods involve analyzing surveillance data to assess changes in the proportion of respiratory admissions testing positive for RSV and other viruses, with an emphasis on identifying whether these changes reflect viral replacement or proportional shifts in disease burden.
analysis.main_results: Trials demonstrated that RSVpreF reduced severe RSV-associated lower respiratory tract illness, and both nirsevimab and clesrovimab decreased RSV-associated hospitalisations in infants. As RSV disease declines, a larger proportion of remaining respiratory admissions may be attributed to other viruses.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that distinguishing between proportional change and true increase in the incidence of other viruses is critical for accurate surveillance, highlighting a novel challenge in the context of expanding RSV prevention efforts.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings inform the need for enhanced surveillance systems to accurately track the impact of RSV prevention strategies on the broader respiratory disease landscape, particularly in regions where such measures are being implemented.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on observational data, which may not account for all confounding factors, and the evidence is moderate due to the absence of direct comparative analysis with other viruses.

analysis.summary_en: This study explores the epidemiological impact of expanding RSV prevention strategies in Latin America, focusing on how they may influence the proportion of respiratory admissions attributed to other viruses. It highlights the need for improved surveillance to differentiate between proportional changes and true increases in viral incidence. The findings suggest that as RSV disease declines, other respiratory viruses may become more prominent, necessitating updated monitoring approaches. The study is based on observational data from respiratory surveillance, which provides moderate evidence due to the lack of direct comparative analysis. The results emphasize the importance of accurate data interpretation in the context of evolving prevention measures. The research underscores the urgency of refining surveillance systems to address the changing dynamics of respiratory infections in the region.
