title: Population attributable mortality associated with respiratory viruses in Ontario, Canada: a population-based ecological analysis
abstract: Abstract Background Respiratory viruses are major contributors to population mortality, but cause-of-death coding undercounts their impact. Ecological regression models linking viral circulation to mortality fluctuations can address this limitation. Aim To estimate the population attributable fraction (PAF) of mortality associated with influenza A and B, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), and SARS-CoV-2 in Ontario, Canada (1993–2025), and to characterize temporal changes in virus-attributable mortality across the pandemic transition. Methods We analysed monthly all-cause mortality data with laboratory surveillance indicators for influenza A, B, RSV, and SARS-CoV-2. Negative binomial models with secular trends, Fourier seasonal terms, and population offsets were fit for pre-pandemic (January 1993–February 2020) and combined pandemic (March 2020–February 2025) periods. PAFs were derived from counterfactual predictions setting viral coefficients to zero. Sensitivity analyses examined temporal stratification of the pandemic period (Public Health Emergency of International Concern [PHEIC] period: March 2020–April 2023; post-PHEIC: May 2023–February 2025), exclusion of the early pandemic period (March–June 2020), and models without Fourier seasonal adjustment. Wald tests compared coefficients across specifications. Results Pre-pandemic, influenza A accounted for 1.8% (95% CI 1.4–2.3%) of mortality; influenza B showed no detectable impact. RSV demonstrated inverse associations in seasonally adjusted models but positive associations (PAF 1.9%, 95% CI 1.3–2.4%) without seasonal adjustment. Over the combined pandemic period (March 2020–February 2025; n=60 months), amid elevated baseline mortality (IRR 1.050, P=0.027), SARS-CoV-2 accounted for 6.1% (95% CI 4.2–8.0%) of deaths, approximately 4-fold the pre-pandemic influenza A burden, despite widespread vaccination and antiviral availability. Model-estimated SARS-CoV-2-attributable deaths closely matched reported COVID-19 deaths from Public Health Ontario over the same period. Temporal stratification identified a significant increase in SARS-CoV-2-attributable mortality in the post-PHEIC period (PAF 9.8%, 95% CI 1.1–17.7%; p=0.027), while post-PHEIC influenza A and B attributable fractions did not differ significantly from pre-pandemic baselines. Excluding March-June 2020 yielded a conservative SARS-CoV-2 PAF of 5.7% (95% CI 3.3–8.1%), confirming robustness of primary estimates. Meta-analyses showed substantial heterogeneity for influenza A (I2=92.8%) and RSV (I2=89.1%) across modeling approaches, but minimal heterogeneity for SARS-CoV-2 (I2=5.5%). Conclusion SARS-CoV-2 was associated with a 3–4-fold higher population mortality burden than seasonal influenza A despite available countermeasures. Post-PHEIC data suggest that the burden of respiratory virus mortality, including for influenza, has not returned to pre-pandemic levels, highlighting the continued importance of respiratory virus prevention strategies. Estimates for influenza A and RSV were sensitive to seasonal adjustment, highlighting the importance of modelling choices when quantifying virus-attributable mortality.

The study aimed to estimate the population attributable fraction (PAF) of mortality associated with influenza A and B, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), and SARS-CoV-2 in Ontario, Canada (1993–2025), and to characterize temporal changes in virus-attributable mortality across the pandemic transition.
analysis.study_design_and_population: An ecological regression analysis was conducted using monthly all-cause mortality data and laboratory surveillance indicators for influenza A, B, RSV, and SARS-CoV-2 in Ontario, Canada, from January 1993 to February 2025. The study included 60 months of data during the combined pandemic period.
analysis.methods: Negative binomial models with secular trends, Fourier seasonal terms, and population offsets were fit for pre-pandemic and combined pandemic periods. Sensitivity analyses examined temporal stratification of the pandemic period and exclusion of the early pandemic period.
analysis.main_results: Pre-pandemic, influenza A accounted for 1.8% (95% CI 1.4–2.3%) of mortality; influenza B showed no detectable impact. RSV demonstrated inverse associations in seasonally adjusted models but positive associations (PAF 1.9%, 95% CI 1.3–2.4%) without seasonal adjustment. Over the combined pandemic period, SARS-CoV-2 accounted for 6.1% (95% CI 4.2–8.0%) of deaths, approximately 4-fold the pre-pandemic influenza A burden. Excluding March-June 2020 yielded a conservative SARS-CoV-2 PAF of 5.7% (95% CI 3.3–8.1%).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that SARS-CoV-2 was associated with a 3–4-fold higher population mortality burden than seasonal influenza A despite available countermeasures. The study highlights the importance of modeling choices when quantifying virus-attributable mortality.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that the burden of respiratory virus mortality, including for influenza, has not returned to pre-pandemic levels, highlighting the continued importance of respiratory virus prevention strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's estimates for influenza A and RSV were sensitive to seasonal adjustment, which may affect the interpretation of virus-attributable mortality. The evidence is moderate, as the results are based on ecological regression models and sensitivity analyses.

analysis.summary_en: This study estimates the population attributable fraction (PAF) of mortality associated with respiratory viruses in Ontario, Canada, from 1993 to 2025. It focuses on influenza A and B, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), and SARS-CoV-2. The research highlights that despite countermeasures, SARS-CoV-2 was associated with a 3–4-fold higher mortality burden than seasonal influenza A. The study also shows that RSV's impact is sensitive to seasonal adjustment, and the burden of respiratory virus mortality has not returned to pre-pandemic levels. The findings emphasize the importance of continued prevention strategies for respiratory viruses. The evidence is moderate due to the use of ecological regression models and sensitivity analyses.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 呼吸道病毒是 死亡率 群体的主要贡献者,但死因编码低估了其影响。该研究旨在估计加拿大安大略省(1993-2025 年)与甲型和乙型流感、呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 和 SARS-CoV-2 相关的 死亡率 的人群归因分数 (PAF),并描述大流行过渡期间病毒归因 死亡率 的时间变化。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 使用 1993 年 1 月至 2025 年 2 月加拿大安大略省甲型、乙型、RSV 和 SARS-CoV-2 流感的每月全因 死亡率 数据和实验室 监测 指标进行生态回归分析。该研究包括合并大流行期间 60 个月的数据。
elements_zh.methods: 具有长期趋势、傅里叶季节性项和人口抵消的负二项式模型适合大流行前和大流行期间。敏感性分析检查了大流行时期的时间分层并排除了早期大流行时期。
elements_zh.main_results: 大流行前,甲型流感占 死亡率 的 1.8%(95% CI 1.4-2.3%);乙型流感没有显示出可检测到的影响。RSV 在经季节性调整的模型中表现出负相关,但在未经季节调整的情况下呈正相关(PAF 1.9%,95% CI 1.3–2.4%)。在整个大流行期间,SARS-CoV-2 占死亡人数的 6.1%(95% CI 4.2-8.0%),大约是大流行前甲型流感负担的 4 倍。排除 2020 年 3 月至 6 月,保守的 SARS-CoV-2 PAF 为 5.7%(95% CI 3.3-8.1%)。

elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究对甲型流感和 RSV 的估计对季节性调整很敏感,这可能会影响病毒归因 死亡率 的解释。证据是中等的,因为结果是基于生态回归模型和敏感性分析。

title_zh: 加拿大安大略省与呼吸道病毒相关的人群归因 死亡率:基于人群的生态分析
source_body_en: Abstract Background Respiratory viruses are major contributors to population mortality, but cause-of-death coding undercounts their impact. Ecological regression models linking viral circulation to mortality fluctuations can address this limitation. Aim To estimate the population attributable fraction (PAF) of mortality associated with influenza A and B, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), and SARS-CoV-2 in Ontario, Canada (1993–2025), and to characterize temporal changes in virus-attributable mortality across the pandemic transition. Methods We analysed monthly all-cause mortality data with laboratory surveillance indicators for influenza A, B, RSV, and SARS-CoV-2. Negative binomial models with secular trends, Fourier seasonal terms, and population offsets were fit for pre-pandemic (January 1993–February 2020) and combined pandemic (March 2020–February 2025) periods. PAFs were derived from counterfactual predictions setting viral coefficients to zero. Sensitivity analyses examined temporal stratification of the pandemic period (Public Health Emergency of International Concern [PHEIC] period: March 2020–April 2023; post-PHEIC: May 2023–February 2025), exclusion of the early pandemic period (March–June 2020), and models without Fourier seasonal adjustment. Wald tests compared coefficients across specifications. Results Pre-pandemic, influenza A accounted for 1.8% (95% CI 1.4–2.3%) of mortality; influenza B showed no detectable impact. RSV demonstrated inverse associations in seasonally adjusted models but positive associations (PAF 1.9%, 95% CI 1.3–2.4%) without seasonal adjustment. Over the combined pandemic period (March 2020–February 2025; n=60 months), amid elevated baseline mortality (IRR 1.050, P=0.027), SARS-CoV-2 accounted for 6.1% (95% CI 4.2–8.0%) of deaths, approximately 4-fold the pre-pandemic influenza A burden, despite widespread vaccination and antiviral availability. Model-estimated SARS-CoV-2-attributable deaths closely matched reported COVID-19 deaths from Public Health Ontario over the same period. Temporal stratification identified a significant increase in SARS-CoV-2-attributable mortality in the post-PHEIC period (PAF 9.8%, 95% CI 1.1–17.7%; p=0.027), while post-PHEIC influenza A and B attributable fractions did not differ significantly from pre-pandemic baselines. Excluding March-June 2020 yielded a conservative SARS-CoV-2 PAF of 5.7% (95% CI 3.3–8.1%), confirming robustness of primary estimates. Meta-analyses showed substantial heterogeneity for influenza A (I2=92.8%) and RSV (I2=89.1%) across modeling approaches, but minimal heterogeneity for SARS-CoV-2 (I2=5.5%). Conclusion SARS-CoV-2 was associated with a 3–4-fold higher population mortality burden than seasonal influenza A despite available countermeasures. Post-PHEIC data suggest that the burden of respiratory virus mortality, including for influenza, has not returned to pre-pandemic levels, highlighting the continued importance of respiratory virus prevention strategies. Estimates for influenza A and RSV were sensitive to seasonal adjustment, highlighting the importance of modelling choices when quantifying virus-attributable mortality.
abstract_zh: 摘要 背景 呼吸道病毒是 死亡率 群体的主要贡献者,但死因编码低估了其影响。将病毒循环与 死亡率 波动联系起来的生态回归模型可以解决这一限制。目的 估计加拿大安大略省(1993-2025 年)与甲型和乙型流感、呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 和 SARS-CoV-2 相关的 死亡率 的人群归因分数 (PAF),并描述大流行过渡期间病毒归因 死亡率 的时间变化。方法 我们使用甲型、乙型、RSV 和 SARS-CoV-2 流感实验室 监测 指标分析了每月全因 死亡率 数据。具有长期趋势、傅里叶季节性项和人口偏移的负二项式模型适合大流行前(1993年1月至2020年2月)和大流行合并时期(2020年3月至2025年2月)。PAF 源自将病毒系数设置为零的反事实预测。敏感性分析检查了大流行期间的时间分层(国际关注的突发公共卫生事件 [PHEIC] 期间:2020 年 3 月至 2023 年 4 月;PHEIC 后:2023 年 5 月至 2025 年 2 月),排除了大流行早期(2020 年 3 月至 6 月),以及没有傅里叶季节调整的模型。Wald 测试比较了不同规格的系数。结果 大流行前,甲型流感占 死亡率 的 1.8%(95% CI 1.4–2.3%);乙型流感没有显示出可检测到的影响。RSV 在经季节性调整的模型中表现出负相关,但在未经季节调整的情况下呈正相关(PAF 1.9%,95% CI 1.3–2.4%)。在整个大流行期间(2020年3月至2025年2月;n=60个月),在基线死亡率升高(IRR 1.050,P=0.027)的情况下,SARS-CoV-2占死亡人数的6.1%(95% CI 4.2-8.0%),大约是大流行前甲型流感负担的4倍,尽管疫苗接种和抗病毒药物 可用性。模型估计的 SARS-CoV-2 死亡人数与同期安大略省公共卫生部门报告的 COVID-19 死亡人数非常吻合。时间分层发现,PHEIC 后时期 SARS-CoV-2 归因的 死亡率 显着增加(PAF 9.8%,95% CI 1.1-17.7%;p=0.027),而 PHEIC 后甲型和 B 型流感归因分数与大流行前的基线没有显着差异。排除 2020 年 3 月至 6 月,保守的 SARS-CoV-2 PAF 为 5.7%(95% CI 3.3-8.1%),证实了初步估计的稳健性。荟萃分析显示,不同建模方法中甲型流感 (I2=92.8%) 和 RSV (I2=89.1%) 存在显着异质性,但 SARS-CoV-2 异质性极小 (I2=5.5%)。结论 尽管有可用的对策,但与季节性甲型流感相比,SARS-CoV-2 造成的人群 死亡率 负担高出 3-4 倍。PHEIC 后的数据表明,呼吸道病毒 死亡率(包括流感病毒)的负担尚未恢复到大流行前的水平,这凸显了呼吸道病毒预防策略的持续重要性。甲型流感和 RSV 的估计对季节性调整敏感,突出了在量化病毒归因 死亡率 时建模选择的重要性。

title: An endpoint multiplex PCR/RT-PCR for detection of viral agents of bovine respiratory disease.
abstract: Abstract Bovine respiratory disease (BRD) is a clinicopathological syndrome caused by complex interactions among host and environmental factors, viruses and bacteria. The multi-agent BRD etiology makes laboratory diagnosis challenging, as various pathogens should be investigated for an accurate results. Herein, we describe an endpoint multiplex PCR/RT-PCR for detection of major BRD-associated viruses: bovine herpesvirus 1 (BoAHV-1), bovine pestiviruses (BVDV-1, BVDV-2, HoBiPeV), bovine parainfluenza virus 3 (BPIV-3), bovine respiratory syncytial virus (BRSV) and bovine coronavirus (BCoV). We designed high-coverage and target-specific primers to be properly combined in the multiplex assay. Following standardization of individual reactions, the multiplex PCR/RT-PCR was optimized for reaction conditions and mix composition. The amplicons of the five targets were easily differentiated in agarose gel: 121 bp (BPIV-3), 157 bp (BoAHV-1), 204 bp (pestiviruses), 282 bp (BRSV) and 323 bp (BCoV). The limits of detection (LoDs) of our multiplex were 38 TCID 50 (BoAHV-1 and BPIV-3), 16 TCID 50 (pestiviruses), 13 TCID 50 (BRSV) and a 10 − 2 dilution of a pool of five BCoV positive samples. No amplification of the main bacteria ( Pasteurella multocida ; Mannheimia haemolytica and Histophilus somni ) potentially involved in BRD was observed. Finally, 289 respiratory specimens from animals with respiratory/nasal signs were evaluated by individual and multiplex PCR/RT-PCR tests to assess the diagnostic performance of the assay. Both tests resulted in 14.8% positive samples (43/289) being 19 for BPIV-3 (19/43), ten for BCoV (10/43), seven for BRSV (7/43), six for BoAHV-1 (6/43) and one for pestiviruses (1/43). Overall, our multiplex PCR/RT-PCR assay represents an alternative for an easier, faster and more practical laboratory diagnosis of viruses associated with BRD.

title: Pregnancy and vaccine acceptance: A global review of hesitancy drivers and strategies for maternal immunization
abstract: During pregnancy, women are more susceptible to viral infections such as COVID-19, influenza, pertussis, Tdap, and respiratory syncytial virus due to changes in the physiological state and immune responses. Various research illustrates that vaccination confers strong protection against severe diseases and complications. The aim of this research is to identify the factors that influence vaccine hesitancy (VH) and proffer solutions that can improve maternal immunization. This review used a narrative synthesis approach to examine maternal vaccine acceptance and hesitancy. Literature was retrieved from sources such as PubMed, Scopus, and Google Scholar, and also from global health agencies [Centers for Disease Control (CDC), United Nations International Children’s Emergency Fund, World Health Organization (WHO), and National Health Services] from 2015 to 2025. Major data on prevalence, determinants, and interventions were extracted and synthesized thematically to identify global trends, equity gaps, and integrated strategies for improving maternal vaccine uptake. Unvaccinated women who contract SARS-COV-2 or influenza face a higher risk of severe illness, hospitalization, complications, and mortality in comparison to those vaccinated. One study reported vaccine effectiveness against severe COVID-19 complications at 48% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 22-65) with a full regimen, rising to 76% (95% CI: 47-89) after a booster. Influenza vaccination during pregnancy reduced confirmed infant cases by 63% and prevented roughly one-third of febrile respiratory illness in mothers and infants. Maternal immunization is vital for protecting mothers and infants, yet VH persists worldwide. Safety concerns, misinformation, low perceived risk, and institutional distrust hinder uptake, especially among vulnerable groups. Strengthening provider communication, integrating vaccines into antenatal care, and culturally tailored interventions are essential to ensure equitable access and improved outcomes. This review goes beyond summarizing hesitancy drivers by explicitly examining the normative-operational divide in maternal immunization policy, contrasting high-income and low- and middle-income countries (LMIC) contexts to identify implementation gaps and equity challenges.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and its impact on pregnant women, examining factors influencing vaccine hesitancy and strategies for improving maternal immunization. The central question is to identify the drivers of vaccine hesitancy and propose solutions to enhance maternal vaccine uptake.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review employed a narrative synthesis approach to analyze maternal vaccine acceptance and hesitancy. Literature was sourced from PubMed, Scopus, and Google Scholar, as well as global health agencies like the CDC, WHO, and NHS, between 2015 and 2025. Data on prevalence, determinants, and interventions were extracted and synthesized thematically.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Maternal immunization is crucial for protecting both mothers and infants from severe RSV-related complications. Evidence indicates that vaccination significantly reduces the risk of severe illness, hospitalization, and mortality in pregnant women and their infants. The review highlights the importance of addressing safety concerns, misinformation, and institutional distrust to improve vaccine uptake.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: There is limited evidence on the effectiveness of maternal immunization against RSV in specific populations, particularly in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). The review notes gaps in understanding the implementation challenges and equity issues in maternal immunization programs for RSV.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: To enhance maternal immunization against RSV, there is a need for stronger provider communication, integration of vaccines into antenatal care, and culturally tailored interventions. Additionally, further research is required to evaluate the effectiveness of RSV vaccines in LMICs and to address the barriers to vaccine acceptance in these regions.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the factors influencing vaccine hesitancy (VH) among pregnant women regarding respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and highlights strategies to improve maternal immunization. It emphasizes the importance of RSV vaccination in reducing severe illness, hospitalization, and mortality in both mothers and infants. The study identifies safety concerns, misinformation, and institutional distrust as key barriers to vaccine uptake, particularly among vulnerable groups. The review advocates for enhanced provider communication, integration of vaccines into antenatal care, and culturally appropriate interventions to ensure equitable access. However, it notes a lack of evidence on RSV vaccine effectiveness in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) and calls for further research to address implementation gaps and equity challenges in maternal immunization programs.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述重点关注 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 及其对孕妇的影响,研究影响 疫苗 犹豫的因素以及改善孕产妇免疫的策略。核心问题是确定 疫苗 犹豫的驱动因素,并提出提高母亲对 疫苗 吸收的解决方案。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述采用叙述综合方法来分析母亲 疫苗 的接受和犹豫。文献来源于 2015 年至 2025 年期间的 PubMed、Scopus 和 Google Scholar,以及 CDC、WHO 和 NHS 等全球卫生机构。按主题提取和综合了 患病率、决定因素和干预措施的数据。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 孕产妇免疫对于保护母亲和婴儿免受严重 RSV 相关并发症至关重要。有证据表明,疫苗接种 显着降低孕妇及其婴儿患严重疾病、住院和 死亡率 的风险。该审查强调了解决安全问题、错误信息和机构不信任的重要性,以提高 疫苗 的采用率。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 关于特定人群(特别是低收入和中等收入国家 (LMIC))孕产妇 RSV 免疫接种的有效性的证据有限。该审查指出了在了解 RSV 孕产妇免疫计划的实施挑战和公平问题方面存在的差距。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 为了加强孕产妇对 RSV 的免疫,需要加强提供者沟通、将 疫苗 纳入产前护理以及根据文化定制干预措施。此外,还需要进一步研究来评估 RSV 疫苗 在中低收入国家中的有效性,并解决这些地区接受 疫苗 的障碍。

abstract_zh: 怀孕期间,女性由于生理状态和免疫应答的变化,更容易受到COVID-19、流感、百日咳、Tdap、呼吸道合胞病毒等病毒感染。各种研究表明,疫苗接种 对严重疾病和并发症具有强大的保护作用。本研究的目的是确定影响 疫苗 犹豫 (VH) 的因素,并提供可以改善母亲免疫的解决方案。本综述使用叙述综合方法来检查母亲 疫苗 的接受和犹豫。文献检索自 2015 年至 2025 年期间的 PubMed、Scopus 和 Google Scholar 等来源以及全球卫生机构 [疾病控制中心 (CDC)、联合国国际儿童紧急基金、世界卫生组织 (WHO) 和国家卫生服务部门]。提取并按主题合成有关 患病率、决定因素和干预措施的主要数据,以确定全球趋势、公平差距和改善孕产妇状况的综合策略疫苗 吸收。与接种疫苗的女性相比,感染 SARS-COV-2 或流感的未接种疫苗的女性面临严重疾病、住院、并发症和 死亡率 的风险更高。一项研究报告称,疫苗 在完整治疗方案中对严重 COVID-19 并发症的有效性为 48%(95% 置信区间 [CI]:22-65),在加强治疗后升至 76%(95% CI:47-89)。怀孕期间感染 疫苗接种 流感可使婴儿确诊病例减少 63%,并预防母亲和婴儿约三分之一的发热呼吸道疾病。孕产妇免疫对于保护母亲和婴儿至关重要,但 VH 在世界范围内持续存在。安全担忧、错误信息、低感知风险和机构不信任阻碍了人们的接受,尤其是在弱势群体中。加强提供者沟通、将 疫苗 纳入产前护理以及根据文化量身定制的干预措施对于确保公平获取和改善结果至关重要。本次审查不仅总结了犹豫不决的因素,还明确审查了孕产妇免疫政策中的规范与操作分歧,对比高收入和低收入和中等收入国家(LMIC)的情况,以确定实施差距和公平挑战。

analysis_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述重点关注 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 及其对孕妇的影响,研究影响 疫苗 犹豫的因素以及改善孕产妇免疫的策略。核心问题是确定 疫苗 犹豫的驱动因素,并提出提高母亲对 疫苗 吸收的解决方案。
analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述采用叙述综合方法来分析母亲 疫苗 的接受和犹豫。文献来源于 2015 年至 2025 年期间的 PubMed、Scopus 和 Google Scholar,以及 CDC、WHO 和 NHS 等全球卫生机构。按主题提取和综合了 患病率、决定因素和干预措施的数据。
analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 孕产妇免疫对于保护母亲和婴儿免受严重 RSV 相关并发症至关重要。有证据表明,疫苗接种 显着降低孕妇及其婴儿患严重疾病、住院和 死亡率 的风险。该审查强调了解决安全问题、错误信息和机构不信任的重要性,以提高 疫苗 的采用率。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 关于特定人群(特别是低收入和中等收入国家 (LMIC))孕产妇 RSV 免疫接种的有效性的证据有限。该审查指出了在了解 RSV 孕产妇免疫计划的实施挑战和公平问题方面存在的差距。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 为了加强孕产妇对 RSV 的免疫,需要加强提供者沟通、将 疫苗 纳入产前护理以及根据文化定制干预措施。此外,还需要进一步研究来评估 RSV 疫苗 在中低收入国家中的有效性,并解决这些地区接受 疫苗 的障碍。

title: Fever Without a Source in Children Under 3 Years of Age: The Role of Respiratory Viruses
abstract: Objective: The aim of this study was to determine the role of respiratory viruses during the disease by evaluating patients who presented with fever of unknown origin during their hospitalization.Materials and Methods: Data from 168 patients aged under 3 years were retrospectively analyzed in terms of demographic, clinical, laboratory, and radiological findings.Results: Median age was 11 (1-35) months, and 48.2% were female. Parainfluenza, rhinovirus, and adenovirus were detected more frequently in patients with a single agent. The duration of fever was longer in the presence of multiple viruses (p = 0.01). There was no statistical difference between the duration of fever and the type of virus. Human bocavirus was the most common type detected in patients presenting with febrile convulsions. C-reactive protein levels were high in 70.2% of patients. Antibiotics were started in 79.2% of patients at the time of admission. The median length of hospital stay was 8 days (2-35 days), and this period was longer when the causative agents were respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and enterovirus. Intensive care unit requirement was 15.4%, mainly in patients diagnosed with RSV.Conclusion: Minimally invasive treatment of respiratory viral infections that begin with fever alone in the clinic offers opportunities for rational antibiotic and health care use.

analysis.study_design_and_population: Data from 168 patients aged under 3 years were retrospectively analyzed in terms of demographic, clinical, laboratory, and radiological findings. The median age was 11 (1-35) months, and 48.2% were female. The median length of hospital stay was 8 days (2-35 days), and this period was longer when the causative agents were respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and enterovirus.
analysis.methods: The study involved retrospective analysis of patient data, including demographic, clinical, laboratory, and radiological findings. Patients were evaluated for the presence of respiratory viruses, and the duration of fever was compared between those with single-agent and multiple-virus infections.
analysis.main_results: Parainfluenza, rhinovirus, and adenovirus were detected more frequently in patients with a single agent. analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that the presence of multiple viruses was associated with prolonged fever. They concluded that minimally invasive treatment of respiratory viral infections that begin with fever alone in the clinic offers opportunities for rational antibiotic and health care use.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that identifying the causative agents of fever without a source in children can inform more targeted antibiotic use and improve health care resource allocation.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on retrospective data, which may introduce bias. The evidence is moderate as it relies on observational findings without experimental validation.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the role of respiratory viruses in children under 3 years with fever of unknown origin. It analyzed data from 168 patients, revealing that parainfluenza, rhinovirus, and adenovirus were more common in single-agent infections, while multiple viruses were linked to longer fever duration. C-reactive protein levels were elevated in 70.2% of patients, and antibiotics were initiated in 79.2%. The authors concluded that targeted treatment of respiratory viral infections could optimize antibiotic use and health care management. The study's limitations include its retrospective design, which may affect the reliability of findings.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在通过评估住院期间出现不明原因发烧的患者来确定呼吸道病毒在疾病期间的作用。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 对 168 名 3 岁以下患者的数据进行了人口统计学、临床、实验室和放射学检查结果的回顾性分析。中位年龄为 11 (1-35) 个月,其中 48.2% 为女性。中位住院时间为8天(2-35天),当病原体为呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)和肠道病毒时,住院时间更长。
elements_zh.methods: 该研究涉及对患者数据的回顾性分析,包括人口统计、临床、实验室和放射学结果。对患者是否存在呼吸道病毒进行了评估,并比较了单药感染者和多病毒感染者的发热持续时间。
elements_zh.main_results: 使用单一药物的患者中更容易检测到副流感、鼻病毒和腺病毒。存在多种病毒时发烧持续时间更长 (p = 0.01)。70.2% 的患者 C 反应蛋白水平较高。79.2%的患者在入院时开始使用抗生素。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,多种病毒的存在与长时间发烧有关。他们的结论是,在临床上仅以发烧开始的呼吸道病毒感染的微创 治疗 为合理使用抗生素和医疗保健提供了机会。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,识别儿童无源发烧的病原体可以为更有针对性的抗生素使用提供信息,并改善医疗保健资源分配。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究基于回顾性数据,可能会引入偏差。证据是温和的,因为它依赖于未经实验验证的观察结果。

analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究基于回顾性数据,可能会引入偏差。证据是温和的,因为它依赖于未经实验验证的观察结果。

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to explore the potential role of asymptomatic toxigenic Clostridioides difficile colonization as a marker of gut dysbiosis and its association with RSV bronchiolitis, highlighting the need to understand the gut-lung axis in pediatric respiratory infections.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was a clinical investigation focusing on RSV bronchiolitis, examining the relationship between gut dysbiosis and respiratory symptoms in pediatric patients.
analysis.methods: The methods involved analyzing clinical data and utilizing assays to assess gut dysbiosis and fecal calprotectin levels in relation to RSV bronchiolitis, with an emphasis on the gut-lung axis.
analysis.main_results: The study found that asymptomatic toxigenic Clostridioides difficile colonization was associated with gut dysbiosis and was observed in patients with RSV bronchiolitis.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted these findings as suggesting a potential link between gut dysbiosis and RSV bronchiolitis, offering a novel perspective on the gut-lung axis in pediatric respiratory diseases.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings may inform future research on the gut-lung axis and its implications for the diagnosis and management of RSV bronchiolitis in children.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its observational nature and potential confounding factors, but the evidence is grounded in clinical observations and provides moderate confidence in the proposed association.

analysis.summary_en: This abstract presents a study on the potential association between asymptomatic toxigenic Clostridioides difficile colonization and RSV bronchiolitis, emphasizing the gut-lung axis in pediatric respiratory infections. The research explores the role of gut dysbiosis as a marker for RSV-related respiratory conditions, offering a novel perspective on the interplay between gastrointestinal and pulmonary health. The study's findings suggest a possible link between gut microbiota and RSV bronchiolitis, which could inform future research and clinical approaches. However, the observational design and potential confounding factors limit the confidence in the conclusions, indicating moderate evidence strength. The implications of this research may contribute to understanding the broader context of respiratory infections in children and the importance of considering gut health in their management.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究是一项针对 RSV 毛细支气管炎 的临床研究,旨在研究儿科患者肠道菌群失调与呼吸道症状之间的关系。
elements_zh.methods: 这些方法包括分析临床数据并利用测定来评估与 RSV 毛细支气管炎 相关的肠道菌群失调和粪便钙卫蛋白水平,重点是肠肺轴。
elements_zh.main_results: 研究发现,无症状产毒艰难梭菌定植与肠道菌群失调相关,并在 RSV 毛细支气管炎 患者中观察到。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为表明肠道菌群失调与 RSV 毛细支气管炎 之间存在潜在联系,为儿科呼吸系统疾病的肠肺轴提供了新的视角。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可能为未来关于肠肺轴的研究及其对 诊断 和儿童 RSV 毛细支气管炎 管理的影响提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究受到其观察性质和潜在混杂因素的限制,但证据基于临床观察,并对拟议的关联提供了适度的信心。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在探讨无症状产毒艰难梭菌定植作为肠道菌群失调标志物的潜在作用及其与 RSV 毛细支气管炎 的关联,强调了解儿科呼吸道感染中肠肺轴的必要性。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究是一项针对 RSV 毛细支气管炎 的临床研究,旨在研究儿科患者肠道菌群失调与呼吸道症状之间的关系。
analysis_zh.methods: 这些方法包括分析临床数据并利用测定来评估与 RSV 毛细支气管炎 相关的肠道菌群失调和粪便钙卫蛋白水平,重点是肠肺轴。

title: Human type 3 parainfluenza virus activates NK cells after in vitro stimulation of peripheral blood mononuclear cells
abstract: Parainfluenza virus (PIV), along with respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), metapneumoviruses, influenza A and B viruses, adenoviruses, etc. plays a significant role in prevalence of acute respiratory viral infections, causing inflammation of upper and lower respiratory tract which may lead to severe bronchitis and pneumonia, especially in young children and immunocompromised adults. Moreover, parainfluenza infection frequently complicates chronic diseases such as asthma and COPD. However, there is currently no specific prophylaxis against parainfluenza, although vaccine development is actively underway worldwide. Smorodintsev Department of Virology and Immunology at the Institute of Experimental Medicine is developing a domestic T cell vaccine against RSV, metapneumovirus, and human PIV type 3 (PIV3). This vaccine is based on a live attenuated influenza vaccine vector. The study revealed high IFNγ expression in cells with the CD3- phenotype. Eleven healthy volunteers aged 23 to 43 years participated in this trial. Their peripheral blood mononuclear cells were stimulated with H1N1, H3N2, RSV, and PIV3 influenza viruses using a panel of antibodies against CD3, CD8, CD4, CD197, CD45RA, CD56, IFNγ, and TNFα antigens. The study was conducted by means of multicolor flow cytometry. It was found that natural killer cells with the CD3-CD56+ phenotype synthesize significant amounts of interferon-γ when treated by human PIV3, but they do not respond to stimulation by RSV and H1N1 and H3N2 influenza viruses. Furthermore, it was found that NK cells release TNFα when stimulated by PIV3, but they are not polyfunctional. The results of this study are consistent with research published worldwide, and they suggest a unique mechanism of immune response to PIV3, which can be used in development of T cell vaccines against human PIV.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the immune response to human type 3 parainfluenza virus (PIV3) and its potential role in vaccine development, as PIV3 is a significant cause of acute respiratory infections, particularly in vulnerable populations.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved eleven healthy volunteers aged 23 to 43 years, whose peripheral blood mononuclear cells were stimulated with various viruses, including PIV3, to assess immune activation.
analysis.methods: Peripheral blood mononuclear cells were stimulated with H1N1, H3N2, RSV, and PIV3 influenza viruses, and a panel of antibodies against CD3, CD8, CD4, CD197, CD45RA, CD56, IFNγ, and TNFα antigens was used to analyze immune responses via multicolor flow cytometry.
analysis.main_results: The study revealed high IFNγ expression in CD3- phenotype cells when stimulated by PIV3, but not by RSV or influenza viruses. NK cells also released TNFα in response to PIV3, though they were not polyfunctional.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest a unique immune response mechanism to PIV3, which may inform the development of T cell vaccines targeting this virus.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results could contribute to understanding immune mechanisms against PIV3 and support the development of targeted vaccines for respiratory viral infections.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to in vitro observations and a small sample size, but the evidence is consistent with global research and provides a novel insight into immune activation by PIV3.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the immune response to human type 3 parainfluenza virus (PIV3) by stimulating peripheral blood mononuclear cells from healthy volunteers. The results showed that PIV3 activates NK cells, leading to high IFNγ expression and TNFα release, but not polyfunctionality. These findings suggest a unique immune mechanism for PIV3, which may be useful in developing T cell vaccines. The study's in vitro design and small sample size limit its generalizability, but the results align with global research and offer new insights into PIV3's interaction with the immune system.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在调查人类 3 型副流感病毒 (PIV3) 的 免疫应答 及其在 疫苗 发展中的潜在作用,因为 PIV3 是急性呼吸道感染的重要原因,特别是在易感人群中。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究涉及 11 名年龄在 23 岁至 43 岁之间的健康志愿者,他们的外周血单核细胞受到包括 PIV3 在内的各种病毒的刺激,以评估免疫激活。
elements_zh.methods: 用 H1N1、H3N2、RSV 和 PIV3 流感病毒刺激外周血单核细胞,并使用一组针对 CD3、CD8、CD4、CD197、CD45RA、CD56、IFNγ 和 TNFα 抗原的抗体通过多色流式细胞术分析 免疫应答。
elements_zh.main_results: 该研究表明,当受到 PIV3 刺激时,CD3-表型细胞中会出现高 IFNγ 表达,但受到 RSV 或流感病毒刺激时则不会。NK 细胞也响应 PIV3 释放 TNFα,尽管它们不是多功能的。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现表明 PIV3 具有独特的 免疫应答 机制,这可能为针对该病毒的 T 细胞 疫苗 的发育提供信息。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果可能有助于了解针对 PIV3 的免疫机制,并支持开发针对呼吸道病毒感染的靶向 疫苗。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于体外观察和小样本量,但证据与全球研究一致,并为 PIV3 的免疫激活提供了新的见解。

abstract_zh: 副流感病毒(PIV)与呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)、偏肺病毒、甲型和乙型流感病毒、腺病毒等在急性呼吸道病毒感染中起重要作用,引起上下呼吸道炎症,可能导致严重支气管炎和肺炎,特别是在幼儿和免疫功能低下的成人中。此外,副流感感染常常使哮喘和慢性阻塞性肺病等慢性疾病复杂化。然而,尽管 疫苗 的开发正在全球范围内积极进行,但目前尚无针对副流感的具体预防方法。Smorodintsev 实验医学研究所病毒学和免疫学系正在开发一种针对 RSV、偏肺病毒和人类 PIV 3 型 (PIV3) 的国产 T 细胞 疫苗。该 疫苗 基于活减毒流感 疫苗 媒介。该研究揭示了具有CD3-表型的细胞中IFNγ的高表达。11名年龄在23岁至43岁之间的健康志愿者参与了这项试验。使用一组针对 CD3、CD8、CD4、CD197、CD45RA、CD56、IFNγ 和 TNFα 抗原的抗体,用 H1N1、H3N2、RSV 和 PIV3 流感病毒刺激他们的外周血单核细胞。该研究是通过多色流式细胞术进行的。研究发现,具有 CD3-CD56+ 表型的自然杀伤细胞在接受人 PIV3 处理时会合成大量干扰素-γ,但它们对 RSV 以及 H1N1 和 H3N2 流感病毒的刺激没有反应。此外,研究发现,NK 细胞在受到 PIV3 刺激时会释放 TNFα,但它们并不是多功能的。这项研究的结果与世界范围内发表的研究结果一致,并提出了免疫应答针对PIV3的独特机制,可用于开发针对人类PIV的T细胞疫苗。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在调查人类 3 型副流感病毒 (PIV3) 的 免疫应答 及其在 疫苗 发展中的潜在作用,因为 PIV3 是急性呼吸道感染的重要原因,特别是在易感人群中。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究涉及 11 名年龄在 23 岁至 43 岁之间的健康志愿者,他们的外周血单核细胞受到包括 PIV3 在内的各种病毒的刺激,以评估免疫激活。
analysis_zh.methods: 用 H1N1、H3N2、RSV 和 PIV3 流感病毒刺激外周血单核细胞,并使用一组针对 CD3、CD8、CD4、CD197、CD45RA、CD56、IFNγ 和 TNFα 抗原的抗体通过多色流式细胞术分析 免疫应答。
analysis_zh.main_results: 该研究表明,当受到 PIV3 刺激时,CD3-表型细胞中会出现高 IFNγ 表达,但受到 RSV 或流感病毒刺激时则不会。NK 细胞也响应 PIV3 释放 TNFα,尽管它们不是多功能的。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现表明 PIV3 具有独特的 免疫应答 机制,这可能为针对该病毒的 T 细胞 疫苗 的发育提供信息。

analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于体外观察和小样本量,但证据与全球研究一致,并为 PIV3 的免疫激活提供了新的见解。

title: From prophylactic mRNA vaccines against viral infections to therapeutic applications: regulatory science considerations for expanding mRNA platforms
abstract: Conventional non-amplifying messenger RNA (mRNA) and self-amplifying RNA (saRNA) medicines generally share a core linear RNA architecture—including a 5′ cap, untranslated regions, one or more open reading frames, and a poly(A) tail—and are commonly formulated with delivery systems such as lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) to enable transient intracellular expression of a target protein. Prophylactic mRNA vaccines are designed primarily to express infectious-disease antigens and generate protective immune memory, whereas mRNA therapeutics exert pharmacological effects intended to treat disease, suppress recurrence, replace proteins, modulate immunity, or deliver gene-editing enzymes. Thus, even products based on similar mRNA–LNP technology may have different regulatory classifications and evidence requirements according to their intended use and mechanism of action. The clinical and regulatory landscape has expanded beyond the first coronavirus disease 2019 vaccines to include respiratory syncytial virus and influenza mRNA vaccines, an influenza–coronavirus disease 2019 combination vaccine, an authorized saRNA vaccine, personalized cancer immunotherapies, protein-replacement therapies, in vivo cell programming, and gene-editing delivery systems. This review examines which prophylactic-vaccine evidence can support therapeutic development and where product-specific quality, nonclinical, clinical, and lifecycle evidence remains necessary. For prophylactic mRNA vaccines, major regulatory considerations include quality, immunogenicity, preventive efficacy, lot release, and safety surveillance after large-scale vaccination. For mRNA therapeutics, the principal issues include delivery to target tissues, function of the expressed product, repeat-dose safety, biodistribution, off-target risk, long-term follow-up, and patient-specific manufacture and traceability. In particular, although personalized mRNA cancer vaccines are commonly described as vaccines, they are closer in regulatory purpose to therapeutics that act on the basis of each patient’s tumor characteristics than to vaccines that prevent infectious disease. Antigen-selection algorithms, patient-specific sequence design, small-batch and multi-product manufacture, product–patient matching, clinical evaluation of combination strategies, manufacturing delays and analysis populations, and risk-based long-term postauthorization follow-up therefore require explicit regulatory consideration. Platform-level knowledge from prophylactic mRNA vaccine authorization can support therapeutic development, but regulatory questions may vary with each new product type; developers will need to track evolving regulatory instruments across jurisdictions and engage regulatory authorities early.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the need to understand how regulatory science considerations for prophylactic mRNA vaccines can be adapted for therapeutic applications, particularly in the context of expanding mRNA platforms to address viral infections such as respiratory syncytial virus (RSV).
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study is a review examining the regulatory landscape for mRNA vaccines and therapeutics, focusing on the clinical and regulatory considerations for expanding mRNA platforms to include therapeutic applications for RSV and other viruses.
analysis.methods: The methods involve a comprehensive review of the regulatory science considerations for prophylactic mRNA vaccines and their potential application to therapeutic mRNA platforms, including an analysis of the differences in evidence requirements based on intended use and mechanism of action.
analysis.main_results: The review highlights that while platform-level knowledge from prophylactic mRNA vaccines can support therapeutic development, regulatory questions may vary with each new product type, necessitating tailored approaches and ongoing engagement with regulatory authorities.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that the regulatory considerations for prophylactic mRNA vaccines are not directly transferable to therapeutic applications, emphasizing the need for product-specific evidence and adaptive regulatory frameworks.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform the development of mRNA therapeutics for RSV by highlighting the importance of addressing unique regulatory challenges such as delivery, function of the expressed product, and patient-specific manufacturing, which are critical for effective treatment and safety.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to a review of existing regulatory frameworks and does not present new empirical data, resulting in a moderate confidence assessment based on the analysis of current literature and regulatory considerations.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the regulatory science considerations for expanding mRNA platforms from prophylactic vaccines to therapeutic applications, with a focus on respiratory syncytial virus (RSV). It highlights that while platform knowledge can support therapeutic development, each new product type requires tailored regulatory approaches. The study emphasizes the need for explicit regulatory consideration of factors such as delivery, function of the expressed product, and patient-specific manufacturing. It also underscores the importance of tracking evolving regulatory instruments across jurisdictions and engaging regulatory authorities early. The findings suggest that the regulatory landscape for mRNA therapeutics differs from that of vaccines, necessitating product-specific evidence and adaptive frameworks. The study's limitations include its reliance on existing literature without new empirical data, which results in a moderate confidence assessment.

abstract_zh: 传统的非扩增信使 RNA (mRNA) 和自扩增 RNA (saRNA) 药物通常共享核心线性 RNA 结构,包括 5' 帽、非翻译区、一个或多个开放阅读框和 Poly(A) 尾,并且通常采用脂质纳米粒子 (LNP) 等递送系统配制,以实现靶蛋白的瞬时细胞内表达。预防性 mRNA 疫苗 主要设计用于表达传染病抗原并产生保护性免疫记忆,而 mRNA 治疗剂则发挥药理作用,旨在治疗疾病、抑制复发、替换蛋白质、调节免疫或传递基因编辑酶。因此,即使是基于类似 mRNA-LNP 技术的产品,根据其预期用途和作用机制,也可能有不同的监管分类和证据要求。临床和监管格局已从第一个冠状病毒疾病 2019 疫苗 扩展到包括 呼吸道合胞病毒 和流感 mRNA 疫苗、流感-冠状病毒疾病 2019 组合 疫苗、授权的 saRNA 疫苗、个性化癌症免疫疗法、蛋白质替代疗法、体内细胞编程和基因编辑传递系统。本综述探讨了哪些预防性 疫苗 证据可以支持治疗开发,以及哪些产品特定质量、非临床、临床和生命周期证据仍然是必要的。对于预防性mRNA 疫苗,主要监管考虑因素包括质量、免疫原性、预防功效、批次放行以及大规模疫苗接种后的安全性监测。对于 mRNA 疗法,主要问题包括递送至靶组织、表达产物的功能、重复剂量安全性、生物分布、脱靶风险、长期随访以及患者特异性制造和可追溯性。特别是,虽然个性化mRNA癌症疫苗通常被描述为疫苗,但它们在监管目的上更接近于根据每位患者的肿瘤特征发挥作用的治疗方法,而不是预防传染病的疫苗。因此,抗原选择算法、患者特异性序列设计、小批量和多产品生产、产品与患者匹配、组合策略的临床评估、生产延迟和分析群体以及基于风险的长期授权后随访都需要明确的监管考虑。来自预防性 mRNA 疫苗 授权的平台级知识可以支持治疗开发,但监管问题可能会因每种新产品类型而异;开发商需要跟踪各个司法管辖区不断变化的监管工具,并尽早与监管机构接触。

title: Is Wastewater Surveillance Predictive during the Endemic Phase of Respiratory Disease? An Analysis Based on Clinical, Wastewater, and Digital Search Data in Detroit, Michigan
abstract: Wastewater-based epidemiology (WBE) has emerged as a major public health innovation catalyzed by the COVID-19 pandemic. However, its potential remains underexplored during and after COVID-19’s transition to endemicity. This study evaluates WBE’s potential to identify the COVID-19 pandemic-to-endemic transition and to provide early warnings across multiple surveillance systems for influenza A (IAV) and B (IBV), respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), and SARS-CoV-2 in the postpandemic era. We monitored SARS-CoV-2 N1 concentrations in wastewater from April 8, 2020, and July 31, 2025, generating the earliest and longest-running wastewater dataset in Detroit, MI. A peak identification method was implemented to identify the pandemic-to-endemic transition by comparing the frequency of N1 concentration peaks between phases. During the endemic phase, from October 1, 2022, and March 31, 2025, we monitored RSV, IAV, IBV, and SARS-CoV-2 in Detroit’s wastewater. Pearson correlations were implemented to quantify the associations between wastewater concentrations and clinical, syndromic, and digital epidemiological data. Time-lagged cross-correlation (TLCC) was used to examine temporal dynamics among these datasets and identify the earliest emerging data for each disease and time lags. Extensive literature studies were conducted to elucidate the time-lag mechanisms for each disease, embracing the TLCC results. Random forest models were established to predict clinical cases based on WBE datasets. This was among the first studies using WBE-based approaches to identify pandemic-to-endemic transition of SARS-CoV-2. The relationships of wastewater data to traditional clinical, syndromic, and digital epidemiological surveillance data were systematically analyzed during the endemic phase of these respiratory diseases. This study demonstrates the predictive value of WBE during the endemic phase, providing early warnings and predictions for seasonal respiratory diseases, including COVID-19, influenza, and flu-like disease.

title: Resveratrol alleviates glucolipid metabolism disorders in diabetic nephropathy via the HIF-1α pathway: a network pharmacology and experimental validation study
abstract: Background Diabetic nephropathy (DN) represents a major microvascular complication of diabetes with complex pathogenesis. Resveratrol (RSV), a polyphenol from Polygonum cuspidatum , is a potential therapeutic agent for DN. However, the exact mechanisms of RSV modulating glucolipid metabolism in DN remain unclear. Methods Potential targets and signaling pathways of RSV against DN were predicted by network pharmacology and molecular docking. Based on the prediction, a DN model was generated in male Wistar rats using a high-fat diet/streptozotocin (HFD/STZ) induction, followed by 12-week RSV (30 mg/kg/d) for in vivo validation. In vitro , HK-2 cells cultured in palmitic acid (PA) were treated with either RSV or LW6, a hypoxia-inducible factor 1α (HIF-1α) inhibitor. Biochemical parameters, histopathological alterations and lipid deposition were examined. AKT/HIF-1α pathway activation and downstream metabolic gene levels were analyzed via Western blot, immunofluorescence and RT-qPCR. Results Bioinformatics findings revealed RSV exerts its anti-DN effects predominantly through the prioritized candidate AKT1 and the highly enriched HIF-1 signaling pathway. In vivo , RSV significantly ameliorated hyperglycemia and renal dysfunction and alleviated histopathological injuries and glycogen storage. Mechanistically, RSV suppressed p-AKT and HIF-1α expression, reduced Glut1 mRNA levels, and elevated Ldlr mRNA levels, significantly. In vitro , RSV effectively decreased lipid accumulation and inhibited HIF-1α expression, downregulating SREBP1, SREBP2, LDLR, GLUT1 and TGF-β1 and upregulating INSIG2. The effects of LW6 were largely consistent with those of RSV but failed to reduce HIF-1α mRNA levels. Conclusion The attenuation of glucolipid metabolic disorders in DN by RSV is associated with suppression of the HIF-1α pathway, highlighting the therapeutic potential of RSV for DN.

source_records.title: Resveratrol alleviates glucolipid metabolism disorders in diabetic nephropathy via the HIF-1α pathway: a network pharmacology and experimental validation study
source_records.abstract: Diabetic nephropathy (DN) represents a major microvascular complication of diabetes with complex pathogenesis. Resveratrol (RSV), a polyphenol from Polygonum cuspidatum , is a potential therapeutic agent for DN. However, the exact mechanisms of RSV modulating glucolipid metabolism in DN remain unclear. Potential targets and signaling pathways of RSV against DN were predicted by network pharmacology and molecular docking. Based on the prediction, a DN model was generated in male Wistar rats using a high-fat diet/streptozotocin (HFD/STZ) induction, followed by 12-week RSV (30 mg/kg/d) for in vivo validation. In vitro , HK-2 cells cultured in palmitic acid (PA) were treated with either RSV or LW6, a hypoxia-inducible factor 1α (HIF-1α) inhibitor. Biochemical parameters, histopathological alterations and lipid deposition were examined. AKT/HIF-1α pathway activation and downstream metabolic gene levels were analyzed via Western blot, immunofluorescence and RT-qPCR. Bioinformatics findings revealed RSV exerts its anti-DN effects predominantly through the prioritized candidate AKT1 and the highly enriched HIF-1 signaling pathway. In vivo , RSV significantly ameliorated hyperglycemia and renal dysfunction and alleviated histopathological injuries and glycogen storage. Mechanistically, RSV suppressed p-AKT and HIF-1α expression, reduced Glut1 mRNA levels, and elevated Ldlr mRNA levels, significantly. In vitro , RSV effectively decreased lipid accumulation and inhibited HIF-1α expression, downregulating SREBP1, SREBP2, LDLR, GLUT1 and TGF-β1 and upregulating INSIG2. The effects of LW6 were largely consistent with those of RSV but failed to reduce HIF-1α mRNA levels. The attenuation of glucolipid metabolic disorders in DN by RSV is associated with suppression of the HIF-1α pathway, highlighting the therapeutic potential of RSV for DN.

title: Suspected nimesulide-associated hypersensitivity myocarditis presenting as ST-elevation myocardial infarction: A case report
abstract: Hypersensitivity myocarditis caused by NSAIDs can mimic acute STEMI, yet nimesulide as the trigger of primary myocardial injury has rarely been documented. This article reports a 57-year-old male who developed rash and persistent chest pain after taking nimesulide for fever due to respiratory syncytial virus infection. Electrocardiogram revealed ST-segment elevation in leads V2-V3, and the patient was admitted with acute heart failure and shock. Norepinephrine was administered to maintain circulation. Suspected nimesulide-associated hypersensitivity myocarditis was considered based on elevated eosinophil count, medication history and rash. Following methylprednisolone therapy and hemodynamic stabilization, coronary angiography showed no vascular lesions. Cardiac magnetic resonance demonstrated myocardial edema and mid-wall injury of the interventricular septum. Continued glucocorticoid treatment resulted in marked improvement in the patient’s symptoms and laboratory findings, with SCAI shock stage improving from stage C on admission to stage A at discharge.Follow-up cardiac magnetic resonance at 3-month after onset showed complete resolution of myocardial injury without fibrosis. Clinicians should be alert to this rare cardiac adverse reaction of nimesulide.
journal: International Journal of Cardiology Cardiovascular Risk and Prevention

title: Comparative clinical, immunological, and pulmonary responses to virulent bovine respiratory syncytial virus infection in colostrum-fed, intranasally vaccinated calves
abstract: Abstract Objective To compare clinical, pulmonary, and immunologic responses to bovine respiratory syncytial virus (BRSV) challenge in colostrum-fed, BRSV-seropositive calves following administration of 2 commercially available intranasal vaccines. Methods 34 male Holstein calves (9 to 20 days old) were randomly assigned to receive vaccine A (Nasalgen; n = 17) or vaccine B (Inforce 3; 17). Nine weeks after vaccination, calves were challenged with virulent BRSV. Clinical observations were recorded daily. Arterial partial pressure of oxygen was measured on day 6 after challenge, and percentage pneumonic lung involvement was assessed at necropsy on day 8. Antibody responses and viral shedding were assessed. Results Clinical signs were infrequent and mild in both groups, and nasal shedding of BRSV was low. Median lung lesion scores were lower in calves receiving vaccine B than in calves receiving vaccine A (2.3% vs 4.6%). Arterial oxygen concentrations were numerically higher in vaccine B calves (median, 91.0 mm Hg) than in vaccine A calves (median, 82.8 mm Hg), although this difference was not significant. A greater proportion of vaccine B calves had Pao 2 values within the normal range (> 87.1 mm Hg) compared to vaccine A calves (12 of 17 [71%] vs 7 of 17 [41%]). Both vaccines induced anamnestic mucosal and systemic antibody responses. Conclusions Both vaccines were associated with minimal clinical disease following BRSV challenge. Clinical Relevance Results suggest a modest advantage of vaccine B with respect to pulmonary involvement and maintenance of arterial oxygenation under these experimental conditions.
journal: Journal of the American Veterinary Medical Association

title: Changing Patterns of Viral Respiratory in Albania: Laboratory Findings from March 2025 to June 2026
abstract: Background: Seasonal influenza is a major cause of acute respiratory infections, with activity typically increasing during the colder months. Because influenza and other respiratory viruses cause similar symptoms, laboratory testing is essential for accurate pathogen identification and appropriate clinical management. Objective: To characterize the distribution and monthly patterns of laboratory-confirmed respiratory viruses from March 2025 to June 2026, and to place these findings in the context of two previous local studies. Methods: We conducted a descriptive analysis of 1,863 laboratory test records. As in the previous research, initial screening for respiratory antigens was followed by molecular confirmation of positive samples. Results: At least one virus was identified in 467 tests (25.1%): 463 cases tested positive for a single virus, and four cases involved more than one virus. Influenza A was the most frequently identified virus (207 cases), followed by SARS-CoV-2 (80), adenovirus (71), RSV (42), influenza B (38), hMPV (23), and parainfluenza virus (2). Conclusions: Influenza A was the most frequent virus among cases that tested positive for a single virus. Influenza A and RSV peaked during the winter, influenza B was identified primarily during the colder months, SARS-CoV-2 showed an increase during the summer and early autumn, while adenovirus was identified throughout the entire study period. Age-specific results demonstrated a marked concentration of several respiratory viruses among children aged 0–10 years.

title: ĐẶC ĐIỂM MỘT SỐ VI SINH VẬT ĐỒNG NHIỄM Ở TRẺ EM MẮC CÚM A ĐIỀU TRỊ TẠI TRUNG TÂM NHI KHOA, BỆNH VIỆN TRUNG ƯƠNG THÁI NGUYÊN
abstract: Mục tiêu: Mô tả một số vi sinh vật được phát hiện kèm theo ở trẻ em mắc cúm A điều trị nội trú. Đối tượng và phương pháp nghiên cứu: Nghiên cứu mô tả cắt ngang trên 170 trẻ từ 1 tháng đến 15 tuổi mắc cúm A, điều trị nội trú từ tháng 1/2025 đến tháng 6/2026. Kết quả: Trẻ 24–59 tháng chiếm 34,1%, nam 64,7%; 92,4% trường hợp nhập viện trong các tháng 10–3. Có 44,7% trẻ phát hiện ít nhất một vi sinh vật kèm theo; tỷ lệ phát hiện vi khuẩn và virus lần lượt là 41,2% và 6,5%. pneumoniae được phát hiện nhiều nhất trong nhóm vi khuẩn dương tính (57,1%); RSV chiếm 72,7% nhóm virus dương tính. Trong các so sánh thăm dò chưa hiệu chỉnh, tỷ lệ phát hiện vi khuẩn khác biệt theo nhóm tuổi, thời điểm mắc bệnh và tình trạng tiêm vaccine phế cầu hoặc Hib ghi trong hồ sơ (p<0,05); dữ liệu tiêm chủng không có số liều hay tình trạng tiêm đủ theo tuổi. Kết luận: Vi sinh vật kèm theo được phát hiện ở trẻ mắc cúm A điều trị nội trú, chủ yếu là vi khuẩn. Các khác biệt trong phân tích thăm dò chưa hiệu chỉnh không chứng minh yếu tố nguy cơ độc lập hoặc hiệu quả bảo vệ của vaccine.
journal: Tạp chí Y học Cộng đồng

title: Multi-model forecasting of respiratory disease activity in Germany during the 2024-2025 season
abstract: Respiratory diseases cause considerable morbidity in autumn and winter and are a priority in public health monitoring. In Germany, they are subject to a number of surveillance systems, including both pathogen-specific and syndromic indicators. In this paper we present a collaborative multi-target and multi-model real-time forecasting system rolled out during the 2024/25 season, and discuss differences to earlier efforts carried out during the COVID-19 pandemic. We focus on general practitioner consultations for acute respiratory infections (ARI) and hospitalizations for severe acute respiratory infections (SARI), where a total of eight models were run to generate nowcasts and forecasts. In addition, we consider confirmed cases of seasonal influenza and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) where one forecasting model each was available. As all indicators were subject to retrospective revisions, forecasting models were combined with a nowcasting step. For the SARI and ARI indicators, we combined the available models into an ensemble and conducted detailed quantitative evaluations. Nowcasts overall showed convincing performance, even though for some models Christmas break effects led to an upward bias in early January. Forecasts were overall well-calibrated and most models outperformed simple benchmark models. When taking into account age-stratified targets, most observed performance differences to a persistence baseline were statistically significant. Anticipating the peak timing and magnitude, however, proved to be challenging, with many models predicting too flat curves with a too early turnaround (e.g., in late January rather than mid-February for SARI). The combined ensemble forecast was among the best-performing approaches, but unlike in previous related projects did not consistently outperform individual models. We conclude by discussing learnings on the organization of collaborative forecasting projects in post-COVID-19 times.

full_text: Back to Journals » ClinicoEconomics and Outcomes Research » Volume 18 Clinical and Economic Impact of Nirsevimab and Bivalent Maternal Vaccine Against RSV Infections in Infants in Italy Authors Bini C, Marcellusi A, Muzii B, Soudani S , Trotta S, Parisi S, Bozzola E, Bonanni P , Boccalini S Received 30 May 2026 Accepted for publication 30 September 2026 Published 3 November 2026 Volume 2026:18 622013 DOI https://doi.org/10.2147/CEOR.S622013 Checked for plagiarism Yes Review by Single anonymous peer review Peer reviewer comments 2 Editor who approved publication: Professor Giorgio Colombo Chiara Bini,1 Andrea Marcellusi,1 Barbara Muzii,2 Samira Soudani,3 Sara Trotta,2 Salvatore Parisi,2 Elena Bozzola,4 Paolo Bonanni,5 Sara Boccalini5 1Centre for Economics and International Studies-Economic Evaluation and Health Technology Assessment (CEIS-EEHTA), Faculty of Economics, University of Rome ‘Tor Vergata’, Rome, 00133, Italy; 2Sanofi, Rome, Italy; 3Sanofi, Lyon, France; 4IRCCS Bambino Gesù Children Hospital, Rome, Italy; 5Department of Health Sciences, University of Florence, Florence, 50134, Italy Correspondence: Chiara Bini, Centre for Economics and International Studies-Economic Evaluation and Health Technology Assessment, Faculty of Economics, University of Rome "Tor Vergata”, Rome, 00133, Italy, Tel +393287236584, Email [email protected] Objective: This study aimed to estimate the potential clinical and economic impact of nirsevimab and of a maternal vaccine in the prevention of medically attended (MA) RSV-associated lower respiratory tract infections (LRTIs) in the entire cohort of newborns entering their first RSV season in Italy compared with the absence of prevention strategies. Methods: A cost-consequence analysis using a static decision tree model previously published was conducted to estimate the RSV-MA-LRTIs and associated mid-long-term complications avoided with each immunization strategy during a single RSV epidemic season. Nirsevimab efficacy was derived from the pooled analysis of Phase 3 MELODY and Phase 2b clinical trials and a protection of 6 months with constant efficacy was considered. For maternal immunization (MI), the efficacy for term infants was derived from MATISSE clinical trial and it was considered until 6 months of age. Zero efficacy was assumed starting from the seventh month for both preventive strategies. The time horizon of the analysis corresponding to one RSV epidemic season. National Health Service (NHS) perspective was considered in the base-case. Results: From the NHS perspective, over the first RSV season, the immunization strategy with MI compared with no preventive strategies could lead to a reduction of 68,358 RSV-MA-LRTIs and 6,417 associated mid-long-term complications. These reductions in terms of RSV‐related health events can be translated into economic savings of about € 24.5 million. The immunization strategy with nirsevimab compared with no preventive strategies could lead to a reduction of 118,123 RSV-MA-LRTIs, 8,480 associated mid-long-term complications. The economic saving associated with these reductions in terms of RSV-related health events was estimated equal to € 34.2 million. Conclusion: Both preventive strategies represent effective measures for the prevention of RSV infections in infants. The organizational impact of these two strategies should also be assessed, in addition to ensuring appropriate counselling for pregnant women and the parents of infants, to avoid missing these immunization opportunities against RSV. These findings may support public health decision-making and inform future policy strategies. Keywords: respiratory syncytial virus, universal immunization, economic evaluation, prophylactic strategies Introduction Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is the most common cause of acute lower respiratory infections in infants, and it is a leading cause of bronchiolitis and pneumonia in children under 5 years of age.1 The infection may cause a significant burden for emergency departments, paediatric wards and intensive care units due to clinical care requirements, including oxygen supplementation and fluid administration. The main risk factors for infection are seasonality, age below one-year, preterm birth, congenital heart disease, bronchopulmonary dysplasia, specific and serious pathologies that lead to immune and neuromuscular deficit.2 However, about 90% of hospitalizations for RSV involve healthy infants born at the end of the gestational period.2,3 Recently, two prophylactic strategies have been approved in Italy to prevent RSV disease in all infants, while palivizumab was already available previously, but its use was limited to high-risk populations. These two new prophylactic strategies are: nirsevimab, a new long-acting monoclonal antibody for passive immunization against RSV of all infants during their first RSV season and for children up to 24 months of age who remain vulnerable to severe RSV disease through their second RSV season;4 and a recombinant bivalent vaccine targeting pregnant women for passive protection up to 6 months of age.5 Immunization with a long-acting RSV-neutralizing monoclonal antibody, currently nirsevimab, is recommended for all infants entering their first RSV season, regardless of whether birth occurs during the RSV season or before its onset.6 Maternal immunization with the bivalent recombinant protein-based RSV vaccine is authorized as a single dose administered between 24 and 36 weeks of gestation, in accordance with the EMA indication. However, in some Italian regions, eligibility has been restricted to 32–36 weeks of gestation, subject to vaccine availability, particularly for pregnant women whose expected date of delivery falls within the RSV circulation season (October to March, based on epidemiological surveillance data, potentially extending through April).6 The objective of this strategy is to prevent RSV-associated disease in both mothers and infants during the first 5–6 months of life. The marketing authorisation of these prophylactic interventions was based on a prespecified pooled analysis of the phase IIb and MELODY trials for nirsevimab7 and the MATISSE clinical study for maternal vaccination.8 The MATISSE clinical study evaluated vaccine efficacy in terms of medically attended RSV-associated lower respiratory tract illness in infants born from vaccinated women within 90, 120, 150, and 180 days after birth.9 It is important to note that the MATISSE clinical trial was not powered to provide estimates of efficacy among preterm infants; in fact, study limitations reported in the final analysis include the exclusion of individuals with high-risk pregnancies.8 Both prevention strategies were available in Italy from 2023. The first regional implementation of nirsevimab occurred in Valle d’Aosta during the 2023–2024 RSV season, with prophylaxis offered to all newborns. These RSV prevention strategies were not initially included in the Italian National Immunization Plan; however, from the 2024–2025 season, universal access to nirsevimab for newborns was supported at the national level through an agreement between the Ministry of Health and the Regions,10 with dedicated funding from the National Health Fund, enabling Regions to provide immunization free of charge. As of February 2026, globally, more than 11 million infants have been immunized with nirsevimab across more than 45 countries.11 A recent study conducted to evaluate potential impacts of nirsevimab or maternal immunization (MI) on hospitalisations due to RSV lower respiratory tract infections in infants aged ≤1 year in Lombardy during the 2024/25 season reported that the administration of nirsevimab to 80% of newborns (uptake levels observed in Spain) was estimated to prevent 50.2% (95% CI: 43.5–55.8) of hospitalisations in the total population.12 Achieving coverage levels comparable to those of routine childhood vaccines (95%) could yield an additional average reduction of 18% in hospitalisations.12 MI administrated to the 65% of pregnant women, consistent with diphtheria–tetanus–pertussis vaccine coverage in Lombardy for this population, was estimated to avert 30.5% (95% CI: 19.6–39.7) of hospitalisations.12 A recent nationwide real-world evidence study implemented in France during RSV season 2024–25 compared the effectiveness of infant immunization with nirsevimab against the vaccination of pregnant woman with the bivalent maternal RSVpreF vaccine.13 Nirsevimab was associated with a lower risk of RSV-related hospitalization compared with the maternal vaccine (adjusted hazard ratio, 0.74 [95% CI, 0.61 to 0.88]).13 Compared with the RSVpreF vaccine, passive infant immunization with nirsevimab was associated with a lower risk of severe outcomes, including Pediatric Intensive Care Unit (PICU) admission (adjusted HR, 0.58 [95% CI, 0.42 to 0.80]), requiring ventilator support (adjusted HR, 0.57 [95% CI, 0.40 to 0.81]), or requiring oxygen therapy (adjusted HR, 0.56 [95% CI, 0.38 to 0.81]).13 The results were consistent across subgroups and in the sensitivity analyses. This study aimed to simulate the potential impact of each of the two RSV immunization programs on the prevention of medically attended RSV-associated lower respiratory tract infection (MA-LRTIS) against the lack of prevention strategies (no intervention) in a cohort of newborns in Italy. | | Table 1 Population, Coverage Rate and Efficacy Data | Methods The potential impact of the implementation of an immunization program with nirsevimab or MI was assessed through a cost-consequence analysis comparing the predicted reduction in RSV-related events and associated costs (excluding the cost of the prophylaxis strategies) compared with the predicted estimates in the absence of preventive strategies. This assessment was performed based on a previously published static decision tree model used to evaluate the universal immunization with nirsevimab among all infants against palivizumab in Italy18 (Supplementary Figure A); the model was adapted in terms of population, efficacy and coverage rate data to reflect the appropriate context and inputs related to the MI. In order to consider that MI may not translate into sufficient protection of the infant in case of extreme premature birth, the subpopulations in the MI model were defined as following: (1) extreme preterm infants, representing newborns with ≤ 31 weeks gestational age (wGA); (2) late preterm infants, representing newborns with 32–36 wGA; 3) term infants, representing newborns with ≥ 37 wGA. For nirsevimab, as done in the previously published study, the subpopulations were defined as following: (1) preterm newborns with ≤ 35 wGA or infants with congenital heart or chronic lung disease; (2) late preterm and term infants, representing newborns with > 35 wGA. Therefore, the subpopulation is divided differently for the two interventions, and each intervention was evaluated using a separate model developed according to this distinct stratification. The proportion of infants belonging to the respective subpopulation was obtained from data published by the Ministry of Health14 and from the literature15,16 (Table 1). In particular, the proportions of extremely preterm infants and late preterm infants used for the MI model were derived from the 2024 CeDAP report published by the Ministry of Health and were estimated at 0.9% and 5.3%, respectively (Table 1). The subpopulation of preterm newborns with ≤ 35 wGA or infants with congenital heart or chronic lung disease considered in the nirsevimab model was calculated adding at the proportion of premature infants (≤35 weeks) equal to 4.7% reported by CeDAP 2024,14 the proportion of children at risk of bronchopulmonary dysplasia of 0.3%15 and the proportion of children with CHD of 0.6%16 (Table 1). These proportions were applied to the total number of newborns in Italy in 2025.19 The time horizon for each immunization strategy refers to one RSV epidemic season. The subpopulations were followed during their first endemic RSV season through the same model structure described in detail in the previous publication.18 For each subpopulation, the model described the RSV-MA-LRTI events in terms of primary care visits, hospital admissions (including admissions in intensive care unit - ICU) and emergency room (ER) visits that occur during the RSV season. Among infants hospitalized due to RSV, the model also considered the probability of developing mid-long-term complications (asthma and wheezing) and the risk of death among RSV inpatient hospitalizations. Long-term complications were incorporated by considering the risk of recurrent wheezing up to 3 years of age and asthma up to 18 years of age, based on published evidence. Specifically, recurrent wheezing probabilities were derived from Li et al 2022,20 which reported a risk of recurrent wheezing during the first, second and third year of age following an RSV hospitalization (Supplementary Table A); the risk of asthma following RSV hospitalization was modeled as a one-off probability, calculated by summing the annual probabilities of asthma-related hospitalization up to 18 years of age among children hospitalized for RSV infection within the first two years of life, based on data coming from Coutts et al 202021 (Supplementary Table A). Monthly probabilities of RSV infection and monthly per-patient risks of RSV-related health event were consistent with those used and validated by clinicians in the previously published study and reported in the Supplementary Materials (Supplementary Table A). In particular, in the MI model, for the extreme preterm infants and late preterm infants subpopulations the monthly per-patient risks of RSV-related health event used for the preterm newborns with ≤ 35 wGA or infants with congenital heart or chronic lung disease were considered. In the base case, both for nirsevimab and MI a coverage rate equal to 75% for each subgroup population was considered. In the scenario analysis, a coverage rate for MI close to the average assumed for other types of maternal vaccination, as derived from data published by individual centres at national level15,19 was evaluated. In particular, a coverage rate equal to 20% was assumed considering the minimum and the maximum coverage rates observed in the literature for maternal immunization and related to influenza vaccination (8.1%)22 and Tdap (43% respectively).23 For MI, in accordance with the expectations of the experts involved in the analysis, the model considered a seasonal vaccination to prevent RSV infections in infants born right before or during the RSV season which would mean to immunize pregnant women when they expect to deliver between the first of August and 31st of March (about 68% of infants of the entire cohort of newborns born during that period). For nirsevimab, as done in the previously published study, the seasonal immunization was considered in a single administration occurring at the beginning of epidemic season which typically starts in late autumn (November), peaks during winter (January), and ends in March (Barbati et al 202024) for infants born before it or during the season for infant born during it; therefore all infants are potentially eligible to the prophylaxis with nirsevimab, even if in the model it was assumed that only 75% of the entire cohort of newborns received the immunization (based on assumed coverage rate). In the base-case the analysis was conducted considering a perspective of the National Health Service (NHS); a societal perspective, including both direct and indirect costs, was evaluated in the scenario analysis. Indirect costs were estimated in terms of productivity loss due to premature RSV-death following a severe RSV infection. Efficacy Data The efficacy of each immunization strategy was measured in terms of reduction in RSV-MA-LRTI events. Nirsevimab efficacy was derived from the pooled analysis of Phase III (MELODY) and phase 2b clinical trials.7 The analysis showed an efficacy for nirsevimab estimated in terms of risk reduction of RSV MA-LRTIs compared with placebo equal to 79.5%. Since pooled analysis of phase III (MELODY) and phase 2b clinical trials has also shown that pharmacokinetic data from the MEDLEY phase 2–3 study25 support the extrapolation of estimated efficacy for infants born preterm and full-term, an efficacy equal to 79.5% was applied to all subgroups (Table 1). A protection of 6 months with constant efficacy was considered for nirsevimab, in line with the duration of protection demonstrated in HARMONIE phase 3b clinical trial.26 The efficacy of MI was derived from MATISSE clinical study. As the MATISSE study reported MI efficacy data starting from 90 to 180 days after birth, assumptions were done to estimate efficacy by single month of age. For term infants, as done in the previously published study of Aldean et al 2024,17 vaccine efficacy by single month of age was derived by fitting a line to the cumulative efficacy datapoints from MATISSE (at 90, 120, 150, and 180 days after birth) and deriving marginal monthly estimates through age 5 to < 6 months. Within this approach, the efficacy against severe RSV-positive MA acute LRI was used as a proxy for efficacy against RSV cases requiring hospitalization, and efficacy against RSV-positive MA acute LRI was used as a proxy for efficacy against RSV cases treated in the emergency department or primary care setting. In the base case analysis, MI efficacy was considered up to 6 months, in order to consider only the observations from the MATISSE study (with zero efficacy from the seventh month onward); in the scenario analysis, vaccine efficacy was assumed to wane linearly to 0% by age 9 to < 10 months (as projected in the study of Aldean et al 2024).17 Additionally, as previously done in the study of Aldean et al, because MATISSE was not powered to provide estimates of efficacy among preterm infants, vaccine efficacy for late pr…

title_original: Clinical and Economic Impact of Nirsevimab and Bivalent Maternal Vaccine Against RSV Infections in Infants in Italy

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to estimate the potential clinical and economic impact of nirsevimab and a maternal vaccine in the prevention of medically attended RSV-associated lower respiratory tract infections (LRTIs) in the entire cohort of newborns entering their first RSV season in Italy compared with the absence of prevention strategies.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A cost-consequence analysis using a static decision tree model was conducted to estimate the impact of immunization strategies during a single RSV epidemic season. The study focused on newborns in Italy, considering coverage rates and risk factors such as preterm birth, congenital heart disease, and bronchopulmonary dysplasia.
analysis.methods: A cost-consequence analysis using a static decision tree model previously published was conducted to estimate the RSV-MA-LRTIs and associated mid-long-term complications avoided with each immunization strategy during a single RSV epidemic season. The subpopulation of preterm newborns and infants with specific risk factors was calculated based on reported proportions from CeDAP 2024.
analysis.main_results: The administration of nirsevimab to 80% of newborns was estimated to prevent 50.2% (95% CI: 43.5–55.8) of hospitalisations in the total population. Achieving coverage levels comparable to routine childhood vaccines (95%) could yield an additional average reduction of 18% in hospitalisations. MI administrated to 65% of pregnant women was estimated to avert 30.5% (95% CI: 19.6–39.7) of hospitalisations.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study concludes that nirsevimab is associated with a lower risk of RSV-related hospitalization compared with the maternal vaccine, and that passive infant immunization with nirsevimab is associated with a lower risk of severe outcomes, including PICU admission, ventilator support, or oxygen therapy.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform public health strategies for the prevention of RSV disease in infants, particularly in the context of Italy, by highlighting the potential benefits of nirsevimab and maternal vaccination programs in reducing hospitalizations and severe outcomes.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study relies on previously published models and assumptions about coverage rates and risk factors, which may limit the confidence in the results. The evidence is based on a static decision tree model and real-world data, providing a moderate level of confidence.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluates the clinical and economic impact of nirsevimab and a bivalent maternal vaccine in preventing RSV-associated lower respiratory tract infections (LRTIs) in Italian infants. The research uses a cost-consequence analysis with a static decision tree model to estimate hospitalizations and complications avoided. Results indicate that nirsevimab, when administered to 80% of newborns, could prevent 50.2% of hospitalizations, while maternal vaccination could avert 30.5%. The study highlights that nirsevimab is associated with a lower risk of severe outcomes compared to the maternal vaccine. These findings suggest potential benefits for public health strategies in Italy. However, the study's reliance on existing models and assumptions about coverage rates introduces limitations, resulting in a moderate confidence assessment.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在评估 尼塞韦单抗 和孕产妇 疫苗 在意大利进入第一个 RSV 季节的整个 队列研究 新生儿中预防就医的 RSV 相关下呼吸道感染 (LRTI) 与缺乏预防策略的情况相比的潜在临床和经济影响。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 使用静态决策树模型进行成本后果分析,以估计单个 RSV 流行季节免疫策略的影响。该研究主要针对意大利的新生儿,考虑了覆盖率和早产、先天性心脏病和支气管肺发育不良等危险因素。
elements_zh.methods: 使用先前发布的静态决策树模型进行成本后果分析,以估计单个 RSV 流行季节期间每种免疫策略避免的 RSV-MA-LRTI 和相关的中长期并发症。具有特定危险因素的早产新生儿和婴儿的亚群是根据 CeDAP 2024 报告的比例计算的。
elements_zh.main_results: 据估计,对 80% 的新生儿施用 尼塞韦单抗 可以预防总人口中 50.2%(95% CI:43.5-55.8)的住院治疗。达到与常规儿童 疫苗 (95%) 相当的覆盖水平可以使住院治疗平均减少 18%。据估计,65% 的孕妇接受 MI 治疗可避免 30.5%(95% CI:19.6-39.7)的住院治疗。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究的结论是,与母亲 疫苗 相比,尼塞韦单抗 与 RSV 相关住院风险较低相关,并且使用 尼塞韦单抗 进行婴儿被动免疫与严重后果风险较低相关,包括 PICU 入院、呼吸机支持或氧疗。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果可以为预防婴儿 RSV 疾病的公共卫生策略提供信息,特别是在意大利,通过强调 尼塞韦单抗 和孕产妇 疫苗接种 计划在减少住院和严重后果方面的潜在益处。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究依赖于先前发布的关于覆盖率和风险因素的模型和假设,这可能会限制结果的可信度。该证据基于静态决策树模型和真实世界数据,提供了中等程度的置信度。
